jobs.description:
Doctoral Researcher in Sustainability Assessment for Evaluating Future Global Food Systems

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Sustainable Food Processing Group uses a combination of innovative sustainability assessment and emerging food system approaches to target fundamental challenges in food science and society, such as the protein transition and food security.

The project aims to further develop and apply sustainability assessment methods to support transformations in future global food systems. By integrating future projections, it will identify improvement potentials in key value chains across diverse geographical contexts. The work will adopt an interdisciplinary approach through close collaboration with other research groups.

Job description

We are seeking a highly motivated candidate to work on this project that assesses the current status and future scenarios of global food systems sustainability across nutrition, environmental, economic, and social dimensions.

Profile

The successful candidate must hold a:

• Master's degree in Sustainability Sciences

• Environmental Engineering

• Data/Computer Sciences

• Bioscience Engineering, or a closely related field

• Excellent proficiency in spoken and written English is mandatory

In addition, the candidate should have:

• Excellent academic qualifications, strong writing skills, self-motivation, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary environment

• Proficiency in statistical analysis, computer programming, and big data handling (essential)

• Experience in quantitative sustainability assessment such as life cycle assessment (essential), mathematical modelling of environmental systems (a plus), and planetary boundaries (a plus)

• Documented work in food system sustainability, bioeconomy, LCA/LCSA, planetary boundaries, or data science programming (Python, R) (a strong plus)

• High curiosity, openness to new ideas, effective teamwork, and communication skills

• Interest in advancing sustainability science in future food systems and mentoring BSc/MSc students

Candidates with experience or strong interest in innovative food technologies and novel protein/micronutrient sources, such as single-cell proteins (incl. microalgae), and plant-based ingredients, will be considered a strong advantage.

Workplace

We offer

• A multicultural group with a diverse and interdisciplinary team composition.

• Exciting and varied projects in an innovative environment.

• Personal development opportunities through training, teaching, and further education.

• Perspectives for career development.

• A dynamic, collegial working environment with flat hierarchies.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application (English, PDF format), including:

• Motivation letter (max. 1 page) outlining your qualifications and motivation for this project

• Research proposal (max. 3 pages) on "Future Global Food Systems Sustainability", addressing current challenges, key literature, and approaches to sustainability in novel food value chains

• CV with list of scientific outputs (e.g., theses, papers)

• Contact details of 2 referees

• Copies of BSc and MSc diplomas*

• Copies of BSc and MSc theses (any language)*

• Transcript listing exams with ECTS cedits and grades

• 1 recommendation letter

*If you haven’t completed y

Doctoral Researcher in Food Processing for Planetary and Human Health

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Sustainable Food Processing Group focuses on advancing food processing technologies and their role in sustainable food systems, using innovative approaches to tackle fundamental challenges such as the protein transition and food security. We use innovative sustainability assessment and emerging food system approaches as key tools to guide processing innovations toward holistic and impactful solutions.

Job description

We are looking for a:

• Highly motivated candidate to join a collaborative research project that explores how food processing affects both nutritional quality and environmental impact.

The overall vision is to identify and develop processing strategies that improve nutritional quality and environmental performance as assessed by nutritional life cycle assessment (nLCA) while creating appealing hybrid protein-rich products. Thus, in addition to executing processing trials, the role includes coordinating collaborations within the team and with external partners to ensure that nutritional, health, and sustainability aspects are systematically integrated into the research.

Our two well-equipped pilot plants, featuring technologies ranging from multi-scale extruders to high-pressure and thermal treatment systems, pulsed electric field (PEF) equipment, and more, will serve as the core experimental platform for the project. Advanced analytical methods (e.g., nutritional profile, bioaccessibility, dynamic mechanical analysis, imaging, spectroscopy) may be employed to assess product quality.

Profile

The candidate must hold a:

• Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Food Technology, Food Engineering, Food Science, Bioengineering, Biotechnology or a closely related field.

In addition, the candidate should have:

• Excellent academic qualifications.

• Advanced knowledge in food processing.

• Strong communication and writing skills and high self-motivation.

• Openness to interdisciplinary work and a flexible mindset.

• Enthusiasm for engineering, food technology, and sustainability-related questions.

• Expertise in structurization via extrusion, disintegration, or preservation technologies, as well as project management and nutrition, will be considered a plus.

Workplace

We offer

• A multicultural group with a diverse and interdisciplinary team composition.

• Exciting and varied projects in an innovative environment.

• Personal development opportunities through training, teaching, and further education.

Doctoral Researcher in Food Processing for Planetary and Human Health 100%, Zurich, fixed-term print Drucken The ETH Sustainable Food Processing Group focuses on advancing food processing technologies and their role in sustainable food systems, using innovative approaches to tackle fundamental challenges such as the protein transition and food security. We use innovative sustainability assessment and emerging food system approaches as key tools to guide processing innovations toward holistic and impactful solutions. Job description We are looking for a:
• Highly motivated candidate to join a collaborative research project that explores how food processing affects both nutritional quality and environmental impact. The overall vision is to identify and develop processing strategies that improve nutritional quality and environmental performance as assessed by nutritional life cycle assessment (nLCA) while creating appealing hybrid protein-rich products. Thus, in addition to executing processing trials, the role includes coordinating collaborations within the team and with external partners to ensure that nutritional, health, and sustainability aspects are systematically integrated into the research. Our two well-equipped pilot plants, featuring technologies ranging from multi-scale extruders to high-pressure and thermal treatment systems, pulsed electric field (PEF) equipment, and more, will serve as the core experimental platform for the project. Advanced analytical methods (e.g., nutritional profile, bioaccessibility, dynamic mechanical analysis, imaging, spectroscopy) may be employed to assess product quality. Profile The candidate must hold a:
• Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Food Technology, Food Engineering, Food Science, Bioengineering, Biotechnology or a closely related field. In addition, the candidate should have:

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Human–Computer Interaction and Extended Reality in Architectural Design and Fabrication

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Human–Computer Interaction in Architecture and Digital Fabrication

This fully funded, full-time PhD position spans four years and is embedded within the interdisciplinary research environment at the Professorship of Architecture and Human Augmentation at ETH Zürich. We are looking for a highly self-driven and motivated researcher with a strong commitment to rigorous and applied research within an interdisciplinary academic environment. The research focuses on human–computer interaction (HCI) in architectural design and fabrication, with a particular emphasis on extended reality (XR), machine vision, and human-robot collaboration.

Project background

The research investigates how interactive computational tools, extended reality (XR), and robotic systems can augment human agency in architectural production. It examines the roles of interfaces, feedback systems, and embodied interaction in bridging design intent, material behaviour, and robotic execution across design-to-fabrication workflows. Specifically, the work will develop within those research streams:

• developing tools and workflows to efficiently assess discarded materials

• creating a digital inventory of reclaimed components

• developing computational representations of assembly and disassembly processes

• establishing a robust pipeline linking this inventory to CAD models

Job description

As a PhD candidate, you will conduct original research, design and run studies, develop and evaluate prototypes, analyze data, and disseminate results through publications and presentations. You will collaborate closely with the research team and partners, contribute to lab life, and support teaching and student supervision. Tasks include:

• Conduct independent research within the project scope

• Perform literature reviews and maintain awareness of related work

• Design and run experiments/case studies

• Document research thoroughly (version control, lab notebooks, protocols, datasets)

• Collect, clean, and analyze data using appropriate methods (e.g., qualitative coding, statistics, simulation, ML )

• Publish results in peer-reviewed venues (conferences/journals) and contribute to paper writing

• Support lab operations as needed (maintaining equipment, onboarding, shared infrastructure)

Teaching:

• Assist with teaching (TA, tutorials, crit sessions) and supervise student projects

• Mentor junior students (Bachelor/Master) and contribute to studio/course activities

Software/Engineering:

• Implement research code and maintain repositories (testing, documentation, reproducibility)

Grants/reporting:

• Contribute to grant writing, progress reports, and project administration

Profile

• You hold an architectural or advanced technical degree corresponding to FHEQ Level 7

• You have a strong interest in programming and, ideally, experience with Python and C# coding language

• You are proficient in 3D modelling environments and XR software; experience with Rhinoceros, Grasshopper and Unity is an advantage

• Experience in robotic fabrication, digital fabrication, or human–robot interaction is highly desirable

• Familiarity with XR technologies, UX development, or experimental prototyping is an asset

• You are fluent in English (written and spoken)

Workplace

We offer

• The opportunity to pursue doctoral research at a world-renowned academic institution

• Access to state-of-the-art computational, XR, and robotic fabrication infrastructure

• Close collaboration with researchers across architecture, robotics, computer science, and engineering

• An engaged international community of researchers and educators

• Professional development and networking opportunities through academic and industry collaborations

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity

jobs.description:
Doctoral student position – Evaluating novel mineral sources for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH Zurich Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism and Sustainable Food Processing Group in the Department of Health Science and Technology are running a joint strategic research line on Microalgae and plant-based foods in Human Nutrition and Health . The Sustainable Food Processing group focuses on a system-oriented approach in food production via the consideration of the total value chain, including emerging needs in society and their environmental, economic, and social impact. Innovative raw materials are utilized within urban farming and processing concepts to enable new ways of sustainable food supply. The Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism aims to gain insights into the complex relationship between nutrition, metabolism and the epigenome with advanced techniques such as single-cell and next-generation sequencing techniques as well as human and murine in vivo and in vitro studies and combine these with genome-wide computational and bioinformatic analysis. With strong support from these two ETH groups, we are recruiting as soon as possible a talented and highly motivated doctoral student on the topic of ‘Novel sources of minerals for treatment of micronutrient deficiencies in humans’, focusing on investigating the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources in vivo in clinical trials.

Project background

Micronutrient deficiency is a widespread global health problem, primarily driven by inadequate dietary intake. More than 5 billion people are estimated to not consume enough of at least one micronutrient. Among those, mineral deficiencies can be particularly critical, namely, iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium deficiencies, which are particularly common in low- and middle-income countries due to low-mineral diets and primarily affect women and children.

Dietary minerals are typically obtained from a variety of foods including animal-based products such as meat, dairy, and seafood, and plant-based foods such as legumes, cereals, nuts, seeds, and leafy vegetables. However, reliance on conventional animal-based foods raises concerns related to environmental sustainability, ethical considerations, and dietary preferences. Although plant-based foods are generally more sustainable, they often have lower mineral content, bioaccessibility, as well as bioavailability due to the presence of absorption inhibitors such as phytates and polyphenols. Given these limitations, the need exists to explore alternative, more sustainable, and mineral-dense food sources that can effectively address global mineral deficiencies.

Novel mineral sources, such as microalgae, could be a rich source of essential minerals, including iron, calcium, zinc, and magnesium, along with proteins, lipids, vitamins, and other bioactive compounds. However, the bioavailability of these minerals needs to be assessed with in vivo clinical trials before large scale application in humans.

Job description

As a doctoral student, you will be responsible for research working towards exploring the absorption and bioavailability of novel mineral sources with clinical trials.

• Summarize the existing knowledge on minerals from novel sources for human nutrition and health

• Design intervention meals (including sensory test) for clinical trials

• Assess the bioaccessibility of minerals in vitro

• Evaluate the mineral bioavailability in vitro

• Carry out clinical trials related to human nutrition enriched with novel mineral sources (key)

• Support teaching activities and co-supervise MSc and BSc students

• Act at the interface between science and technology when supervising students and collaborating with partners from academia and industry

• Support grant applications for the team and support related activities from Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for S

descriptionByLocale.it: Descrizione Posizione dottorale degli studenti – Valutazione di nuove fonti minerali per il trattamento delle carenze micronutrienti negli esseri umani 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Laboratorio ETH di Epigenetica, Nutrizione e Metabolismo e Gruppo di Elaborazione Alimentare Sostenibile presso il Dipartimento di Scienze e Tecnologie della Salute gestisce una linea di ricerca strategica congiunta su Microalgae e alimenti a base vegetale nella Nutrizione Umana e nella Salute. Il gruppo Sustainable Food Processing si concentra su un approccio orientato al sistema nella produzione alimentare attraverso la considerazione della catena del valore totale, compresi i bisogni emergenti nella società e il loro impatto ambientale, economico e sociale. Le materie prime innovative sono utilizzate all'interno di concetti di agricoltura urbana e di lavorazione per consentire nuove modalità di approvvigionamento alimentare sostenibile. Il Laboratorio di Epigenetica, Nutrizione e Metabolismo si propone di approfondire il complesso rapporto tra nutrizione, metabolismo e epigeno con tecniche avanzate come le tecniche di sequenziamento monocellulare e di prossima generazione, nonché studi umani e murini in vivo e in vitro e combinarli con l'analisi computazionale e bioinformatica a livello genoma. Con il forte sostegno di questi due gruppi ETH, stiamo reclutando il più presto possibile uno studente di dottorato di talento e altamente motivato sul tema “Novel fonti di minerali per il trattamento delle carenze micronutrienti nell’uomo”, concentrandosi sull’indagine sull’assorbimento e la biodisponibilità di nuove fonti minerali in vivo in studi clinici. Sfondo del progetto La carenza di micronutrienti è un problema di salute globale diffuso, principalmente guidato da un'assunzione dietetica insufficiente. Più di 5 miliardi di persone sono stimate di non consumare abbastanza di almeno un micronutriente. Tra questi, le carenze minerali possono essere particolarmente critiche, vale a dire, le carenze di ferro, calcio, zinco e magnesio, che sono particolarmente comuni nei paesi a basso e medio reddito a causa di diete poco minerali e riguardano principalmente donne e bambini. I minerali alimentari sono tipicamente ottenuti da una varietà di alimenti tra cui prodotti a base di animali come carne, latticini e frutti di mare, e alimenti a base vegetale come legumi, cereali, noci, semi e verdure a foglia. Tuttavia, l'affidamento sugli alimenti tradizionali basati sugli animali solleva preoccupazioni relative alla sostenibilità ambientale, considerazioni etiche e preferenze alimentari. Anche se gli alimenti a base vegetale sono generalmente più sostenibili, hanno spesso contenuti minerali più bassi, bioaccessibilità, così come la biodisponibilità a causa della presenza di inibitori di assorbimento come i fiati e i polifenoli. Data queste limitazioni, esiste la necessità di esplorare fonti alimentari alternative, più sostenibili e minerali che possano affrontare efficacemente le carenze minerali globali. Fonti minerali novelli, come le microalghe, potrebbero essere una ricca fonte di minerali essenziali, tra cui ferro, calcio, zinco e magnesio, insieme a proteine, lipidi, vitamine e altri composti bioattivi. Tuttavia, la biodisponibilità di questi minerali deve essere valutata con studi clinici in vivo prima dell'applicazione su larga scala negli esseri umani. Descrizione del lavoro In qualità di studente di dottorato, sarai responsabile della ricerca che lavorerà per esplorare l'assorbimento e la biodisponibilità di nuove fonti minerali con studi clinici. - Summarizzare le conoscenze esistenti sui minerali da fonti nuove per la nutrizione umana e la salute - Pasti di intervento di progettazione (compreso test sensoriale) per studi clinici - Valutare la bioaccessibilità dei minerali in vitro - Valutare la biodisponibilità minerale in vitro - Effettuare prove cliniche relative alla nutrizione umana arricchita da nuove fonti minerali (chiave) - Supportare attività didattiche e co-supervise studenti MSc e BSc - Agire nell'interfaccia tra scienza e tecnologia quando supervisionare gli studenti e collaborare con i partner dell'accademia e dell'industria - Sostegno alle domande di sovvenzione per il team e le attività di supporto da Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for S

descriptionByLocale.de: Beschreibung Doktorandenposition – Bewertung neuartiger Mineralquellen zur Behandlung von Mikronährstoffmangel beim Menschen 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Das ETH Zürich Laboratory of Epigenetics, Nutrition and Metabolism and Sustainable Food Processing Group im Department of Health Science and Technology betreibt eine gemeinsame strategische Forschungslinie über Mikroalgen und pflanzliche Lebensmittel in Human Nutrition and Health. Die Gruppe Sustainable Food Processing konzentriert sich auf einen systemorientierten Ansatz in der Lebensmittelproduktion unter Berücksichtigung der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette, einschließlich der aufstrebenden Bedürfnisse in der Gesellschaft und ihrer ökologischen, wirtschaftlichen und sozialen Auswirkungen. Innovative Rohstoffe werden in städtischen Landwirtschafts- und Verarbeitungskonzepten eingesetzt, um neue Wege der nachhaltigen Lebensmittelversorgung zu ermöglichen. Das Labor für Epigenetik, Ernährung und Metabolismus zielt darauf ab, Einblicke in die komplexe Beziehung zwischen Ernährung, Stoffwechsel und Epigenom mit fortschrittlichen Techniken wie Einzell- und Next-Generation Sequenzierungstechniken sowie menschliche und murine in vivo und in vitro Studien zu gewinnen und diese mit genomweiten rechnerischen und bioinformatischen Analysen zu kombinieren. Mit starker Unterstützung dieser beiden ETH-Gruppen rekrutieren wir so bald wie möglich einen talentierten und hochmotivierten Doktoranden zum Thema „Neue Mineralquellen zur Behandlung von Mikronährstoffmangel beim Menschen“, der sich auf die Untersuchung der Absorption und Bioverfügbarkeit neuartiger Mineralquellen in vivo in klinischen Studien konzentriert. Projekt Hintergrund Mikronährstoffmangel ist ein weit verbreitetes globales Gesundheitsproblem, vor allem durch unzureichende Nahrungsaufnahme angetrieben. Mehr als 5 Milliarden Menschen werden geschätzt, um nicht genug von mindestens einem Mikronährstoff zu konsumieren. Unter diesen können mineralische Mängel besonders kritisch sein, nämlich Eisen-, Kalzium-, Zink- und Magnesiummangel, die besonders häufig in Ländern mit niedrigem und mittlerem Einkommen aufgrund niedrigmineralischer Ernährung und vor allem Frauen und Kinder betreffen. Dietäre Mineralien werden typischerweise aus einer Vielzahl von Lebensmitteln wie Fleisch, Milch und Meeresfrüchten sowie pflanzlichen Lebensmitteln wie Hülsenfrüchten, Getreide, Nüssen, Samen und fruchtigen Gemüsen gewonnen. Die Abhängigkeit von konventionellen tierbasierten Lebensmitteln führt jedoch zu Bedenken im Zusammenhang mit ökologischer Nachhaltigkeit, ethischen Erwägungen und Ernährungspräferenzen. Obwohl pflanzliche Lebensmittel in der Regel nachhaltiger sind, haben sie aufgrund der Anwesenheit von Absorptionsinhibitoren wie Phytate und Polyphenole oft einen geringeren Mineralgehalt, eine Bioverfügbarkeit sowie eine Bioverfügbarkeit. Angesichts dieser Einschränkungen besteht die Notwendigkeit, alternative, nachhaltigere und mineraldichte Lebensmittelquellen zu erforschen, die weltweite Mineralmangel wirksam beheben können. Neuartige Mineralquellen wie Mikroalgen könnten eine reiche Quelle von essentiellen Mineralien sein, einschließlich Eisen, Calcium, Zink und Magnesium, zusammen mit Proteinen, Lipiden, Vitaminen und anderen bioaktiven Verbindungen. Die Bioverfügbarkeit dieser Minerale muss jedoch vor der großtechnischen Anwendung im Menschen mit in vivo klinischen Studien beurteilt werden. Jobbeschreibung Als Doktorandin sind Sie für die Forschung verantwortlich, um die Absorption und Bioverfügbarkeit neuartiger Mineralquellen mit klinischen Studien zu erforschen. - Verbessern Sie das vorhandene Wissen über Mineralien aus neuartigen Quellen für die menschliche Ernährung und Gesundheit - Design Interventionsmehle (einschließlich sensorischer Test) für klinische Studien - Ermöglicht die biologische Zugänglichkeit von Mineralien in vitro - Bewertung der Mineralbioverfügbarkeit in vitro - Durchführung klinischer Studien im Zusammenhang mit der menschlichen Ernährung mit neuartigen Mineralquellen (Schlüssel) - UnterstÃ1⁄4tzung von Lehraktivitäten und Co-Supervise MSc und BSc Studenten - Akt an der Schnittstelle zwischen Wissenschaft und Technologie bei der Betreuung von Studenten und Zusammenarbeit mit Partnern aus Wissenschaft und Industrie - Unterstützungsanträge für das Team und unterstützende Aktivitäten des Singapore-ETH Centre, Bezos Centre for S
descriptionByLocale.fr: Descrizione Position des étudiants au doctorat – Évaluation de nouvelles sources minérales pour le traitement des carences en micronutriments chez l'homme 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le Laboratoire d'épigénétique, de nutrition et de métabolisme et le Groupe de la transformation durable des aliments du Département de la science et de la technologie de la santé de Zurich gèrent une ligne de recherche stratégique conjointe sur les microalgues et les aliments à base de plantes dans la nutrition et la santé humaines. Le groupe de la transformation durable des aliments se concentre sur une approche systémique de la production alimentaire en tenant compte de la chaîne de valeur totale, y compris les besoins émergents de la société et leurs incidences environnementales, économiques et sociales. Les matières premières innovantes sont utilisées dans l'agriculture urbaine et les concepts de transformation pour permettre de nouveaux modes d'approvisionnement alimentaire durable. Le Laboratoire d'Epigénétique, de Nutrition et de Métabolisme vise à mieux comprendre la relation complexe entre la nutrition, le métabolisme et l'épigénome avec des techniques avancées telles que les techniques de séquençage monocellulaire et de prochaine génération, ainsi que les études in vivo et in vitro humaines et murines, et à les combiner avec des analyses computationnelles et bio-informatiques à l'échelle du génome. Avec l'appui fort de ces deux groupes d'ETH, nous recrutons dès que possible un doctorant talentueux et très motivé sur le thème «Nouvelles sources de minéraux pour le traitement des carences en micronutriments chez l'humain», en se concentrant sur l'étude de l'absorption et de la biodisponibilité de nouvelles sources minérales in vivo dans les essais cliniques. Contexte du projet La carence en micronutriments est un problème de santé mondial généralisé, principalement dû à une alimentation inadéquate. On estime que plus de 5 milliards de personnes ne consomment pas suffisamment d'au moins un micronutriment. Parmi celles-ci, les carences minérales peuvent être particulièrement critiques, à savoir les carences en fer, en calcium, en zinc et en magnésium, qui sont particulièrement courantes dans les pays à faible revenu et à revenu intermédiaire en raison de régimes à faible revenu minier et touchent principalement les femmes et les enfants. Les minéraux alimentaires sont généralement obtenus à partir de divers aliments, notamment des produits à base d'animaux comme la viande, les produits laitiers et les fruits de mer, et des aliments à base de plantes comme les légumineuses, les céréales, les noix, les graines et les légumes à feuilles. Toutefois, la dépendance à l'égard des aliments traditionnels à base d'animaux soulève des préoccupations liées à la durabilité environnementale, aux considérations éthiques et aux préférences alimentaires. Bien que les aliments à base de plantes soient généralement plus durables, ils ont souvent une teneur minérale inférieure, la bioaccessibilité, ainsi que la biodisponibilité en raison de la présence d'inhibiteurs d'absorption tels que les phytates et les polyphénols. Compte tenu de ces limites, il est nécessaire d'explorer d'autres sources alimentaires, plus durables et plus riches en minéraux, susceptibles de remédier efficacement aux carences minérales mondiales. De nouvelles sources minérales, comme les microalgues, pourraient être une riche source de minéraux essentiels, notamment le fer, le calcium, le zinc et le magnésium, ainsi que des protéines, des lipides, des vitamines et d'autres composés bioactifs. Cependant, la biodisponibilité de ces minéraux doit être évaluée au moyen d'essais cliniques in vivo avant une application à grande échelle chez l' homme. Description du poste En tant qu'étudiant au doctorat, vous serez responsable de la recherche visant à explorer l'absorption et la biodisponibilité de nouvelles sources minérales avec des essais cliniques. - Résumer les connaissances existantes sur les minéraux provenant de sources nouvelles pour la nutrition et la santé humaines - Concevoir des repas d'intervention (y compris des tests sensoriels) pour les essais cliniques - Évaluer la bioaccessibilité des minéraux in vitro - Évaluer la biodisponibilité minérale in vitro - Effectuer des essais cliniques liés à la nutrition humaine enrichie en nouvelles sources minérales (clé) - Soutenir les activités d'enseignement et co-superviser les étudiants en maîtrise et en baccalauréat - Agir à l'interface entre la science et la technologie lors de la supervision des étudiants et de la collaboration avec des partenaires du milieu universitaire et de l'industrie - Demandes de subvention d ' appui à l ' équipe et activités connexes du Centre Singapour-ETH, Centre Bezos

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

Project background

As high-performance computing, AI, and cloud technologies continue to converge, CSCS is redefining how to design and deliver advanced computational services. Modern scientific and engineering workloads are no longer just large; they are complex, data-intensive, and highly diverse, meaning they push existing infrastructure to its limits.

This position is funded via the Helvetic AI Resources ,Technologies, and Services (HEARTS) project, and is based on a two‑year contract, which can be extended or potentially become permanent.

Our core values:

We are looking for candidates who share our guiding principles:

• Curiosity: You enjoy learning, exploring new ideas, and understanding problems deeply.

• Openness: You listen, collaborate, and are receptive to different perspectives.

jobs.description:
Postdoc Position in Experimental Quantum Engineering (EQE) Group

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Experimental Quantum Engineering (EQE) group at ETH Zurich and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) invites applications for a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to work at the interface of quantum optics, quantum information science and quantum many-body physics.

Led by Prof. Wenchao Xu , the EQE group develops programmable quantum systems based on neutral atoms and Rydberg interactions to advance both fundamental quantum science and next-generation quantum technologies. Our research combines atomic physics, quantum control, and scalable architectures for fault-tolerant quantum computation, hybrid quantum simulation, and quantum-enhanced sensing.

Project background

Our group addresses key challenges in quantum science by building and exploiting hybrid quantum systems consisting of individually controlled atoms and atomic ensembles.

Current research directions include:

• Demonstrating scalable architectures for fault-tolerant quantum information processing, featuring reconfigurable local control, rapid quantum non-demolition readout, and fast error-syndrome extraction

• Developing strong atom–light interfaces to enable quantum interconnects and modular quantum systems

• Investigating non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics and quantum information dynamics in programmable atom arrays

Job description

We seek a postdoctoral researcher to contribute to a new experimental platform based on dual-type tweezer atom arrays.

The project aims to demonstrate the unique advantages for:

• Reconfigurable local quantum control

• Rapid, non-demolition state detection of both single- and multi-qubit states

• Novel phenomena in quantum dynamics arising from the interplay with measurement

These capabilities enable new routes toward fault-tolerant quantum computation and open exciting opportunities for exploring frontier problems in quantum information dynamics.

The successful candidate will:

• Design, build, and operate state-of-the-art neutral-atom experiments

• Demonstrate novel quantum control and measurement protocols

• Lead research projects and mentor students

• Collaborate closely with researchers at ETH Zurich, PSI, and international partners

More information about the project and the group can be found on our website .

Starting date: flexible in 2026

Employment: full-time

Profile

• PhD in physics or a related field

• Strong background in experimental AMO physics or quantum optics

• Experience with cold atoms, optical tweezers, lasers, or quantum control techniques is highly desirable

• Strong interest in neutral-atom quantum technologies and many-body quantum physics

• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively

• Good communication skills in English (German is a plus)

Workplace

We offer

• A highly creative and collaborative research environment

• Freedom to develop independent research directions

• Access to world-class infrastructure at ETH Zurich and PSI

• Opportunities for interdisciplinary and international collaborations

• Competitive salary and benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

• CV (with publication list)

• Cover letter

• 2-3 references

Please submit your application through our onli

Project background Our group addresses key challenges in quantum science by building and exploiting hybrid quantum systems consisting of individually controlled atoms and atomic ensembles. Current research directions include:
• Demonstrating scalable architectures for fault-tolerant quantum information processing, featuring reconfigurable local control, rapid quantum non-demolition readout, and fast error-syndrome extraction
• Developing strong atom–light interfaces to enable quantum interconnects and modular quantum systems
• Investigating non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics and quantum information dynamics in programmable atom arrays Job description We seek a postdoctoral researcher to contribute to a new experimental platform based on dual-type tweezer atom arrays. • Reconfigurable local quantum control
• Rapid, non-demolition state detection of both single- and multi-qubit states

jobs.description:
Earth Systems Data Manager (Petabyte-Scale Infrastructure)

80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Center for Climate Systems Modeling (C2SM) at ETH Zurich is a joint, interdisciplinary center linking ETH Zurich with partner institutions. It provides a technology and networking platform to support the development and application of Earth system, weather, and climate modeling, data infrastructure, and impact research.

Project background

There is an ever-increasing amount and diversity of Earth observations collected from satellites, airborne instruments, in-situ measurement networks, and high-resolution climate modeling data produced at C2SM. Harnessing these data effectively is essential for advancing our understanding of the Earth system. C2SM in collaboration with Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) is extending its data services and is building a petabyte-scale data lake consisting of highly diverse observational and model data.

To address this challenge, a robust data management framework is being developed to make rapidly growing Earth-system datasets accessible and usable for the scientific community. We are looking for an Earth Systems Data Manager to play a pivotal role in shaping this framework. This technical position focuses on identifying observational datasets relevant to Earth science research across disciplines, curating and documenting data collections to ensure quality and scientific value, and establishing metadata and access standards to support data discovery and reproducibility. Working closely with researchers and developers from C2SM, ETH, CSCS, as well as national and international institutions, the successful candidate will support operating and advancing the data platform, assist interdisciplinary projects that integrate multiple data sources, and use high-performance computing resources to manage and process large environmental datasets such that they are ready to be used for research.

Job description

• Identify Earth system observations that are relevant to interdisciplinary research needs

• Curate data collections by assessing quality, completeness, and scientific value

• Create comprehensive metadata and documentation to support data discovery and use

• Begin developing a platform to provide users with an overview of the available data

• Coordinate with researchers in climate science, environmental monitoring, data science, and related fields

• Collaborate with a dynamic and international team of developers and researchers developers to operate and further advance the data platform

• Support interdisciplinary research projects that require multiple data sources

• Work with high-performance computing platforms for data storage and to provide analysis tools for researchers

Profile

• Degree in data science, computer science, Earth or atmospheric sciences, or a related field

• Knowledge of satellite data and remote sensing

• Experience with very large datasets (petabyte-scale), data management and data quality control

• Very good skills with programming languages such as Python/R/Julia, use of scientific data libraries (e.g., xarray, netCDF4, HDF5, Zarr), and workflow automation on HPC systems

• At least 3 years of interdisciplinary work experience (PhD not included)

• Strong communication skills for working across different scientific disciplines

Beneficial:

• Experience working in an interdisciplinary environment

• PhD in remote sensing or a related field

• Experience in working with very large atmospheric observational or model data

• Experience in leading projects, ideally within multiple different domains

• Experience with user support, data documentation, FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable)

Workplace

We offer

In this role, you will work at the cutting-edge intersection of Earth system modelling, high-performance computing and data-driven science. You will join the Center for Climate Systems Modeling (C2SM),

Il fournit une plate-forme technologique et de réseautage pour appuyer le développement et l'application du système terrestre, de la modélisation météorologique et climatique, de l'infrastructure de données et de la recherche sur l'impact. Contexte du projet - La quantité et la diversité des observations de la Terre recueillies à partir de satellites, d ' instruments aéroportés, de réseaux de mesure in situ et de données de modélisation climatique à haute résolution sont de plus en plus nombreuses. - Il est essentiel d'exploiter efficacement ces données pour mieux comprendre le système terrestre - C2SM, en collaboration avec le Centre National de SuperComputation (CSCS), étend ses services de données et construit un lac de données à l'échelle des pétaoctets composé de données d'observation et de modèles très divers - Pour relever ce défi, un solide cadre de gestion des données est en cours d ' élaboration afin de rendre les ensembles de données du système terrestre rapidement en croissance accessibles et utilisables par la communauté scientifique. - Nous sommes à la recherche d'un gestionnaire de données des systèmes de Terre pour jouer un rôle central dans l'élaboration de ce cadre - Cette position technique vise à identifier les ensembles de données d'observation pertinents pour la recherche en sciences de la Terre dans toutes les disciplines, à assurer la conservation et la documentation des collections de données afin d'en assurer la qualité et la valeur scientifique, et à établir des métadonnées et des normes d'accès pour appuyer la découverte et la reproductibilité des données - Travailler en étroite collaboration avec des chercheurs et des développeurs de C2SM, ETH, SCCS, ainsi qu'avec des institutions nationales et internationales, le candidat retenu appuiera le fonctionnement et le développement de la plate-forme de données, aidera les projets interdisciplinaires qui intègrent de multiples sources de données et utilisera des ressources informatiques de haute performance pour gérer et traiter de grands ensembles de données environnementales de sorte qu'ils soient prêts à être utilisés pour la recherche Description du poste - Identifier les observations du système terrestre pertinentes aux besoins de recherche interdisciplinaires - Collecte de données curatives en évaluant la qualité, l'exhaustivité et la valeur scientifique - Créer des métadonnées et une documentation complètes pour appuyer la découverte et l'utilisation des données - Commencer à développer une plate-forme pour fournir aux utilisateurs un aperçu des données disponibles - Coordonner avec les chercheurs en sciences du climat, surveillance de l'environnement, science des données et domaines connexes - Collaborer avec une équipe dynamique et internationale de développeurs et de chercheurs développeurs pour exploiter et faire progresser la plate-forme de données - Soutenir des projets de recherche interdisciplinaires nécessitant plusieurs sources de données - Travailler avec des plateformes informatiques performantes pour le stockage des données et fournir des outils d'analyse aux chercheurs Profil - Diplôme en sciences des données, en informatique, en sciences de la Terre ou de l'atmosphère, ou dans un domaine connexe - Connaissance des données satellitaires et de la télédétection - Expérience avec de très grands ensembles de données (à l'échelle du petabyte), gestion des données et contrôle de la qualité des données - De très bonnes compétences avec des langages de programmation tels que Python/R/Julia, l'utilisation de bibliothèques de données scientifiques (par exemple xarray, netCDF4, HDF5, Zarr) et l'automatisation des flux de travail sur les systèmes HPC - Au moins 3 ans d'expérience de travail interdisciplinaire (PhD non inclus) - Fortes compétences en communication pour travailler dans différentes disciplines scientifiques Bénéfice - Expérience de travail dans un environnement interdisciplinaire - Doctorat en télédétection ou dans un domaine connexe - Expérience de travail avec de très grandes données d'observation atmosphérique ou de modèle - Expérience dans les projets de pointe, idéalement dans plusieurs domaines différents - Expérience avec support utilisateur, documentation de données, principes de données FAIR (fichable, accessible, interopérable, réutilisable) Lieu de travail Lieu de travail
• Cosa offriamo - Dans ce rôle, vous travaillerez à l'intersection de pointe de la modélisation du système terrestre, de l'informatique à haute performance et de la science axée sur les données - Vous rejoindrez le Centre de modélisation des systèmes climatiques (C2SM)

jobs.description:
Doctoral researcher (PhD Position) in Conversational AI for Customer and Employee Interactions

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Technology Marketing Group , founded by Florian von Wangenheim in 2013, is a pioneering research group at ETH Zurich dedicated to exploring the intersection of marketing, technology, and societal impact. Together with its associated centres and labs, we investigate how to effectively market innovative offerings and how emerging technologies transform the relationship between organisations and their stakeholders.

The current PhD position offers an exciting opportunity to work with two centres within the Chair on managerially-relevant applied research:

The Mobiliar Lab for Analytics at ETH Zurich develops and tests digital interactions using emerging technologies and artificial intelligence. As a joint initiative of ETH Zurich and a Swiss insurer, we focus on exploring the benefits of emerging technologies balanced against their dark sides. Our research at the intersection of data, behavioural, and computer science draws on data from real-world and experimental settings

The Centre for AI Value identifies and implements AI applications to generate economic value. It bridges academic AI research with practical business applications, focusing on customer service, multimodal data modelling, and process automation

Project background

During your PhD, you will examine how conversational AI can be deployed effectively to frontline service interactions with customers or as a support tool for employees. Projects will explore success factors in designing and deploying Conversational AI. This could include, for example, varying technical foundations (e.g., prompt engineering, fine-tuning, model architecture and retrieval strategies), the usage context (e.g., routine vs. special services), or unique individual level factors (e.g., personality profile, AI literacy) to ensure Conversational AI is optimised for its deployment context and contributes to excellent customer service and workplace efficiency. Research output will therefore have clear managerial relevance. Research activities will involve analysis of primary and secondary data, in both controlled and field settings. The successful candidate will shape projects and research questions within this overarching scope, whilst working alongside closely industry partners and reacting to emergent research opportunities.

Job description

We are currently seeking a doctoral researcher with both technical knowledge and skills related to the technical foundations of conversational AI as well as domain knowledge on how and why it can be deployed effectively. You should have knowledge and skills in both data analytics (e.g., machine learning, statistics, econometrics) and behavioural sciences (e.g., experimental design, survey research, application/development of managerially relevant theory). Software engineering skills (e.g., REST API development, SQL/NoSQL databases, cloud deployment (AWS/Azure/GCP), Docker) are also very welcome. You will need to be highly flexible and responsive to emerging opportunities with partners from industry. The candidate should be highly motivated to drive projects forward, as well as network across Switzerland.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Using data and technology to conduct managerially relevant research

• Collaborating with experts and industry partners

• Attending international conferences to share your work

• Publishing in top scientific journals in Marketing and Information Systems fields (e.g., Journal of Marketing, Marketing Science, Management Information Systems Quarterly, Information Systems Research, Decision Support Systems etc.).

• Communicating and engaging with the public

• Teaching support and supervision under the umbrella of the Chair of Technology Marketing, D-MTEC

Profile

Essential requirements:

• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English

• Master&rsqu

Descrizione Ricercatore di dottorato (PhD Position) in AI Conversazionale per le interazioni tra clienti e dipendenti 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Technology Marketing Group, fondato da Florian von Wangenheim nel 2013, è un gruppo di ricerca pionieristico dell'ETH Zurich dedicato all'esplorazione dell'intersezione del marketing, della tecnologia e dell'impatto sociale. Insieme ai suoi centri e laboratori associati, studiamo come commercializzare efficacemente offerte innovative e come le tecnologie emergenti trasformino il rapporto tra le organizzazioni e i loro stakeholder. L'attuale posizione PhD offre un'emozionante opportunità di lavorare con due centri all'interno della Cattedra sulla ricerca applicata gestionale-rilevante: Il Laboratorio Mobiliar per l'analisi di ETH Zurich sviluppa e testa le interazioni digitali utilizzando tecnologie emergenti e intelligenza artificiale. Come iniziativa congiunta di ETH Zurich e di un assicuratore svizzero, ci concentriamo sull'esplorazione dei benefici delle tecnologie emergenti bilanciate contro i loro lati oscuri. La nostra ricerca all'intersezione di dati, comportamenti e informatica si basa sui dati provenienti da contesti reali e sperimentali Il Centre for AI Value identifica e implementa le applicazioni AI per generare valore economico. Esso collega la ricerca accademica AI con applicazioni pratiche aziendali, concentrandosi sul servizio clienti, la modellazione di dati multimodali, e l'automazione dei processi Sfondo del progetto Durante il dottorato, esaminerai come l'IA conversazione può essere implementata efficacemente per front-line interazioni di servizio con i clienti o come strumento di supporto per i dipendenti. I progetti esploreranno i fattori di successo nella progettazione e distribuzione di AI Conversational. Ciò potrebbe includere, ad esempio, diverse basi tecniche (ad esempio, ingegneria rapida, fine-tuning, architettura del modello e strategie di recupero), il contesto di utilizzo (ad esempio, servizi speciali di routine e), o fattori di livello individuale unici (ad esempio, profilo della personalità, alfabetizzazione dell'AI) per garantire che l'IA Conversazionale sia ottimizzata per il suo contesto di distribuzione e contribuisca all'eccellente assistenza clienti e all'efficienza sul luogo di lavoro. La produzione di ricerca avrà quindi una chiara rilevanza manageriale. Le attività di ricerca coinvolgeranno l'analisi dei dati primari e secondari, sia nelle impostazioni controllate che sul campo. Il candidato di successo formerà i progetti e le domande di ricerca all'interno di questo ambito di overarching, mentre lavorerà accanto a partner del settore e reagirà alle opportunità di ricerca emergenti. Descrizione del lavoro Siamo attualmente alla ricerca di un ricercatore di dottorato con conoscenze tecniche e competenze relative alle basi tecniche di AI colloquiale e conoscenze di dominio su come e perché può essere implementato in modo efficace. Si dovrebbe avere conoscenze e competenze in entrambe le analisi dei dati (ad esempio, machine learning, statistiche, econometria) e scienze comportamentali (ad esempio, progettazione sperimentale, ricerca di indagine, applicazione / sviluppo di teoria managerialmente rilevante). Le competenze di ingegneria del software (ad esempio, sviluppo REST API, database SQL/NoSQL, distribuzione cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), Docker) sono anche molto benvenuti. Dovrai essere altamente flessibile e reattivo alle opportunità emergenti con partner del settore. Il candidato dovrebbe essere altamente motivato a guidare i progetti in avanti, così come la rete in tutta la Svizzera. Le responsabilità includono, ma non sono limitate a:
• Utilizzo dei dati e della tecnologia per condurre ricerche gestionali rilevanti
• Collaborare con esperti e partner del settore
• Partecipare a conferenze internazionali per condividere il vostro lavoro
• Pubblicazione in riviste scientifiche superiori nei settori Marketing e Sistemi Informativi (ad esempio, Journal of Marketing, Marketing Science, Management Information Systems Quarterly, Information Systems Research, Decision Support Systems ecc.).
• Comunicare e impegnarsi con il pubblico
• Supporto didattico e supervisione sotto l'ombrello della Cattedra di Marketing Tecnologico, D-MTEC Profilo Requisiti essenziali:
• Eccellente capacità di comunicazione scritta e orale in inglese
• Master&rsqu

Beschreibung Doktorand (PhD-Position) in Konversations-KI für Kunden- und Mitarbeiterinteraktionen 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Die 2013 von Florian von Wangenheim gegründete Technologie-Marketing-Gruppe ist eine Pionier-Forschungsgruppe an der ETH Zürich, die sich für die Erkundung der Schnittstelle von Marketing, Technologie und gesellschaftlicher Wirkung einsetzt. Gemeinsam mit den dazugehörigen Zentren und Laboren untersuchen wir, wie wir innovative Angebote effektiv vermarkten und wie sich aufstrebende Technologien die Beziehung zwischen Organisationen und ihren Interessenvertretern verändern. Die aktuelle PhD-Position bietet eine spannende Gelegenheit, mit zwei Zentren im Lehrstuhl für managerrelevante angewandte Forschung zu arbeiten: Das Mobiliar Lab for Analytics der ETH Zürich entwickelt und testet digitale Interaktionen mit aufstrebenden Technologien und künstlicher Intelligenz. Als gemeinsame Initiative der ETH Zürich und eines Schweizer Versicherers konzentrieren wir uns auf die Erkundung der Vorteile der aufstrebenden Technologien, die gegen ihre dunklen Seiten ausgewogen sind. Unsere Forschung an der Schnittstelle von Daten, Verhalten und Informatik bezieht sich auf Daten aus realen und experimentellen Einstellungen Das Zentrum für KI-Wert identifiziert und implementiert KI-Anwendungen, um wirtschaftlichen Wert zu generieren. Es überbrückt akademische KI-Forschung mit praktischen Geschäftsanwendungen, konzentriert sich auf Kundendienst, multimodale Datenmodellierung und Prozessautomatisierung Projekt Hintergrund Während Ihres PhD werden Sie untersuchen, wie konversale KI effektiv eingesetzt werden kann, um Service-Interaktionen mit Kunden oder als Support-Tool für Mitarbeiter vorzustellen. Projekte werden Erfolgsfaktoren bei der Konzeption und Bereitstellung von Conversational AI untersuchen. Dazu gehören beispielsweise unterschiedliche technische Grundlagen (z.B. schnelles Engineering, Feinabstimmung, Modellarchitektur und Retrievalstrategien), der Nutzungskontext (z.B. Routine vs. Sonderdienste) oder einzigartige individuelle Levelfaktoren (z.B. Persönlichkeitsprofil, AI-Literatur) um sicherzustellen, dass Conversational AI für seinen Einsatzkontext optimiert ist und zu ausgezeichneter Kundendienst- und Arbeitsplatzeffizienz beiträgt. Die Forschungsleistung wird daher eine klare leitungsbezogene Relevanz haben. Die Forschungsaktivitäten werden die Analyse der primären und sekundären Daten sowohl in kontrollierten als auch in Feldeinstellungen beinhalten. Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird Projekte und Forschungsfragen in diesem übergeordneten Bereich prägen, gleichzeitig eng mit Industriepartnern zusammenarbeiten und auf neue Forschungsmöglichkeiten reagieren. Jobbeschreibung Wir suchen derzeit einen Doktoranden mit technischen Kenntnissen und Fähigkeiten im Zusammenhang mit den technischen Grundlagen der gesprächigen KI sowie Domänenkenntnissen, wie und warum sie effektiv eingesetzt werden können. Sie sollten Kenntnisse und Fähigkeiten in beiden Datenanalysen (z.B. maschinelles Lernen, Statistik, Ökonometrie) und Verhaltenswissenschaften (z.B. experimentelles Design, Umfrageforschung, Anwendung/Entwicklung von managerrelevanten Theorien) haben. Software Engineering-Fähigkeiten (z.B. REST API-Entwicklung, SQL/NoSQL-Datenbanken, Cloud-Bereitstellung (AWS/Azure/GCP), Docker) sind ebenfalls sehr willkommen. Sie müssen mit Partnern aus der Industrie sehr flexibel und auf neue Chancen reagieren. Der Kandidat sollte sehr motiviert sein, Projekte voranzutreiben, sowie Netzwerk in der Schweiz. Zu den Aufgaben gehören:
• Verwendung von Daten und Technologien zur leitungsrelevanten Forschung
• Zusammenarbeit mit Experten und Industriepartnern
• Internationale Konferenzen zum Austausch Ihrer Arbeit
• Veröffentlichen in Top-wissenschaftlichen Zeitschriften in den Bereichen Marketing und Informationssysteme (z.B. Journal of Marketing, Marketing Science, Management Information Systems Quarterly, Information Systems Research, Decision Support Systems etc.).
• Kommunikation und Beteiligung an der Öffentlichkeit
• Lehrunterstützung und Aufsicht unter dem Dach des Lehrstuhls für Technologiemarketing, D-MTEC Profil Wesentliche Anforderungen:

Descrizione Chercheur au doctorat (poste de doctorat) en AI conversationnelle pour les interactions avec les clients et les employés 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le Technology Marketing Group , fondé par Florian von Wangenheim en 2013, est un groupe de recherche pionnier à l'ETH Zurich dédié à explorer l'intersection du marketing, de la technologie et de l'impact sociétal. Avec ses centres et laboratoires associés, nous étudions comment commercialiser efficacement des offres innovantes et comment les technologies émergentes transforment les relations entre les organisations et leurs parties prenantes. Le poste actuel de PhD offre une excellente occasion de travailler avec deux centres de la Chaire sur la recherche appliquée pertinente en gestion : Le Mobiliar Lab for Analytics de l'ETH Zurich développe et teste des interactions numériques à l'aide de technologies émergentes et d'intelligence artificielle. En tant qu'initiative conjointe de l'ETH Zurich et d'un assureur suisse, nous nous concentrons sur l'exploration des avantages des technologies émergentes en équilibre avec leur côté sombre. Nos recherches à l'intersection des données, du comportement et de l'informatique s'appuient sur des données provenant de milieux réels et expérimentaux. Le Centre de la valeur de l'IA identifie et met en œuvre des applications d'IA pour générer de la valeur économique. Il relie la recherche universitaire sur l'IA avec des applications commerciales pratiques, en mettant l'accent sur le service à la clientèle, la modélisation de données multimodales et l'automatisation des processus Contexte du projet Pendant votre doctorat, vous examinerez comment l'IA conversationnelle peut être déployée efficacement dans les interactions de service de première ligne avec les clients ou comme outil de soutien pour les employés. Les projets exploreront les facteurs de succès dans la conception et le déploiement de l'IA conversationnelle. Cela pourrait inclure, par exemple, divers fondements techniques (p. ex., ingénierie rapide, réglage fin, architecture de modèles et stratégies de récupération), le contexte d'utilisation (p. ex., routine ou services spéciaux) ou des facteurs individuels uniques (p. ex., profil de la personnalité, connaissance de l'IA) pour s'assurer que l'IA conversationnelle est optimisée pour son contexte de déploiement et contribue à un excellent service à la clientèle et à une efficacité en milieu de travail. Les résultats de la recherche seront donc clairement pertinents pour la gestion. Les activités de recherche comprendront l'analyse des données primaires et secondaires, tant sur le terrain que sur le terrain. Le candidat retenu façonnera les projets et les questions de recherche dans ce cadre global, tout en collaborant étroitement avec les partenaires de l'industrie et en réagissant aux possibilités de recherche émergentes. Description du poste Nous cherchons actuellement un doctorant possédant à la fois des connaissances techniques et des compétences liées aux fondements techniques de l'IA conversationnelle ainsi que des connaissances de domaine sur la façon et les raisons de son déploiement efficace. Vous devriez posséder des connaissances et des compétences en analyse des données (p. ex., apprentissage automatique, statistiques, économétrie) et en sciences du comportement (p. ex., conception expérimentale, recherche sur les enquêtes, application/développement d'une théorie pertinente pour la gestion). Les compétences en génie logiciel (par exemple, développement de l'API REST, bases de données SQL/NoSQL, déploiement de cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), Docker) sont également les bienvenues. Vous devrez être très souple et réceptif aux nouvelles possibilités avec des partenaires de l'industrie. Le candidat devrait être très motivé pour faire avancer les projets, ainsi que le réseau à travers la Suisse. Les responsabilités comprennent, sans s'y limiter :
• Utiliser les données et la technologie pour mener des recherches pertinentes du point de vue de la gestion
• Collaborer avec des experts et des partenaires industriels
• Assister à des conférences internationales pour partager votre travail
• Publication dans des revues scientifiques de haut niveau dans les domaines du marketing et des systèmes d'information (par exemple, Journal of Marketing, Marketing Science, Management Information Systems Quarterly, Information Systems Research, Decision Support Systems, etc.).
• Communiquer et dialoguer avec le public
• Appui pédagogique et supervision sous l'égide de la Chaire de marketing technologique, D-MTEC Profil Exigences essentielles:
• Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale en anglais

jobs.description:
Postdoc Position in Advanced Bioelectronic & Electrical Conversion Research

100%, Basel, fixed-term

print
Drucken

A World-Class Research Environment at the Nexus of Biology, Engineering, and Physical Sciences

The Biotechnology and Bioengineering group led by Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger at the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) of ETH Zurich in Basel invites exceptional candidates to apply for a Postdoc position in pioneering projects at the intersection of synthetic biology, nanotechnology, and bioelectronics .

The D-BSSE is ETH Zurich's first truly interdisciplinary research department uniting theoretical and experimental biology with advanced bioengineering and fostering close collaborations with leaders in materials science, physics, and chemistry to drive transformative advances in systems biology, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Situated in Basel, Switzerland, at the heart of the BioValley , a tri-national region that hosts 40% of the global life sciences industry and numerous major pharmaceutical companies, the D-BSSE offers a unique environment for high-impact translational research with unparalleled access to academic and industrial expertise.

Project background

Advancing the Frontiers of Bioelectronics and Synthetic Biology

Our group integrates state-of-the-art synthetic biology with advanced nanotechnology, and electrogenetic interfaces to engineer human cells for next generation bioelectronic medicine, designing programmable cells that respond to electrical, electromagnetic, acoustic and biochemical cues to achieve wireless, real-time control of therapeutic protein expression and metabolic regulation. Leveraging innovative platforms such as direct-current-actuated regulation , electromagnetic programming of wireless expression , and closed-loop systems , we aim to translate these technologies into clinically relevant, minimally invasive therapies for cancer, as well as metabolic, neurodegenerative, autoimmune, and infectious diseases.

Job description

• Postdoctoral projects will combine catalyst engineering, computational simulation, bioelectrode device fabrication, and electrical engineering to develop bioelectronic interfaces enabling closed-loop programming of cellular behaviour and real-time monitoring of metabolic activity

• There will also be opportunities to design novel bioelectronic implants and develop specialized control software

Profile

• We are seeking highly motivated applicants with a background in physics, material science, or chemistry

• Ideally with expertise in bioelectronics or software simulations, or a strong willingness to acquire it, alongside solid knowledge of electrochemistry and materials chemistry

• Candidates should be eager to collaborate closely with molecular biologists and bioengineers and demonstrate a strong academic record with the ambition to pursue a career in industrial R&D, or entrepreneurship

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Descrizione Postdoc Posizione nella Ricerca avanzata di Bioelettronica e conversione elettrica 100%, Basilea, a tempo determinato Un ambiente di ricerca di classe mondiale al Nexus di biologia, ingegneria e scienze fisiche Il gruppo Biotecnologia e Bioingegneria guidato dal Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger presso il Dipartimento di Scienze e Ingegneria dei Biosistemi (D-BSSE) dell'ETH di Zurigo a Basilea invita candidati eccezionali a richiedere una posizione Postdoc nei progetti pionieristici all'incrocio di biologia sintetica, nanotecnologia e bioelettronica. Il D-BSSE è il primo dipartimento di ricerca veramente interdisciplinare dell'ETH di Zurigo che unisce biologia teorica e sperimentale con una bioingegneria avanzata e promuove una stretta collaborazione con i leader nella scienza dei materiali, nella fisica e nella chimica per guidare i progressi trasformativi nella biologia dei sistemi, nella biotecnologia e nella biologia sintetica. Situato a Basilea, in Svizzera, nel cuore della BioValley, una regione trinazionale che ospita il 40% dell'industria globale delle scienze della vita e numerose importanti aziende farmaceutiche, il D-BSSE offre un ambiente unico per la ricerca traduttiva ad alto impatto con un accesso senza precedenti alle competenze accademiche e industriali. Sfondo del progetto Promuovere le frontiere della bioelettronica e della biologia sintetica Il nostro gruppo integra la biologia sintetica all'avanguardia con le nanotecnologie avanzate e le interfacce elettrogenetiche per l'ingegneria delle cellule umane per la medicina bioelettronica di nuova generazione, progettando cellule programmabili che rispondono a segnali elettrici, elettromagnetici, acustici e biochimici per ottenere il controllo wireless, in tempo reale dell'espressione proteica terapeutica e della regolazione metabolica. Sfruttando piattaforme innovative come la regolazione a corrente diretta, la programmazione elettromagnetica dell'espressione wireless e sistemi a ciclo chiuso, intendiamo tradurre queste tecnologie in terapie clinicamente rilevanti, minimamente invasive per il cancro, così come le malattie metaboliche, neurodegenerative, autoimmuni e infettive. Descrizione del lavoro - I progetti postdoctoral combinano l'ingegneria catalizzante, la simulazione computazionale, la fabbricazione di dispositivi bioelettrodi e l'ingegneria elettrica per sviluppare interfacce bioelettroniche che permettono la programmazione a ciclo chiuso del comportamento cellulare e il monitoraggio in tempo reale dell'attività metabolica - Ci saranno anche opportunità di progettare nuovi impianti bioelettronici e sviluppare software di controllo specializzato Profilo -
• Stiamo cercando candidati altamente motivati con un background in fisica, scienza materiale, o chimica - Idealmente con competenze in bioelettronica o simulazioni software, o una forte disponibilità ad acquisirlo, oltre a una solida conoscenza della chimica elettrochimica e dei materiali - I candidati dovrebbero essere desiderosi di collaborare strettamente con i biologi molecolari e i bioingegneria e dimostrare un forte record accademico con l'ambizione di perseguire una carriera nella R&D industriale, o imprenditorialità Luogo di lavoro Luogo di lavoro Cosa? - Il tuo lavoro con impatto: Diventa parte dell'ETH di Zurigo, che non solo supporta lo sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce attivamente al cambiamento positivo nella società - Siamo attivamente impegnati in un'università sostenibile e neutrale dal clima - Puoi aspettarti numerosi vantaggi, come i biglietti per la stagione dei trasporti pubblici e la condivisione delle auto, una vasta gamma di sport offerti dall'ASVZ, dall'assistenza all'infanzia e dalle interessanti prestazioni pensionistiche Lavoro, insegnamento e ricerca presso l'ETH di Zurigo Apprezziamo la diversità e la sostenibilità In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoc Position in Advanced Bioelectronic & Electrical Conversion Research 100%, Basel, fixed-term print Drucken A World-Class Research Environment at the Nexus of Biology, Engineering, and Physical Sciences The Biotechnology and Bioengineering group led by Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger at the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) of ETH Zurich in Basel invites exceptional candidates to apply for a Postdoc position in pioneering projects at the intersection of synthetic biology, nanotechnology, and bioelectronics . The D-BSSE is ETH Zurich's first truly interdisciplinary research department uniting theoretical and experimental biology with advanced bioengineering and fostering close collaborations with leaders in materials science, physics, and chemistry to drive transformative advances in systems biology, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Situated in Basel, Switzerland, at the heart of the BioValley , a tri-national region that hosts 40% of the global life sciences industry and numerous major pharmaceutical companies, the D-BSSE offers a unique environment for high-impact translational research with unparalleled access to academic and industrial expertise. Project background Advancing the Frontiers of Bioelectronics and Synthetic Biology Our group integrates state-of-the-art synthetic biology with advanced nanotechnology, and electrogenetic interfaces to engineer human cells for next generation bioelectronic medicine, designing programmable cells that respond to electrical, electromagnetic, acoustic and biochemical cues to achieve wireless, real-time control of therapeutic protein expression and metabolic regulation. Leveraging innovative platforms such as direct-current-actuated regulation , electromagnetic programming of wireless expression , and closed-loop systems , we aim to translate these technologies into clinically relevant, minimally invasive therapies for cancer, as well as metabolic, neurodegenerative, autoimmune, and infectious diseases. Job description
• Postdoctoral projects will combine catalyst engineering, computational simulation, bioelectrode device fabrication, and electrical engineering to develop bioelectronic interfaces enabling closed-loop programming of cellular behaviour and real-time monitoring of metabolic activity
• There will also be opportunities to design novel bioelectronic implants and develop specialized control software Profile
• We are seeking highly motivated applicants with a background in physics, material science, or chemistry
• Ideally with expertise in bioelectronics or software simulations, or a strong willingness to acquire it, alongside solid knowledge of electrochemistry and materials chemistry
• Candidates should be eager to collaborate closely with molecular biologists and bioengineers and demonstrate a strong academic record with the ambition to pursue a career in industrial R&D, or entrepreneurship Workplace Workplace We offer
• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society
• We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university
• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits chevron_right Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future . C

jobs.description:
PhD Position for Synthetic Biology-Inspired Therapies

100%, Basel, fixed-term

print
Drucken

A World-Class Research Environment at the Nexus of Biology, Engineering, and Physical Sciences

The Biotechnology and Bioengineering group led by Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger at the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) of the ETH Zurich in Basel invites exceptional candidates to apply for a PhD position in pioneering projects developing synthetic biology-inspired human therapies.

The D-BSSE is the first truly interdisciplinary research department, uniting theoretical and experimental biology with advanced bioengineering and fostering close collaborations with leaders in material science, physics, and chemistry to drive transformative advances in systems biology, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Situated in Basel, Switzerland, at the heart of the BioValley, a tri-national region that hosts 40% of the global life science industry and numerous major pharmaceutical companies, the D-BSSE offers a unique environment for high-impact translational research with unparalleled access to academic and industrial expertise.

Project background

Advancing the Frontiers of Cell-based therapies and Synthetic Biology

Our group applies state-of-the-art synthetic biology principles to engineer human cells and create next-generation cell-based therapies targeting cancer as well as metabolic, neurodegenerative, autoimmune and infectious diseases. Leveraging innovative platforms such as novel biosensors, gene switches, genetic closed-loop circuits, and chemical structures that interface with and actuate cellular activities, we design programmable cellular implants and devices for therapeutic applications. By integrating fundamental discoveries with translational development, we aim to shape the future of biomedical innovation.

Job description

• PhD projects will combine molecular engineering, cell programming, and chemical–biological interfacing to engineer human cells using synthetic gene circuits and biosensing platforms, develop novel biosensing systems for real-time monitoring of cellular states, create genetic architectures for precise therapeutic protein regulation, and translate these research advances into programmable cellular implant prototypes

• Projects will be highly interdisciplinary, fostering close collaboration with molecular biologists, bioengineers, and clinical researchers to accelerate translation into clinically relevant therapies

Profile

• We are seeking highly motivated applicants eager to bridge basic and translational research in cell biology and synthetic biology

• Candidates should have strong skills in molecular and cell biology techniques, including cultivation and engineering of primary human cells and mammalian cell lines. Experience with in vivo techniques, as well as completion of an accredited course in laboratory animal science (FELASA / LTK or equivalent), would be an asset

• We welcome applicants with an outstanding academic record and who are enthusiastic about building a career in academia, industrial R&D, or biotechnology entrepreneurship

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity websi
