jobs.description:
Postdoc Position for Synthetic Biology-Inspired Therapies

100%, Basel, fixed-term

print
Drucken

A World-Class Research Environment at the Nexus of Biology, Engineering, and Physical Sciences

The Biotechnology and Bioengineering group led by Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger at the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) of the ETH Zurich in Basel invites exceptional candidates to apply for a postdoctoral position in pioneering projects developing synthetic biology-inspired human therapies.

The D-BSSE is the first truly interdisciplinary research department, uniting theoretical and experimental biology with advanced bioengineering and fostering close collaborations with leaders in material science, physics, and chemistry to drive transformative advances in systems biology, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Situated in Basel, Switzerland, at the heart of the BioValley, a tri-national region that hosts 40% of the global life science industry and numerous major pharmaceutical companies, the D-BSSE offers a unique environment for high-impact translational research with unparalleled access to academic and industrial expertise.

Project background

Advancing the Frontiers of Cell-based therapies and Synthetic Biology

Our group applies state-of-the-art synthetic biology principles to engineer human cells and create next-generation cell-based therapies targeting cancer as well as metabolic, neurodegenerative, autoimmune and infectious diseases. Leveraging innovative platforms such as novel biosensors, gene switches, genetic closed-loop circuits, and chemical structures that interface with and actuate cellular activities, we design programmable cellular implants and devices for therapeutic applications. By integrating fundamental discoveries with translational development, we aim to shape the future of biomedical innovation.

Job description

• Postdoctoral projects will combine molecular engineering, cell programming, and chemical–biological interfacing to engineer human cells using synthetic gene circuits and biosensing platforms, develop novel biosensing systems for real-time monitoring of cellular states, create genetic architectures for precise therapeutic protein regulation, and translate these research advances into programmable cellular implant prototypes

• Projects will be highly interdisciplinary, fostering close collaboration with molecular biologists, bioengineers, and clinical researchers to accelerate translation into clinically relevant therapies

Profile

• We are seeking highly motivated applicants eager to bridge basic and translational research in cell biology and synthetic biology

• Candidates should have strong skills in molecular and cell biology techniques, including cultivation and engineering of primary human cells and mammalian cell lines, Experience with in vivo techniques, as well as completion of an accredited course in laboratory animal science (FELASA / LTK or equivalent), would be an asset

• We welcome applicants with a strong publication record and the ambition to pursue a career in academia, industrial R&D, or biotechnology entrepreneurship

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity

Postdoc Posizione per Biologia Sintetica - Terapie ispirate 100%, Basilea, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Un ambiente di ricerca di classe mondiale al Nexus di biologia, ingegneria e scienze fisiche Il gruppo Biotecnologia e Bioingegneria guidato dal Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger presso il Dipartimento di Scienze e Ingegneria dei Biosistemi (D-BSSE) dell'ETH di Zurigo a Basilea invita candidati eccezionali a candidarsi per una posizione post-dottorale in progetti pionieristici che sviluppano terapie umane di ispirazione biologica sintetica. Il D-BSSE è il primo reparto di ricerca veramente interdisciplinare, unendo biologia teorica e sperimentale con bioingegneria avanzata e promuovendo strette collaborazioni con leader nella scienza materiale, nella fisica e nella chimica per guidare i progressi trasformativi nella biologia dei sistemi, nella biotecnologia e nella biologia sintetica. Situato a Basilea, in Svizzera, nel cuore della BioValley, una regione trinazionale che ospita il 40% dell'industria della scienza della vita globale e numerose importanti aziende farmaceutiche, il D-BSSE offre un ambiente unico per la ricerca traduttiva ad alto impatto con un accesso senza precedenti alle competenze accademiche e industriali. Sfondo del progetto Promuovere le Frontiere di Terapie a base cellulare e Biologia sintetica Il nostro gruppo applica principi di biologia sintetica all'avanguardia per l'ingegneria delle cellule umane e creare terapie cellulari di nuova generazione che mirano al cancro, così come le malattie metaboliche, neurodegenerative, autoimmuni e infettive. Sfruttando piattaforme innovative come i nuovi biosensori, gli interruttori genici, i circuiti geneticamente chiusi e le strutture chimiche che interfacciano e attuano le attività cellulari, progettiamo impianti cellulari programmabili e dispositivi per applicazioni terapeutiche. Integrando scoperte fondamentali con lo sviluppo traduttivo, ci proponiamo di plasmare il futuro dell'innovazione biomedica. Descrizione del lavoro
• I progetti postdoctoral combinano ingegneria molecolare, programmazione cellulare e interfacciamento chimico-biologico per l'ingegneria delle cellule umane utilizzando circuiti genetici sintetici e piattaforme di biosensazione, sviluppare nuovi sistemi di biosensazione per il monitoraggio in tempo reale degli stati cellulari, creare architetture genetiche per una regolazione accurata delle proteine terapeutiche, e tradurre questi progressi di ricerca in prototipi di impianto cellulare programmabili
• I progetti saranno altamente interdisciplinari, promuovendo una stretta collaborazione con biologi molecolari, bioingegneria e ricercatori clinici per accelerare la traduzione in terapie clinicamente rilevanti Profilo
• Stiamo cercando candidati altamente motivati desiderosi di colmare la ricerca di base e di traduzione in biologia cellulare e biologia sintetica
• I candidati dovrebbero avere forti competenze nelle tecniche di biologia molecolare e cellulare, tra cui la coltivazione e l'ingegneria delle cellule umane primarie e delle linee cellulari dei mammiferi, Esperienza con tecniche in vivo, nonché il completamento di un corso accreditato in scienza animale di laboratorio (FELASA / LTK o equivalente), sarebbe un bene
• Accogliamo favorevolmente i candidati con un forte record di pubblicazione e l'ambizione di perseguire una carriera in accademia, R&D industriale, o imprenditore di biotecnologia Luogo di lavoro Luogo di lavoro Offriamo
• Il tuo lavoro con impatto: Diventa parte dell'ETH di Zurigo, che non solo supporta lo sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce attivamente al cambiamento positivo nella società
• Siamo attivamente impegnati in un'università sostenibile e neutrale dal clima
• Puoi aspettarti numerosi vantaggi, come i biglietti per la stagione dei trasporti pubblici e la condivisione delle auto, una vasta gamma di sport offerti dall'ASVZ , dall'assistenza all'infanzia e dalle interessanti prestazioni pensionistiche chevron right Lavoro, insegnamento e ricerca presso l'ETH di Zurigo Apprezziamo la diversità e la sostenibilità In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza di opportunità, la diversità di valore e nutrire un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui i diritti e la dignità di tutto il nostro staff e gli studenti sono rispettati. Visita le nostre pari opportunità e diversità

jobs.description:
PhD Position in Advanced Bioelectronic & Electrical Conversion Research

100%, Basel, fixed-term

print
Drucken

A World-Class Research Environment at the Nexus of Biology, Engineering, and Physical Sciences

The Biotechnology and Bioengineering group led by Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger at the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) of ETH Zurich in Basel invites exceptional candidates to apply for a PhD position in pioneering projects at the intersection of synthetic biology, nanotechnology, and bioelectronics .

The D-BSSE is ETH Zurich's first truly interdisciplinary research department uniting theoretical and experimental biology with advanced bioengineering and fostering close collaborations with leaders in materials science, physics, and chemistry to drive transformative advances in systems biology, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Situated in Basel, Switzerland, at the heart of the BioValley , a tri-national region that hosts 40% of the global life sciences industry and numerous major pharmaceutical companies, the D-BSSE offers a unique environment for high-impact translational research with unparalleled access to academic and industrial expertise.

Project background

Advancing the Frontiers of Bioelectronics and Synthetic Biology

Our group integrates state-of-the-art synthetic biology with advanced nanotechnology, and electrogenetic interfaces to engineer human cells for next generation bioelectronic medicine, designing programmable cells that respond to electrical, electromagnetic, acoustic and biochemical cues to achieve wireless, real-time control of therapeutic protein expression and metabolic regulation. Leveraging innovative platforms such as direct-current-actuated regulation , electromagnetic programming of wireless expression , and closed-loop systems , we aim to translate these technologies into clinically relevant, minimally invasive therapies for cancer, as well as metabolic, neurodegenerative, autoimmune, and infectious diseases.

Job description

• PhD projects will combine catalyst engineering, computational simulation, bioelectrode device fabrication, and electrical engineering to develop bioelectronic interfaces enabling closed-loop programming of cellular behaviour and real-time monitoring of metabolic activity

• There will also be opportunities to design novel bioelectronic implants and develop specialized control software

Profile

• We are seeking highly motivated applicants with a background in physics, material science, or chemistry

• Ideally with expertise in bioelectronics or software simulations, or a strong willingness to acquire it, alongside solid knowledge of electrochemistry and materials chemistry

• Candidates should be eager to collaborate closely with molecular biologists and bioengineers and demonstrate a strong academic record with the ambition to pursue a career in industrial R&D, or entrepreneurship

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. PhD Posizione nella Ricerca avanzata di Bioelettronica e conversione elettrica 100%, Basilea, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Un ambiente di ricerca di classe mondiale al Nexus di biologia, ingegneria e scienze fisiche Il gruppo Biotecnologia e Bioingegneria guidato dal Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger presso il Dipartimento di Scienze e Ingegneria dei Biosistemi (D-BSSE) dell'ETH di Zurigo a Basilea invita candidati eccezionali a richiedere una posizione di dottorato in progetti pionieristici all'incrocio di biologia sintetica, nanotecnologia e bioelettronica. Il D-BSSE è il primo dipartimento di ricerca veramente interdisciplinare dell'ETH di Zurigo che unisce biologia teorica e sperimentale con una bioingegneria avanzata e promuove una stretta collaborazione con i leader nella scienza dei materiali, nella fisica e nella chimica per guidare i progressi trasformativi nella biologia dei sistemi, nella biotecnologia e nella biologia sintetica. Situato a Basilea, in Svizzera, nel cuore della BioValley, una regione trinazionale che ospita il 40% dell'industria globale delle scienze della vita e numerose importanti aziende farmaceutiche, il D-BSSE offre un ambiente unico per la ricerca traduttiva ad alto impatto con un accesso senza precedenti alle competenze accademiche e industriali. Sfondo del progetto Promuovere le frontiere della bioelettronica e della biologia sintetica Il nostro gruppo integra la biologia sintetica all'avanguardia con le nanotecnologie avanzate e le interfacce elettrogenetiche per l'ingegneria delle cellule umane per la medicina bioelettronica di nuova generazione, progettando cellule programmabili che rispondono a segnali elettrici, elettromagnetici, acustici e biochimici per ottenere il controllo wireless, in tempo reale dell'espressione proteica terapeutica e della regolazione metabolica. Sfruttando piattaforme innovative come la regolazione a corrente diretta , la programmazione elettromagnetica dell'espressione wireless e i sistemi a ciclo chiuso, intendiamo tradurre queste tecnologie in terapie clinicamente rilevanti, minimamente invasive per il cancro, così come le malattie metaboliche, neurodegenerative, autoimmuni e infettive. • Ci saranno anche opportunità di progettare nuovi impianti bioelettronici e sviluppare software di controllo specializzato Profilo

Le D-BSSE est le premier département de recherche véritablement interdisciplinaire de Zurich à unir la biologie théorique et expérimentale à la bioingénierie avancée et à favoriser des collaborations étroites avec des leaders en science des matériaux, en physique et en chimie pour stimuler les avancées transformatrices en biologie des systèmes, en biotechnologie et en biologie synthétique. Situé à Bâle, en Suisse, au cœur de la BioValley , une région trinationale qui accueille 40% de l'industrie mondiale des sciences de la vie et de nombreuses grandes sociétés pharmaceutiques, le D-BSSE offre un environnement unique pour la recherche translationnelle à haut impact avec un accès inégalé à l'expertise académique et industrielle. Contexte du projet Faire progresser les frontières de la bioélectronique et de la biologie synthétique Notre groupe intègre une biologie synthétique de pointe avec des nanotechnologies avancées et des interfaces électrogénétiques pour concevoir des cellules humaines pour la médecine bioélectronique de prochaine génération, en concevant des cellules programmables qui répondent aux signaux électriques, électromagnétiques, acoustiques et biochimiques pour atteindre un contrôle sans fil en temps réel de l'expression thérapeutique des protéines et de la régulation métabolique. jobs.description:
PhD position in light controlled variable stiffness for soft robotics

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated PhD student for the topic of light programmable stiffness for reconfigurable soft devices and robots. This 4-year PhD position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant .

Project background

The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. As a parallel to the thriving fields of soft devices and robots controlled by electrical signals, soft optics is emerging as a new platform that uses the modulation of light in soft matter to encode multifunctionalities in the optical path.

The first part of this project will center around developing light-stimulated stiffness programming methods that surpass the performance of current variable stiffness benchmarks. The second part will focus on the application of this principle in several soft device/robot systems to demonstrate reconfigurability and multifunctionality for real-world tasks.

Job description

• Creation of methods to program material stiffness in-situ with light. Goals: high stiffness contrast (rigid-soft), fast transition (

This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Profile

• MS degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields from a top-notch university

• Candidates with strong track records of research in soft robotics, smart materials, or related fields (especially with experience of working on variable stiffness materials and robots) are highly welcomed to apply

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and a passion for interdisciplinary research

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

• Strong connections with academic, industrial, and clinical partners in materials science, robotics, and healthcare.

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your application with the following documents as a single PDF:

• A cover letter

• CV

• Publication list, if any, with a few sentences highlighting representative works

• Contact details of two referees

• Transcripts of academic records

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the positions are filled. The preferred start date is as soon as possible in the third quarter of 2026 . Further information should be directed to Prof. Hedan Bai at hedan.bai@mat.ethz.ch . All applications should be submitted through this portal, and applications through emails may not be considered due to the high volume.

jobs.description:
Postdoc position in soft optical fiber-based artificial muscle for biomedical applications

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated postdoc for the topic of soft optical fiber-based artificial muscle for biomedical applications . This position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant .

Project background

The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. As a parallel to the thriving fields of soft devices and robots controlled by electrical signals, soft optics is emerging as a new platform that uses the modulation of light in soft matter to encode multifunctionalities in the optical path.

The focus of this project is to create biocompatible, high performance soft actuators multiplexed by light, all integrated on a miniature fiber, delivering advanced robotic and biomedical functions as minimally invasive surgical tools and implantable devices.

Job description

• Develop biocompatible soft actuators controlled by light with performance matching benchmarked soft robotic actuators

• Design and microfabrication of soft optical fibers densely distributed with actuators

• Develop actuator multiplexing methods for individual addressability

• Demonstration for advanced robotic functions as minimally invasive surgical tools

• Integration with bioelectronic functions (e.g., sensing) for closed-loop controlled diagnostic and therapeutic functions.

• Demonstration as robotic/biomedical devices for real-world application through collaborations.

• Supervise master/bachelor students

• Teaching assistant for the robotic materials class

Profile

• PhD degree in Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields from a top university.

• Strong research track records in one or more of the following: bioelectronics, soft robotics, flexible electronics, fiber-based devices, functional materials, wearable systems, or biomedical devices.

• Hands-on experience in device design, prototyping, experimental characterization, and TRL 3-5 demonstrations.

• Knowledge of biomedical soft materials, textile/fiber processing, microfabrication, or soft actuators is highly desirable

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and a passion for interdisciplinary research.

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

• Strong connections with academic, industrial, and clinical partners in materials science, robotics, and healthcare.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your application with the following documents as a single PDF:

• A cover letter

• CV

• Publication list with a few sentences highlighting representative works

• Contact details of two referees

• Optional: transcripts of academic records

The preferred start date is as soon as possible in the third quarter of 2026 .

Questa posizione è finanziata dal nostro ERC Start Grant . Sfondo del progetto L'introduzione di fibre ottiche negli anni '70 ha rivoluzionato l'industria delle telecomunicazioni sulla sostituzione dei fili di rame e ha svolto un ruolo importante nell'avvento dell'età dell'informazione - Un cavo in fibra ottica ad alta larghezza di banda può sostituire migliaia di collegamenti elettrici per trasmettere la stessa quantità di informazioni. L'obiettivo di questo progetto è quello di creare attuatori morbidi biocompatibili, ad alte prestazioni multiplexed dalla luce, tutti integrati su una fibra in miniatura, offrendo funzioni robotiche e biomediche avanzate come strumenti chirurgici minimamente invasivi e dispositivi impiantabili. • Esperienza pratica nella progettazione dei dispositivi, nella prototipazione, nella caratterizzazione sperimentale e nelle dimostrazioni TRL 3-5.

jobs.description:
Postdoc position in light multiplexed, fiber-based artificial sensorimotor network

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Robotic Materials group is looking for a highly motivated postdoc for the topic of light multiplexed artificial sensorimotor network . This position is funded by our ERC Starting Grant .

Project background

The introduction of fiber optics in the 1970s has revolutionized the telecommunications industry upon the replacement of copper wires and played a major role in the advent of the Information Age - One high bandwidth fiber optic cable can replace thousands of electrical links to transmit the same amount of information. As a parallel to the thriving fields of soft devices and robots controlled by electrical signals, soft optics is emerging as a new platform that uses the modulation of light in soft matter to encode multifunctionalities in the optical path.

The focus of this project is to expand both actuation and sensing capacities with light. The project will create an artificial sensorimotor network with densely distributed actuators and sensors similar to the biological neuromasculature. The first part of the project will develop a single soft optical fiber with distributed multimodal actuators that are also self-sensing. The second part will study grouped behavior of these “muscle bundles” to enable muscle coordination for complex/adaptive/efficient movements.

Job description

• Based on existing light actuators in our group, develop self-sensing methods where the transducer serves both for actuation and sensing, and is feedback controlled with onboard optoelectronics

• Design and microfabrication of a soft optical fiber distributed with such transducers configured for multiple modalities, and enable individual addressability through light multiplexing, based on the group’s expertise

• Demonstrate the single artificial neuromuscular fiber for advanced robotic functions arising from the distributed and multimodal actuators and sensors

• In the second part, create grouped neuromuscular bundles with extremely high functional density approaching orders of magnitude of biology

• Investigate emergent coordinated bundle behavior and motion patterns arising from biologically similar redundancy with collaborations of control and learning

• Demonstrate for advanced robotic functions

• Supervise master/bachelor students

• Teaching assistant for the robotic materials class

This is a full-time position that starts as soon as possible. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Profile

• PhD degree in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering or related fields from a top university

• Strong research track records in one or more of the following: micro robots, soft robotics, fiber-based robots, or related

• Hands-on experience in robot design, prototyping, experimental characterization, and TRL 3-5 demonstration

• Knowledge of reconfigurable/multifunctional microrobots, small-scale soft robotics, feedback controlled soft robotic systems is highly desirable

• Excellent problem-solving abilities and a passion for interdisciplinary research

Workplace

We offer

• A productive working environment with training and guidance from the PI on a regular basis

• Competitive salary according to ETH standards (fully funded, full-time, fixed term position)

• An interdisciplinary, international, and diverse team of talents and a stimulating, vibrant, collaborative group

• Strong connections with academic, industrial, and clinical partners in materials science, robotics, and healthcare

Questa posizione è finanziata dal nostro ERC Start Grant . Sfondo del progetto L'introduzione di fibre ottiche negli anni '70 ha rivoluzionato l'industria delle telecomunicazioni sulla sostituzione dei fili di rame e ha svolto un ruolo importante nell'avvento dell'età dell'informazione - Un cavo in fibra ottica ad alta larghezza di banda può sostituire migliaia di collegamenti elettrici per trasmettere la stessa quantità di informazioni. Parallelamente ai campi fiorenti di dispositivi morbidi e robot controllati da segnali elettrici, l'ottica morbida sta emergendo come una nuova piattaforma che utilizza la modulazione della luce in materia morbida per codificare le multifunzionalità nel percorso ottico. L'obiettivo di questo progetto è di espandere sia le capacità di azionamento che di rilevamento con la luce. Il progetto creerà una rete di sensorimotori artificiali con attuatori e sensori densamente distribuiti simili alla neuromascolatura biologica. La prima parte del progetto svilupperà una singola fibra ottica morbida con attuatori multimodali distribuiti che sono anche auto-sensibilizzanti. La seconda parte studierà il comportamento raggruppato di questi “pacchetti muscolari” per consentire il coordinamento muscolare per movimenti complessi/adaptivi/efficienti. Descrizione del lavoro
• Basato sugli attuatori di luce esistenti nel nostro gruppo, sviluppare metodi di auto-sensazione in cui il trasduttore serve sia per l'azione che per il rilevamento, ed è controllato da feedback con optoelettronica a bordo
• Design e microfabricazione di una fibra ottica morbida distribuita con tali trasduttori configurati per molteplici modalità, e consentire l'individual indirizzabilità attraverso il multiplexing della luce, in base alle competenze del gruppo
• Dimostrare il singolo neuromus artificiale avanzato Nella seconda parte, creare fasci neuromuscolari raggruppati con densità funzionale estremamente elevata avvicinando ordini di grandezza della biologia
• Investigare comportamenti e modelli di movimento coordinati dei fasci emerse derivanti da ridondanza biologicamente simile con collaborazioni di controllo e apprendimento
• Dimostrare funzioni robotiche avanzate
• Supervise master/bachelor studenti

• Conoscenza di microrobots multifunzionali altamente controllati Un team interdisciplinare, internazionale e diversificato di talenti e un gruppo stimolante, vibrante, collaborativo

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral position – Co-evaluating bio-inputs for Smallholder Farmers in Kenya

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Sustainable Agroecosystem group at ETH Zurich is looking for a highly motivated Postdoc for a project on smallholder farmer relevant agroecological innovations in Kenya. The Sustainable Agroecosystem Group focuses on the feedbacks between agroecosystem management options, plant-soil interactions, nutrient cycling, and soil microbiome functioning within a transdisciplinary framework to ensure relevance and viability of the research outcomes for a farmer-led transition to sustainable agriculture.

Project background

A new farmer-based agroecology innovation research initiative (Agroecology Academy - Africa) has been established at ETH Zurich with a parallel base in Western Kenya to contribute with the latest insights into agroecological science. It will investigate easily adoptable solutions to improve the farmers’ situation by enhancing soil fertility, crop productivity, income, farming system resilience and agricultural sustainability in general. It will act as a bridge between research and practice by connecting agricultural stakeholders (i.e. smallholder farmers, extension specialist, food processors, etc.) and academics. Besides delivering excellent research, a strong focus will be on achieving impact on the ground and thus contributing to the smallholder farmers’ livelihood. The initiative's work will focus on three key areas: farmer-centred research, translation of research into action, and knowledge exchange, training and education. To further leverage project outcomes and to scale it to additional regions and communities, universal principles will be identified in order to apply them across the African continent.

Job description

This specific postdoc project is aimed at compiling local farmer knowledge on agroecological practices, emphasizing on locally produced bioinputs (biofertilizers and biopesticides) to increase productivity, not only in the short-term, but also in the long-term.

To this aim, you will:

• Conduct a local farming practices knowledge study for Western Kenya through literature search, surveys with farmers, focus group discussion with smallholder farmers and other food systems actors, interviews with local food system authorities

• Perform a meta-analysis on locally produced bio-inputs (i.e. fertilizer and pesticides) across sub-Saharan Africa

• Rigorous (on-farm) testing of locally sourced bio-inputs (i.e. fertilizer and pesticides) in Western Kenya

Profile

• PhD in agronomy, soil science, crop science or similar

• Experience in interdisciplinary projects to holistically assess the sustainability of agriculture

• Interested and experienced in Agroecology both from a theoretical and practical perspective

• Excellent academic track record. You have a strong background in agroecosystem management research, data compilation, and data analysis techniques and methodologies

• Experience with surveys, focus group discussions, and interviewing is a major plus

• Highly motivated and self-organized

• You will be expected to help us maintain a positive team dynamic and a welcoming work environment

• You should be able to combine strong individual research with teamwork within an interdisciplinary project. You should be open-minded towards research within a transdisciplinary approach

• Be ready for heavy field-work in the tropical sun

• Excellent communication skills in English, both verbally and written

Workplace

We offer

You will work in a highly stimulating environment with state-of-the-art infrastructure measurement and computational facilities. The position provides the opportunity to work within a transdisciplinary environment, allowing for a broadening of perspectives and networks. We offer salaries according to Postdoctoral levels at ETH Zurich as well as other attractive working conditions. The envisaged starting date is 1 July 2026. Th

Oltre a fornire una ricerca eccellente, un forte focus sarà sul raggiungimento dell’impatto sul terreno e contribuire così al sostentamento dei piccoli agricoltori. Il lavoro dell'iniziativa si concentrerà su tre settori chiave: la ricerca contadina, la traduzione della ricerca in azione e lo scambio di conoscenze, la formazione e l'istruzione. Per sfruttare ulteriormente i risultati del progetto e scalarlo ad altre regioni e comunità, i principi universali saranno identificati per applicarli in tutto il continente africano. jobs.description:
PhD position on high-order harmonic generation spectroscopy in noble-gas liquids

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

We are offering a PhD position in attosecond science and strong-field physics at the Laboratory of Physical Chemistry, ETH Zürich. The project focuses on high-order harmonic generation (HHG) in noble-gas liquids, in particular liquid helium. This research aims to explore a new regime of ultrafast electron dynamics in condensed matter and to bridge the gap between gas-phase and liquid-phase HHG. The position offers the opportunity to work at the forefront of attosecond spectroscopy using state-of-the-art ultrafast laser systems and cryogenic technology. This 4-year PhD position is funded by our SNSF grant.

Project background

High-order harmonic generation has become a cornerstone of attosecond science, enabling the observation of electron dynamics on their natural timescales. While HHG is well understood in gases and increasingly explored in solids, its extension to liquids offers intriguing opportunities to study electron scattering and delocalization properties. Noble-gas liquids, and liquid helium in particular, provide a unique platform: they combine the simplicity of atomic systems with the density of condensed matter. Their relatively long electron mean free paths offer access to a regime where strong-field physics can be studied under conditions intermediate between gases and molecular liquids. This project aims to establish HHG spectroscopy in noble liquids, investigate the role of electron scattering and coherence, and explore new phenomena such as HHG in the superfluid phase of helium.

Job description

• Design and perform experiments on high-order harmonic generation in liquid and gas-phase targets

• Develop and operate cryogenic liquid-jet systems for noble-gas liquids

• Implement advanced ultrafast laser techniques (e.g., few-cycle pulses, two-colour fields, CEP stabilization)

• Analyze experimental data to extract information on electron dynamics (cut-off scaling, phase, emission times)

• Contribute to the development of new experimental methods in attosecond spectroscopy

• Present results at international conferences and publish in high-impact journals

Profile

• Master’s degree in physics, physical chemistry, or a closely related field

• Strong interest in ultrafast laser science, attosecond physics, or strong-field phenomena

• Experimental skills and motivation to work on complex laboratory setups

• Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative research team

• Good communication skills in English (spoken and written)

Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: ultrafast optics, nonlinear optics, HHG/strong-field physics, vacuum technology, spectroscopy, or scientific programming (Python, MATLAB).

Workplace

We offer

• A fully funded PhD position at ETH Zürich, one of the world’s leading universities

• Access to state-of-the-art ultrafast laser systems and experimental infrastructure

• A stimulating, international research environment with strong collaborations

• Opportunities to attend international conferences and build a scientific network

• Supervision and training in cutting-edge experimental techniques in attosecond science

• Attractive working conditions and benefits according to ETH Zürich standards

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Il progetto si concentra sulla generazione armonica ad alto ordine (HHG) in liquidi a gas nobile, in particolare elio liquido. Questa ricerca mira a esplorare un nuovo regime di dinamiche elettroni ultraveloci in materia condensata e a colmare il divario tra la fase gassosa e la fase liquida HHG. La posizione offre l'opportunità di lavorare all'avanguardia della spettroscopia dell'attosecondo utilizzando sistemi laser ultraveloci all'avanguardia e tecnologia criogenica. Questa posizione di dottorato di 4 anni è finanziata dalla nostra sovvenzione SNSF. La generazione armonica di alto ordine è diventata una pietra angolare della scienza dell'attosecondo, consentendo l'osservazione delle dinamiche elettrone sulle loro scale temporali naturali. Mentre HHG è ben compresa nei gas e sempre più esplorata nei solidi, la sua estensione ai liquidi offre intriganti opportunità di studiare elettroni spargimento e delocalizzazione proprietà. Il loro elettrone relativamente lungo significa percorsi liberi offrono l'accesso a un regime in cui la fisica del campo forte può essere studiata in condizioni intermedie tra gas e liquidi molecolari. Questo progetto mira a stabilire la spettroscopia HHG in liquidi nobili, indagare il ruolo di spargimento elettrone e coerenza, ed esplorare nuovi fenomeni come HHG nella fase superfluida dell'elio.

Das Projekt konzentriert sich auf die hochrangige harmonische Generation (HHG) in Edelgasflüssigkeiten, insbesondere flüssiges Helium. Diese Forschung zielt darauf ab, ein neues Regime der ultraschnellen Elektronendynamik in Kondensstoffen zu erforschen und den Spalt zwischen Gasphase und Flüssigphase HHG zu überbrücken. Die Position bietet die Möglichkeit, an der Spitze der Attosekundenspektroskopie mit modernsten ultraschnellen Lasersystemen und der kryogenen Technologie zu arbeiten. Diese 4-jährige PhD-Position wird durch unseren SNSF-Zuschuss finanziert. Projekthintergrund Hochrangige harmonische Generation ist zu einem Eckpfeiler der Attosekunden-Wissenschaft geworden, der die Beobachtung der Elektronendynamik auf ihren natürlichen Zeitskala ermöglicht. Während HHG in Gasen gut verstanden und in Feststoffen zunehmend erforscht wird, bietet seine Ausdehnung auf Flüssigkeiten faszinierende Möglichkeiten, Elektronenstreu- und Delokalisierungseigenschaften zu untersuchen. Edelgasflüssigkeiten und insbesondere flüssiges Helium bieten eine einzigartige Plattform: Sie kombinieren die Einfachheit atomarer Systeme mit der Dichte von Kondensstoffen. Ihre relativ langen elektronenmittleren freien Wege bieten Zugang zu einem Regime, in dem die Feldphysik unter Zwischenbedingungen zwischen Gasen und molekularen Flüssigkeiten untersucht werden kann. Dieses Projekt zielt darauf ab, HHG-Spektroskopie in edlen Flüssigkeiten zu etablieren, die Rolle der Elektronenstreuung und Kohärenz zu untersuchen und neue Phänomene wie HHG in der suprafluiden Phase des Heliums zu erforschen.

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD position sur la spectroscopie de génération harmonique de haut niveau dans les liquides à gaz noble 100%, Zurich, tirage à terme fixe Drucken Nous offrons un poste de doctorat en science attoseconde et physique de terrain fort au Laboratoire de chimie physique, ETH Zürich. Le projet met l'accent sur la génération harmonique à haut ordre (HHG) dans les liquides à gaz nobles, en particulier l'hélium liquide. Cette recherche vise à explorer un nouveau régime de dynamique des électrons ultrarapides dans la matière condensée et à combler l'écart entre la phase gazeuse et la phase liquide HHG. La position offre la possibilité de travailler à l'avant-garde de la spectroscopie attoseconde à l'aide de systèmes laser ultrarapides de pointe et de technologie cryogénique. Ce poste de doctorat de 4 ans est financé par notre subvention SNSF. Contexte du projet La génération harmonique de haut niveau est devenue une pierre angulaire de la science de l'attoseconde, permettant l'observation de la dynamique électronique sur leurs échelles de temps naturelles. Bien que le HHG soit bien compris dans les gaz et de plus en plus exploré dans les solides, son extension aux liquides offre des possibilités intrigantes d'étudier les propriétés de diffusion et de délocalisation des électrons. Les liquides à gaz noble, et l'hélium liquide en particulier, constituent une plateforme unique : ils combinent la simplicité des systèmes atomiques avec la densité de la matière condensée. Leurs voies libres moyennes d'électrons relativement longues donnent accès à un régime où la physique des champs forts peut être étudiée dans des conditions intermédiaires entre gaz et liquides moléculaires. Ce projet vise à établir la spectroscopie HHG dans les liquides nobles, à étudier le rôle de la diffusion et de la cohérence des électrons et à explorer de nouveaux phénomènes tels que HHG dans la phase superfluide de l'hélium. Description de travail
• Concevoir et réaliser des expériences sur la génération harmonique à haut niveau dans des cibles en phase liquide et en phase gazeuse
• Développer et exploiter des systèmes cryogéniques à jet liquide pour des liquides à gaz nobles
• Mettre en oeuvre des techniques laser ultrarapides avancées (p. ex. impulsions à peu de cycles, champs bicolores, stabilisation du CEP)
• Analyser des données expérimentales pour extraire des informations sur la dynamique des électrons (échelle de coupure, phase, temps d'émission)
• Contribuer au développement de nouvelles méthodes expérimentales en spectroscopie attoseconde
• Présenter les résultats lors de conférences internationales et publier dans des revues à grand impact Profil
• Maîtrise en physique, chimie physique ou domaine étroitement lié
• Fort intérêt pour la science laser ultrarapide, en physique attoseconde ou en phénomènes à champ fort

jobs.description:
Architekt:in oder Bauingenieur:in mit Fokus Nachhaltigkeit Living Lab HIL (m/w/d)

100%, Zürich, befristet

print
Drucken

Die ETH Zürich startet ein pionierhaftes Forschungsprojekt mit direktem Bezug zur Baupraxis. Das HIL-Gebäude auf dem Campus Hönggerberg wird zu einem Living Lab transformiert. Der sanierungsbedürftige Bau wird umgebaut und erweitert.

Professuren der Departemente Architektur (D-ARCH) sowie Bau, Umwelt und Geomatik (D-BAUG) erforschen und planen in den kommenden Jahren die Sanierung des Gebäudes HIL im Sinne des zirkulären Bauens. Ziel ist es, nachhaltiges Entwerfen und Bauen im Bestand weiterzuentwickeln und exemplarisch an einem realen Planungs- und Bauprojekt zu demonstrieren.

Für die Entwicklung von Strategien, Auswertungen in Anlehnung methodischer Ansätze sowie die übergeordnete Koordination der Nachhaltigkeitsplanung im Architekturprojekt suchen wir ab 1. Juli 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung eine engagierte und vielseitige Architektin, Architekten oder Bauingenieurin, Bauingenieur mit Schwerpunkt Nachhaltigkeit.

Sie arbeiten im interdisziplinären Team des Living Lab HIL und stehen in engem Austausch mit verschiedenen Professuren. Dabei tragen Sie dazu bei, innovative Ansätze aus Forschung und Praxis in der nachhaltigen Gebäudeentwicklung zu verbinden und weiterzuentwickeln.

Stellenbeschreibung

Nebst den Entwicklungs- und Planungsaufgaben im Team des Living Lab HIL arbeiten Sie mit Fokus auf Nachhaltigkeitsthemen an folgenden Aufgaben:

• Entwicklung und Koordination von Nachhaltigkeitsstrategien

• Datenintegration von ökologischen und energetischen Analysen im Kontext des digitalen Gebäudemodells

• Steuerung und Abstimmung von Nachhaltigkeitszielen mit interdisziplinären Planungsteams

• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit beteiligten Professuren im Rahmen des Living Lab HIL

• Integration innovativer Forschungsansätze in konkrete Planungsprozesse

• Entwicklung von Konzepten zu klimabewusstem Bauen, Materialstrategien und Ressourceneffizienz

• Begleitung der Projektentwicklung in der gesamten Planungsphase

• Erstellung von Entscheidungsgrundlagen, Berichten und Präsentationen

• Monitoring, Evaluation und Weiterentwicklung der Nachhaltigkeitsziele

• Austausch mit externen Fachplanern, Behörden und Zertifizierungsstellen

Profil

• Abgeschlossenes Studium in Architektur (ETH/FH oder vergleichbar)

• Berufserfahrung von Vorteil, idealerweise im Hochschul- oder Forschungsumfeld

• Kenntnisse der Schweizer Bauvorschriften sowie der SIA-Normen

• Kenntnisse der Zertifizierungen und Standards

• Selbständige, strukturierte und verantwortungsbewusste Arbeitsweise

• Kommunikationsstärke, Flexibilität und lösungsorientiertes Denken

• Gute Kenntnisse mit 3D-CAD / BIM

• Erfahrung mit Rhino, Grasshopper erwünscht

• Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sowie gute Englischkenntnisse

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

Abwechslungsreiche Projektbearbeitung in einem inspirierenden Umfeld an der Schnittstelle von Architektur, Forschung und Praxis.

Ihr Arbeitsort ist im neuen Projektbüro im HIL-Gebäude auf dem ETH Campus Hönggerberg. Ihre Position ist dem Projektteam im Departement Architektur angegliedert, welches die Projektinitiative lanciert hat und leitet. Wir bieten attraktive Arbeitsbedingungen in einem dynamischen und innovativen internationalen Umfeld. Sie arbeiten eigenverantwortlich und in ständigem kollegialem Austausch mit unserem Team und einer Vielfalt an Partner:innen und Anspruchsgruppen.

chevron_right
Arbeiten, Lehren und Forschen an der ETH Zürich

Diversität und Nachhaltigkeit sind uns wichtig

Im Einklang mit unseren Werten unterstützt die ETH Zürich eine inklusive Kultur. Wir fördern Chancengleichheit, schätzen Vielfalt und pflegen ein Arbeits- und Lernumfeld, in dem die Rechte und die Würde aller Mitarbeitenden und Studierenden respektiert werden. Auf unserer W

jobs.description:
PhD Researcher - tenoexo

100%, Singapore, fixed-term

Drucken

The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions.

Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) .

The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems.

Project background

Stroke remains a leading cause of disability worldwide. While improved early stroke response has reduced mortality, it has also led to a growing population of stroke survivors, increasing the demand for long-term rehabilitation and placing significant clinical and economic burden on healthcare systems. The current neurorehabilitation model relies heavily on resource-intensive, therapist-led care to meet the growing demand, underscoring the need for scalable, cost-effective solutions that extend into home settings. To address this gap the first phase of the Future Health Technologies Programme (FHT1) at the Singapore-ETH Centre (SEC) (https://fht.ethz.ch) developed and piloted innovative upper limb rehabilitation technologies and evaluated them in a clinical context, both in the hospital and at the home of post-stroke subjects. Building on this progress, FHT2 seeks to scale up these technologies and conduct more extensive clinical evaluation to promote integration of technology-based clinic-to-home rehabilitation into Singapore’s healthcare system.

Specifically, one of our projects focuses on the technical development and clinical validation of a soft robotic hand orthosis to enhance upper limb rehabilitation sessions in the clinic and allow for additional task-oriented training at home. The project will build on the RELab tenoexo technology, a soft exoskeleton that was developed at ETH Zurich and refined during FHT1. As main features, RELab tenoexo can support grasping, is fully tailorable to the hand of the user, is fully wearable and weighs less than 300g. A proof-of-concept trial demonstrated preliminary feasibility and safety of using RELab tenoexo in chronic stroke.

Within this PhD project, the objective will be to further develop and evaluate RELab tenoexo and demonstrate that a soft hand exoskeleton can be a cost-efficient way to increase therapy dose at home and improve upper limb function of post-stroke subjects. To achieve this goal, we will (i) improve and optimize several key design features of RELab tenoexo,(ii) combine RELab tenoexo with behavioural interventions delivered by a motivational AI chatbot (developed by another PhD student) to enhance motivation to engage in therapy at home, and (iii) evaluate long-term adherence to use at home, functional improvements, movement quality metrics, as well as required resources/costs in the context of a proof of value clinical trial.

jobs.description:
PhD Researcher - PDTx

100%, Singapore, fixed-term

Drucken

The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions.

Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) .

The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems.

Project background

Stroke remains a leading cause of disability worldwide. While improved early stroke response has reduced mortality, it has also led to a growing population of stroke survivors, increasing the demand for long-term rehabilitation and placing significant clinical and economic burden on healthcare systems. The current neurorehabilitation model relies heavily on resource-intensive, therapist-led care to meet the growing demand, underscoring the need for scalable, cost-effective solutions that extend into home settings. To address this gap, the first phase of the Future Health Technologies Programme (FHT1) at the Singapore-ETH Centre (SEC) (https://fht.ethz.ch)developed and piloted innovative upper limb rehabilitation technologies and evaluated them in a clinical context, both in the hospital and at the home of post-stroke subjects. Building on this progress, FHT2 seeks to scale up these technologies and conduct more extensive clinical evaluation to promote integration of technology-based clinic-to-home rehabilitation into Singapore’s healthcare system.

Specifically, one of our projects focuses on the development of a soft robotic hand orthosis to enhance upper limb rehabilitation sessions in the clinic and allow for additional task-oriented training at home. A first version of the soft exoskeleton has been developed within FHT1 and a proof-of-concept trial demonstrated preliminary feasibility, with post-stroke subjects using the rehabilitation device at home. However, adherence to home rehabilitation without therapist supervision and support can be challenging, ultimately affecting therapy dose. In this project, we will complement the exoskeleton with an AI-based digital health intervention, specifically an LLM-based conversational agent that will deliver support via a companion mobile app. The app will serve as both the user interface for daily interaction and support and a digital platform for data collection, remote monitoring, and telerehabilitation.

Within this PhD project, the objective will be to (i) derive the key requirements for the design of the digital platform and the LLM-based conversational agent (together with the input from end-users and building on pre-existing prototypes); (ii) iteratively develop the app and key interactive features (e.g., AI-based conversational agent, motivational interviewing, etc.) including their validation; (iii) interface the app with the soft hand exoskeleton technology (developed by another PhD student) (data transfer, data interpretation, feedback provision); and (iv) evaluate its impact on long-term adherence to a technology-supported rehabilitation intervention at home in the context of a 6-week proof of value clinical trial.

jobs.description:
Software Engineer

100%, Singapore, fixed-term

Drucken

The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions.

Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) .

The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems.

Project background

FHT2 is an NRF-CREATE programme co-funded by the National Research Foundation (NRF), ETH Zurich, and NHG-NTU, and represents the second phase of the FHT initiative launched in 2020. The programme brings together psychologists, neuroscientists, computer scientists, engineers and clinicians to develop next-generation digital health solutions.

The Software Engineer will join the Monitoring and Supporting Cognitive Health in the Community project. This project focuses on the development and deployment of an AI-powered mobile platform designed to assess, monitor, and support cognitive health during real-world navigation. The platform integrates cognitive and navigation assessments, smartphone sensor data, and AI-driven conversational agents.

A central component of the project is the development of a robust, scalable, and user-friendly mobile application ecosystem across iOS, Android, and web platforms. The Software Engineer will play a key role in building and maintaining this system, enabling real-time interaction, data collection, and AI-driven feedback. The project is closely aligned with Healthier SG and the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, with clear pathways for real-world deployment in Singapore.

Job description

The successful candidate will be responsible for the design, development, and maintenance of a cross-platform mobile and web application for cognitive health monitoring and support.

Working within a highly multidisciplinary team across the Singapore-ETH Centre (SEC), NUS, and NTU, the Software Engineer will collaborate closely with researchers, designers, and clinicians to translate research prototypes into reliable and scalable software systems.

Key responsibilities include developing and maintaining mobile applications for iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin), as well as contributing to the web-based frontend (ReactJS) and backend services (NodeJS). The candidate will implement features enabling user interaction with AI-driven conversational agents, integrate APIs and sensor data pipelines, and ensure smooth communication between frontend and backend systems.

The role also involves optimizing app performance, ensuring data security and privacy, and supporting deployment and testing in real-world environments. The Software Engineer will contribute to system architecture decisions and help establish best practices for scalable and maintainable software development.

Given the translational nature of the project, the position offers the opportunity to work on impactful real-world applications at the intersection of AI, mobile computing, and digital health.

A central component of the project is the development of a robust, scalable, and user-friendly mobile application ecosystem across iOS, Android, and web platforms. The Software Engineer will play a key role in building and maintaining this system, enabling real-time interaction, data collection, and AI-driven feedback. The project is closely aligned with Healthier SG and the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, with clear pathways for real-world deployment in Singapore.

jobs.description:
Leitung Lehrlabor Physiklaboranten:innen im D-PHYS (m/w/d)

80%-100%, Zürich, unbefristet

print
Drucken

Die ETH Zürich ist der Studien-, Forschungs- und Arbeitsplatz von rund 30’000 Menschen aus über 120 Ländern. Das Departement Physik (D-PHYS) verfolgt eine vielfältige Forschungsagenda und ein breites Unterrichtsprogramm, von der Erforschung von Grundprinzipien der Natur bis zu innovativen Technologien für die Gesellschaft. Ein Grossteil der rund 1'500 Bachelor-, Master- und PhD-Studierenden, Postdocs und Professoren, Lernenden sowie wissenschaftlichen und Service-Mitarbeitenden ist dabei auf die ein oder andere Art in die Forschung involviert.

Auch im Bereich der beruflichen Grundbildung engagiert sich die ETH Zürich: Insgesamt werden bis zu 200 Lernende ausgebildet, davon rund 65 im Departement Physik in vier verschiedenen Berufsrichtungen . Diese arbeiten eng zusammen und unterstützen sich gegenseitig in der Ausbildung der Lernenden.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams der Berufsbildung in den Technischen Betrieben suchen wir per 1. Juni 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung eine Leitung Lehrlabor Physiklaboranten:innen.

Stellenbeschreibung

In dieser Funktion sind Sie verantwortlich für die Organisation, den Betrieb und die Weiterentwicklung des Lehrlabors sowie der Berufsbildung der Physiklaborant:innen an der ETH Zürich. Zudem führen Sie die zweite Ausbildungsperson.

Sie führen die Grundbildung während der ersten beiden Lehrjahre in Form interner Kurse durch, entwickeln Ausbildungsinhalte / Module weiter und planen die Rotationsplätze der Lehrjahre drei und vier. Dabei begleiten Sie als zentrale Ansprechperson die Lernenden über die gesamte Lehrzeit hinweg, fördern die Lernenden fachlich, methodisch sowie in ihrer Sozial‑ und Selbstkompetenz und sorgen für einen reibungslosen Übergang sowie eine erfolgreiche betriebliche Ausbildung.

Darüber hinaus sind Sie für die Durchführung von Schnupperlehren zuständig sowie für die Rekrutierung zukünftiger Lernender. Sie sind Ansprechperson für die Berufsbildenden auf den Rotationsplätzen, unterstützen und befähigen sie in der Begleitung der Lernenden und bei der Abnahme der praktischen Lehrabschlussprüfungen. Die Zusammenarbeit mit dem zentralen Berufsbildungsteam bildet einen weiteren Bestandteil Ihrer Tätigkeit. Bei Projekten übernehmen Sie eine aktive Rolle, um eine moderne Art der Berufsbildung umzusetzen und weiterzuentwickeln.

Profil

Idealerweise bringen Sie folgende Qualifikationen mit:

• Begeisterung für Physik und deren praktische Anwendung

• Abgeschlossene berufliche Grundausbildung als Physiklaborant:in, Automatiker:in oder Elektroniker:in EFZ

• Alternativ eine andere technische Grundausbildung EFZ mit anschliessender Weiterbildung beispielsweise in den Bereichen Physik, Messtechnik, Konstruktion, Elektronik, oder ein fachlich passendes Studium (HF, FH oder Universitär)

• Freude an der Arbeit mit Jugendlichen und bereits erste Erfahrung in der Lernendenbetreuung

• 10 Jahre Arbeitserfahrung

• Bereitschaft zur Absolvierung der Weiterbildung SVEB 1, eidg. Fachausweis Ausbildner:in oder ein bereits abgeschlossener entsprechender Ausbildungsnachweis

• Freude an der Konzeptionierung und Weiterentwicklung der Ausbildungsinhalte

• Engagement für bereichsübergreifende Zusammenarbeit in der Berufsbildung, sowohl innerhalb der ETH als auch ausserhalb

• Kommunikationsstärke auf verschiedenen Ebenen sowie eine strukturierte und organisierte Arbeitsweise

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

• Gestaltungsspielraum bei der Umsetzung und der Weiterentwicklung der Physiklaboranten Ausbildung

• Vielfältige interne Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten mittels Kursen oder dem Lifelong Learning Hub , sowie Unterstützung bei externen Weiterbildungen

• Ein super Arbeitsumfeld auf dem Campus Höngg

chevron ha lasciato Panoramica chevron ha lasciato Head of Physics Laboratories:in D-PHYS (m/w/d) 80%-100%, Zurigo, stampa illimitata Stampa ETH Zurich è lo studio, la ricerca e il posto di lavoro di circa 30’000 persone da oltre 120 paesi. Il Dipartimento di Fisica (D-PHYS) persegue un programma di ricerca diversificato e un ampio programma educativo, dalla ricerca di principi fondamentali della natura alle tecnologie innovative per la società. Una gran parte dei circa 1.500 studenti di laurea, master e PhD, postdoc e professori, studenti e dipendenti scientifici e di servizio è coinvolta nella ricerca in un modo o nell'altro. L'ETH Zurigo è attiva anche nel campo della formazione professionale di base: fino a 200 studenti sono formati in totale, tra cui circa 65 nel Dipartimento di Fisica in quattro professioni diverse. Questi lavori si uniscono e si sostengono a vicenda nella formazione degli studenti. Al fine di rafforzare il nostro team di formazione professionale nelle aziende tecniche, stiamo guardando 1. Giugno 2026 o d'accordo un direttore del Laboratorio di Fisica: dentro. In questa funzione è responsabile per l'organizzazione, il funzionamento e l'ulteriore sviluppo del laboratorio didattico e la formazione professionale del laboratorio di fisica:innen an der ETH Zurich. Potrai anche guidare la seconda persona di allenamento. Essi svolgono un'istruzione di base durante i primi due anni di insegnamento sotto forma di corsi interni, sviluppano contenuti di formazione / moduli e pianificano le posizioni di rotazione degli anni di insegnamento tre e quattro. Come persona di contatto centrale, accompagni gli studenti durante tutto il periodo di insegnamento, promuovi gli studenti professionalmente, metodicamente e nella loro social e auto-competenza e garantisci una transizione regolare e una formazione operativa di successo. Inoltre, siete responsabili per l'attuazione degli insegnamenti del ciuccio e per il reclutamento di futuri studenti. Essi sono la persona di contatto per l'istruzione e la formazione professionale presso i centri di rotazione, di sostegno e di consentire loro di sostenere gli studenti e di accettare gli esami pratici. La cooperazione con il gruppo centrale di formazione professionale costituisce un'altra parte della vostra attività. Per i progetti, si svolge un ruolo attivo nell'attuazione e nello sviluppo di un moderno tipo di formazione professionale.
• Formazione professionale e formazione professionale

chevron left Overview chevron left Head of Physics Laboratories:in D-PHYS (m/w/d) 80%-100%, Zurich, unlimited print Print ETH Zurich is the study, research and workplace of around 30’000 people from over 120 countries. The Department of Physics (D-PHYS) pursues a diverse research agenda and a broad educational programme, from researching basic principles of nature to innovative technologies for society. A large part of the approximately 1,500 bachelor, master and PhD students, postdocs and professors, learners as well as scientific and service employees is involved in research in one way or another. ETH Zurich is also active in the field of basic vocational training: up to 200 learners are trained in total, including around 65 in the Department of Physics in four different professions. These work closely together and support each other in the training of learners. In order to strengthen our team of vocational training in the technical companies, we are looking at 1. June 2026 or by agreement a director of the Physics Laboratory:inside. In this function you are responsible for the organization, operation and further development of the teaching laboratory and the vocational training of the physics laboratory:innen an der ETH Zurich. You will also lead the second training person. They carry out basic education during the first two years of teaching in the form of internal courses, develop training contents/modules and plan the rotation positions of the teaching years three and four. As a central contact person, you accompany the learners throughout the entire teaching period, promote the learners professionally, methodically and in their social and self-competence and ensure a smooth transition as well as successful operational training. In addition, you are responsible for the implementation of pacifier teachings and for the recruitment of future learners. They are the contact person for the vocational education and training at the centres of rotation, support and enable them in the support of the learners and in the acceptance of the practical examinations. Cooperation with the central vocational training team forms another part of your activity. For projects, you play an active role in implementing and developing a modern type of vocational training. Profile Ideally, you will have the following qualifications:
• Enthusiasm for physics and their practical application
• Complete basic vocational training as a physics laboratory:in, automatic:in or electronic:in EFZ
• Alternative a different basic technical training EFZ with subsequent training, for example in the fields of physics, measuring technology, construction, electronics, or a professionally appropriate study (HF, FH or university)
• Pleasure to work with young people and already initial experience
• Pleasure in the design and development of the training content
• Commitment for cross-departmental cooperation in vocational training, both within the ETH and outside
• Communication strength at different levels and a structured and organised work place Workplace We offer
• Design space in the implementation and further development of the physics laboratory training
• Variety of internal training by means of courses or life A super working environment

jobs.description:
PhD position on quantum computing

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

We invite applications for a PhD position in the field of quantum computing, to be advised by Dominik Hangleiter and co-advised by Renato Renner. In our group in Zurich, you will find a welcoming, open, and highly interactive research environment. Our work is collaborative and interdisciplinary, and it is firmly embedded in the international quantum computing community.

Job description

• The topic of your PhD will be at the interface of theoretical computer science, quantum computing architectures, and the foundations of quantum computing with a focus depending on your interests

• If you want to read more about the kind of research questions and challenges that we investigate in our group, you can find more detailed information on our website at dhangleiter.eu

Profile

• We strongly encourage you to submit an application if you have an academic background in computer science, mathematics, or theoretical physics

• You are highly motivated to pursue a PhD, and if you are enthusiastic about collaborating and working together with others

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents in a single merged pdf file in this order :

• your CV, including the contact details of one or two references (max 2 pages),

• a statement explaining how you came to be interested in the theory of quantum computing, a question you are particularly excited about, and why you want to pursue a PhD (max. 500 words),

• a transcript of records (Bachelor’s and Master’s),

• a sample of your own academic writing, for example, a thesis or essay.

We are starting to consider applications and contact your references on June 15, 2026 , but applications can still be submitted until the job is filled. The starting date is flexible.

Further information about D-PHYS can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dominik Hangleiter, dhangleiter@ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

About ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

chevron left Übersicht chevron left Übersicht PhD posizione sul calcolo quantistico 100%, Zurigo, stampa a tempo fisso Drucken Invitiamo le applicazioni per una posizione di dottorato nel campo del calcolo quantistico, da consigliare da Dominik Hangleiter e co-consultato da Renato Renner. jobs.description:
Doctoral position on PFAS Pathways: Tracking “Forever Chemicals” through Soil–Groundwater Interfaces for Safer Water

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Subsurface Environmental Processes Group (Eawag and ETH Zurich) is seeking a dynamic and motivated doctoral student to study the dynamics of PFAS in subsurface environments. Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a class of highly persistent synthetic compounds increasingly detected in soils and aquifers worldwide. Their extreme stability and mobility make PFAS a critical challenge for groundwater quality and drinking water security. Although PFAS contamination has been reported in many regions, the fundamental mechanisms controlling PFAS fate and transport in coupled soil–aquifer systems remain poorly understood.

Job description

• The focus of this PhD project will be on quantifying the control exerted by soil physico-chemical properties and episodic recharge events on the fate, transport, and transformation of PFAS

• The student will have the unique opportunity to learn, develop, and apply a range of cutting-edge (laboratory) experimental and modeling techniques, including the integration of machine learning and process-based models

• Measurements will be guided by and compared with the modeling developed in this project

• Findings will help advance our knowledge of governing processes of PFAS mobility in soils and aquifers, providing a robust scientific basis for predictive modelling, risk assessment, and the development of sustainable groundwater protection strategies

Profile

• The successful candidate should have a background in groundwater hydrology, soil physics, engineering, or related areas, with a strong quantitative inclination

• They should have a desire to work experimentally at the interface between physics, chemistry, and engineering, and to combine experimental research with mathematical modeling

• The student will have the opportunity to work in a highly interdisciplinary, fast-paced research environment, to gain skills in several technologies (analytical and computational), to learn about fundamental physical and chemical processes in porous media and subsurface environmental processes in general, and to interact with world-class collaborators in environmental chemistry, reactive transport, and hybrid approaches (process-based models and machine learning)

• The ability to work independently, but also to interact and collaborate within a team, will be a great asset

• An interest for contributing to teaching activities is highly valued

• The project will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Joaquin Jimenez-Martinez (Eawag and ETH Zurich)

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

• a CV

• full transcripts from undergraduate studies (both Bachelor and Masters)

• a brief (1-2 page) statement of research interests

• at least 2 (preferably 3) letters of reference

Further information about Subsurface Environmental
