PhD Studenti in economia circolare e cambiamento climatico Resilienza 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Il Gruppo per l'Economia Circolare all'interno del Dipartimento di Gestione, Tecnologia ed Economia dell'ETH Zurigo indaga il ruolo che le innovazioni tecnologiche, gli interventi politici e le strategie di business svolgono nel passaggio verso un'economia circolare sostenibile. Per ampliare la nostra ricerca sulle vie di transizione circolari cerchiamo: 2 dottorandi in economia circolare e resilienza della catena del valore per la decarbonizzazione e l'adattamento climatico (100%). Sfondo del progetto Posizione 1: ACHIEVE Il PhD è incorporato nel progetto del consorzio SWEET ACHIEVE, che indaga su come affrontare le emissioni di gas a effetto serra meno facile e difficile in Svizzera. La vostra ricerca si concentrerà sulla comprensione del ruolo delle misure di economia circolare nella riduzione delle emissioni in settori impegnativi, tra cui prodotti chimici e farmaceutici e trattamento dei rifiuti. Basandosi su questo, si combinano metodi qualitativi e quantitativi per valutare l'attuazione di misure di economia circolare da prospettive di livello, politica e catena del valore, esaminando i percorsi di adozione, requisiti politici, e come queste misure creano nuovi collegamenti intersettoriali e flussi di materiali di rasatura. Posizione 2: NCCR Clim+ Il NCCR CLIM+ sostiene la Svizzera nella trasformazione verso una società responsabile del clima. Insieme con le parti interessate, la comunità interdisciplinare di ricerca NCCR CLIM+ affronta spazi di soluzione inesplorati alla crisi del clima e sviluppa un progetto per la ricerca a livello mondiale. NCCR CLIM+ comunica e condivide la conoscenza, e forma una nuova generazione di esperti con il dominio necessario e la conoscenza transdisciplinare. La vostra ricerca si concentrerà sulla comprensione di come le interruzioni indotte dal clima, come gli shock della supply chain, la carenza di materie prime o i guasti delle infrastrutture, spingono cambiamenti strutturali duraturi nelle imprese, nelle industrie e nella politica. Combinate metodi qualitativi e quantitativi per analizzare i casi storici e contemporanei di ristrutturazione industriale in risposta agli shock climatici e ambientali, e sviluppare scenari previsionali che dotano alle aziende e ai responsabili politici strategie attuabili per navigare in una crescente variabilità climatica e interdipendenza globale. Descrizione del lavoro Per entrambe le posizioni: Ci aspettiamo che la vostra ricerca sia scientificamente rigorosa e rilevante per i politici e i manager. Collaborerai a stretto contatto con altri ricercatori del nostro gruppo, altri membri dei consorzi di ricerca, oltre a interagire con i responsabili politici e con altri stakeholder. Come parte integrante del tuo lavoro, pubblicherai i tuoi risultati in riviste peer-reviewed ad alto impatto e outlet. Potrai anche supervisionare gli studenti master e sostenere le attività didattiche del gruppo. Profilo Il candidato ideale dovrebbe:
• Tenere una laurea in economia, ingegneria, scienze ambientali o una disciplina strettamente correlata
• Avere un eccellente record accademico
• Avere forti competenze analitiche, compresa l'esperienza con metodi di ricerca qualitativi e quantitativi
• Siate appassionati di sostenibilità, economia circolare e resilienza climatica
• Siate interessati all'intersezione della ricerca sulla sostenibilità e alla sua politica e applicazioni aziendali nel mondo reale
• Essere in grado di lavorare in modo indipendente, gestire più compiti e scadenze
• Essere un giocatore di squadra con forti capacità di comunicazione
• Avere esperienza con codifica e modellazione (ad esempio, con Python)
• Sii fluente in inglese parlato e scritto Non richiesto, ma un plus a:
• Avere esperienza di lavoro in una zona collegata
• Avere pubblicazioni scientifiche precedenti in un settore relativo
• Avere esperienza di lavoro in progetti o team interdisciplinari, tra cui impegno degli stakeholder o lavoro di interfaccia di scienza-politica
• Avere familiarità con la politica industriale ed ambientale svizzera o europea Luogo di lavoro Luogo di lavoro Offriamo Offriamo un ambiente di ricerca positivo in un grande

Votre recherche visera à comprendre le rôle des mesures de l'économie circulaire dans la réduction des émissions dans les secteurs difficiles, y compris les produits chimiques et pharmaceutiques, et le traitement des déchets. Sur cette base, vous combinerez des méthodes qualitatives et quantitatives pour évaluer la mise en oeuvre des mesures de l'économie circulaire au niveau des entreprises, des politiques et de la chaîne de valeur, en examinant les voies d'adoption, les exigences politiques et la façon dont ces mesures créent de nouveaux liens intersectoriels et remodelent les flux matériels. Position 2: NCCR Clim+ Le NCCR CLIM+ soutient la Suisse dans sa transformation vers une société résiliente au climat. En collaboration avec les parties prenantes, la communauté de recherche interdisciplinaire NCCR CLIM+ s'attaque aux espaces de solutions inexplorés à la crise climatique et élabore un plan de recherche sur le climat réalisable dans le monde entier. Le CCNR CLIM+ communique et partage largement ses connaissances et forme une nouvelle génération d'experts possédant les connaissances transdisciplinaires et de domaine nécessaires. Votre recherche visera à comprendre comment les perturbations induites par le climat, comme les chocs de la chaîne d'approvisionnement, les pénuries de matières premières ou les défaillances de l'infrastructure, entraînent des changements structurels durables dans les entreprises, les industries et les politiques. Vous combinerez des méthodes qualitatives et quantitatives pour analyser des cas historiques et contemporains de restructuration de l'industrie en réponse aux chocs climatiques et environnementaux, et développerez des scénarios prospectifs qui équiperont les entreprises et les décideurs avec des stratégies réalisables pour naviguer sur une variabilité climatique croissante et l'interdépendance mondiale. Description de l'emploi Pour les deux positions: Nous nous attendons à ce que votre recherche soit scientifiquement rigoureuse et pertinente pour les décideurs et les gestionnaires. Vous collaborerez étroitement avec d'autres chercheurs de notre groupe, d'autres membres de consortiums de recherche, ainsi qu'interagirez avec les décideurs et d'autres intervenants. En tant que partie intégrante de votre travail, vous publierez vos résultats dans des revues et des points de presse ayant un grand impact sur les pairs. jobs.description:
Postdoctoral researcher in optimization for robust railway timetables

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Despite the excellent quality of public transport systems in Switzerland, the railway system needs to increase its performance (quality, for instance, travel time, and delays) and capacity (amount of services run) and attract more travellers to match the ambitious targets from policy and environmental goals. One key aspect of traditional railway transport systems is their plan, which is based on predetermined routes, lines, and scheduled times, with little possibility of adjusting to unplanned and unexpected circumstances. On the other hand, delays and disruption might affect many services throughout a network by means of propagation. The project focuses on timetable planning that is able to minimize delays and their impacts.

To do so, large-scale optimisation addresses the railway timetabling problem. Typically Mixed Integer Linear Programming approaches are used, which are mathematically complex, and with some limits, when modelling real-life complexity. Incorporating robustness against delays is an additional important aspect. This project assumes that we are able to quantify how small delays develop and propagate throughout the network; how larger disruptions develop and propagate in the network. Given this, we want to determine robust timetables, with suitable choice of buffers and running time reserves. Those timetables, under delays, are able to perform quantitatively better (i.e. less delays, fewer larger delays,...).

This position will be available, with an ideal starting date between September 2026 and April 2027, or further upon agreement; the planned duration of the initial contract is one year, to be extended based on successful performance, for up to 2 years.

Project background

The focus of this project is to understand how delays occur and propagate in a real-life railway network. This exposes some complex dynamics as response to external events (small delays, larger disruptions), and some impact, which can be characterized by simulation models. The scientific challenge involves designing timetabling models that can deal with the complexity of existing system dynamics, in a variety of integrative aspects.

The project is designed in collaboration with industry player operating as railway infrastructure manager. The project bases on available solvers for non-periodic timetabling, which include MILP and Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition approaches. This research is carried out within an international cooperation with the Complex Systems group at Utrecht University, in the Netherlands.

Job description

• expand and consolidate existing timetabling models to include constraints from limited resources; and complex dynamics resulting from variable choices.

• expand scope of scheduling models to tackle multi objective problems, and non-scalar objective functions (like probability of delays).

• study local and systemic impacts of timetables when exposed to expected or speculative delay dynamics.

Profile

Ideally, you have (or are about to receive) a Doctoral Degree in transport sciences, management/ decision sciences, applied mathematics, econometrics, statistics, computer science, physics or related fields.

Your research track is consistent and shows a track record, or clear potential, for analysing, modelling, control, and optimisation of transport systems. You are highly motivated and self-driven, with a clear research vision, academic ambition, and excellent communication and writing skills (fluent spoken and written English is mandatory). Moreover, the following skills are expected of a promising candidate:

• Computer science and ability to program independently complex software

• Ability to model and work with algorithmic design, existing software and data provided by industrial partners

• Knowledge of mathematical optimisation (MILP, IP, LP) and/or control sciences

• Team working and commun

descriptionByLocale.it:
Ricercatore post-dottorato in ottimizzazione per robusti orari ferroviari 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Nonostante l'eccellente qualità dei sistemi di trasporto pubblico in Svizzera, il sistema ferroviario deve aumentare le sue prestazioni (qualità, ad esempio, tempi di viaggio e ritardi) e la capacità (importo dei servizi gestiti) e attirare più viaggiatori per soddisfare gli obiettivi ambiziosi da obiettivi politici e ambientali. Un aspetto chiave dei tradizionali sistemi di trasporto ferroviario è il loro piano, che si basa su percorsi predeterminati, linee e tempi programmati, con poca possibilità di adattarsi a circostanze non pianificate e inaspettate. D'altra parte, ritardi e interruzioni potrebbero influenzare molti servizi in tutta una rete per mezzo di propagazione. Il progetto si concentra sulla pianificazione degli orari che è in grado di minimizzare i ritardi e i loro impatti. Per farlo, l'ottimizzazione su larga scala affronta il problema del timetabling ferroviario. In genere vengono utilizzati approcci di programmazione lineare Integer Misti, matematicamente complessi, e con alcuni limiti, quando si modella la complessità della vita reale. Incorporare robustezza contro ritardi è un ulteriore aspetto importante. Questo progetto presuppone che siamo in grado di quantificare come piccoli ritardi si sviluppano e si propagano in tutta la rete; come le interruzioni più grandi si sviluppano e si propagano nella rete. Chercheur postdoctoral en optimisation pour des horaires ferroviaires robustes 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée Malgré l'excellente qualité des systèmes de transport en commun en Suisse, le système ferroviaire doit améliorer ses performances (qualité, par exemple, temps de déplacement et retards) et sa capacité (nombre de services offerts) et attirer davantage de voyageurs pour atteindre les objectifs ambitieux de politique et d'environnement. Un aspect clé des systèmes de transport ferroviaire traditionnels est leur plan, qui est basé sur des itinéraires, des lignes et des horaires prédéterminés, avec peu de possibilités d'adaptation aux circonstances imprévues et imprévues. D'autre part, les retards et les perturbations pourraient affecter de nombreux services à travers un réseau par la propagation. Le projet met l'accent sur la planification du calendrier qui permet de minimiser les retards et leurs répercussions. Pour ce faire, l'optimisation à grande échelle s'attaque au problème de la chronologie ferroviaire. Ces délais, en raison de retards, sont en mesure d'améliorer quantitativement (c'est-à-dire moins de retards, moins de retards plus importants,...). Ce poste sera disponible, avec une date de début idéale entre septembre 2026 et avril 2027, ou plus tard après accord; la durée prévue du contrat initial est d'un an, à prolonger sur la base d'une performance réussie, pour une durée maximale de deux ans. Contexte du projet Ce projet vise à comprendre comment les retards se produisent et se propagent dans un réseau ferroviaire réel. Cela expose certaines dynamiques complexes comme réponse à des événements externes (petits retards, perturbations plus importantes) et certains impacts, qui peuvent être caractérisés par des modèles de simulation. Le défi scientifique consiste à concevoir des modèles chronométrés qui peuvent traiter de la complexité de la dynamique du système existante, sous divers aspects intégratifs. Le projet est conçu en collaboration avec les acteurs de l'industrie qui travaillent comme gestionnaire de l'infrastructure ferroviaire. Le projet s'appuie sur des résolveurs disponibles pour l'établissement de délais non périodiques, qui comprennent les approches MILP et Benders-Decomposition basées sur la logique. Ces recherches sont menées dans le cadre d'une coopération internationale avec le groupe des systèmes complexes de l'Université d'Utrecht, aux Pays-Bas. Description de l'emploi
• développer et consolider les modèles de calendrier existants afin d'y inclure les contraintes découlant de ressources limitées et la dynamique complexe résultant de choix variables.
• élargir la portée des modèles de programmation pour s'attaquer aux problèmes multi-objectifs et aux fonctions objectives non scalaires (comme la probabilité de retards).
• étudier les impacts locaux et systémiques des calendriers lorsqu'ils sont exposés à une dynamique de retard prévisible ou spéculative. Profil Idéalement, vous avez (ou êtes sur le point de recevoir) un doctorat en sciences des transports, de la gestion/de la décision, mathématiques appliquées, économétrie, statistiques, informatique, physique ou domaines connexes. Votre parcours de recherche est cohérent et montre un parcours, ou un potentiel clair, pour l'analyse, la modélisation, le contrôle et l'optimisation des systèmes de transport. Vous êtes très motivé et autodidacte, avec une vision de recherche claire, l'ambition académique, et d'excellentes compétences de communication et d'écriture (l'anglais parlé et écrit est obligatoire). En outre, les compétences suivantes sont attendues d'un candidat prometteur:
• Informatique et capacité à programmer des logiciels complexes indépendants
• Capacité de modéliser et de travailler avec la conception algorithmique, les logiciels existants et les données fournies par les partenaires industriels
• Connaissance de l'optimisation mathématique (MILP, IP, LP) et/ou des sciences de contrôle
• Travail d'équipe et communauté

Despite the excellent quality of public transport systems in Switzerland, the railway system needs to increase its performance (quality, for instance, travel time, and delays) and capacity (amount of services run) and attract more travellers to match the ambitious targets from policy and environmental goals. One key aspect of traditional railway transport systems is their plan, which is based on predetermined routes, lines, and scheduled times, with little possibility of adjusting to unplanned and unexpected circumstances. Given this, we want to determine robust timetables, with suitable choice of buffers and running time reserves. Those timetables, under delays, are able to perform quantitatively better (i.e. less delays, fewer larger delays,...).

The focus of this project is to understand how different timetables result in complex dynamics as response to external events (small delays, larger disruptions). This research targets improvement of timetable planning models, adjusting the amount and placement of buffers, and reserve times.

Dabei wollen wir robuste Zeitpläne mit geeigneter Wahl von Puffern und Laufzeitreserven bestimmen. Diese Zeitpläne können unter Verzögerungen quantitativ besser durchgeführt werden (d.h. weniger Verzögerungen, weniger größere Verzögerungen,...). Diese Position wird verfügbar sein, mit einem idealen Starttermin zwischen August 2026 und Februar 2027, oder weiter nach Vereinbarung; die geplante Dauer des ersten Vertrags beträgt 18 Monate, danach wird ein Eignungskolloquium die weitere Fortsetzung des Promotionsprojekts bestimmen. Das gesamte Promotionsprojekt soll in insgesamt 4 Jahren abgeschlossen werden. Projekt Hintergrund Der Schwerpunkt dieses Projekts ist zu verstehen, wie unterschiedliche Zeitpläne zu komplexen Dynamiken führen, als Reaktion auf externe Ereignisse (kleine Verzögerungen, größere Störungen). Die wissenschaftliche Herausforderung besteht darin, diese Dynamik in bestehende Zeitvertreibsmodelle zu integrieren, um jene Zeitpläne zu identifizieren, die tatsächlich besser sind, unter Verzögerungen. Diese Forschung zielt auf die Verbesserung der Zeitplanplanungsmodelle, die Anpassung der Menge und Platzierung von Puffern und Reservezeiten. Das Projekt ist in Zusammenarbeit mit dem als Eisenbahninfrastrukturmanager tätigen Industrieplayer konzipiert. Das Projekt basiert auf verfügbaren Solvents für nicht-periodische Zeitvertreibungen, darunter MILP und Logic-Based Benders-Decomposition Ansätze. Diese Forschung wird in einer internationalen Zusammenarbeit mit der Gruppe Complex Systems an der Universität Utrecht in den Niederlanden durchgeführt. Jobbeschreibung
• Erstellung und Nutzung von mathematischen Modellen für die umfassende Zeitplanung, mit Einschränkungen für Fahrzeuge, Besatzung und Infrastruktur, in der Lage, die Platzierung von Puffern
• Entwurf und Umsetzung einer Simulationsoptimierungs-Ansicht zur Bewertung von zeltativen Lösungen unter Berücksichtigung der geschätzten Verzögerungsdynamik und der möglichen Umplanungsgrade, um die Robustheit gegenüber kleinen und großen Verzögerungen proaktiv und reaktiv zu verbessern.
• die Nützlichkeit der vorgeschlagenen Entscheidung quantitativ zu verstehen, ihre Empfindlichkeit auf die betrachteten Annahmen zu schätzen; und im Vergleich zur typischen Reaktion im realen Leben Profil Idealerweise haben Sie (oder sind über zu empfangen) einen Master-Abschluss in Transportwissenschaften, Management / Entscheidungswissenschaften, Ökonometrie, Mathematik, Statistik, Informatik, Physik oder verwandten Bereichen. Ihr Forschungspfad ist konsistent und zeigt einen Rekord oder ein klares Potenzial für die Analyse, Modellierung, Steuerung und Optimierung von Transportsystemen. Sie sind hoch motiviert und selbstfahrend, mit einer klaren Forschungsvision, akademischem Ehrgeiz und exzellenten Kommunikations- und Schreibfähigkeiten ( fließendes gesprochenes und geschriebenes Englisch ist obligatorisch). Chercheur au doctorat en optimisation pour des horaires ferroviaires robustes 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Purée Malgré l'excellente qualité des systèmes de transport en commun en Suisse, le système ferroviaire doit améliorer ses performances (qualité, par exemple, temps de déplacement et retards) et sa capacité (nombre de services offerts) et attirer davantage de voyageurs pour atteindre les objectifs ambitieux de politique et d'environnement. Un aspect clé des systèmes de transport ferroviaire traditionnels est leur plan, qui est basé sur des itinéraires, des lignes et des horaires prédéterminés, avec peu de possibilités d'adaptation aux circonstances imprévues et imprévues. D'autre part, les retards et les perturbations pourraient affecter de nombreux services à travers un réseau par la propagation. Le projet met l'accent sur la planification du calendrier qui permet de minimiser les retards et leurs répercussions. Pour ce faire, l'optimisation à grande échelle s'attaque au problème de la chronologie ferroviaire. Les approches de programmation linéaire intégrales généralement mixtes sont utilisées, qui sont mathématiquement complexes, et avec certaines limites, lors de la modélisation de la complexité de la vie réelle. L'incorporation de la robustesse contre les retards est un autre aspect important. Ce projet suppose que nous sommes en mesure de quantifier la façon dont les petits retards se développent et se propagent dans l'ensemble du réseau; comment les perturbations plus importantes se développent et se propagent dans le réseau. Compte tenu de cela, nous voulons déterminer des calendriers robustes, avec un choix approprié de tampons et de réserves de temps de fonctionnement. Ces délais, en raison de retards, sont en mesure d'améliorer quantitativement (c'est-à-dire moins de retards, moins de retards plus importants,...). Ce poste sera disponible, avec une date de début idéale entre août 2026 et février 2027, ou après accord; la durée prévue du contrat initial est de 18 mois, après quoi un colloque d'aptitude déterminera la poursuite du projet de doctorat. Le projet de doctorat total devrait être terminé en 4 ans au total. Contexte du projet Ce projet vise à comprendre comment les différents calendriers entraînent une dynamique complexe en réponse à des événements externes (petits retards, perturbations plus importantes). Le défi scientifique consiste à intégrer ces dynamiques dans les modèles de calendrier existants, afin d'identifier les calendriers qui sont en fait meilleurs, en cas de retard. Cette recherche vise l'amélioration des modèles de planification du calendrier, l'ajustement du montant et de l'emplacement des tampons, et les temps de réserve. Le projet est conçu en collaboration avec les acteurs de l'industrie qui travaillent comme gestionnaire de l'infrastructure ferroviaire. Le projet s'appuie sur des résolveurs disponibles pour l'établissement de délais non périodiques, qui comprennent les approches MILP et Benders-Decomposition basées sur la logique. Ces recherches sont menées dans le cadre d'une coopération internationale avec le groupe des systèmes complexes de l'Université d'Utrecht, aux Pays-Bas. Description de l'emploi
• établir et utiliser des modèles mathématiques pour l'établissement de calendriers à grande échelle, avec des contraintes sur les véhicules, l'équipage et l'infrastructure, capables de régler le placement des tampons
• concevoir et mettre en œuvre une simulation-optimisation pour évaluer les solutions provisoires, en tenant compte de la dynamique estimée des retards et des degrés possibles de rééchelonnement, afin d'améliorer de manière proactive et réactive la robustesse face aux retards petits et importants.
• comprendre quantitativement l'utilité de la décision proposée, estimer sa sensibilité aux hypothèses considérées et comparer à la réaction typique dans la vie réelle Profil Idéalement, vous avez (ou êtes sur le point de recevoir) une maîtrise en sciences des transports, gestion / sciences décisionnelles, économétrie, mathématiques, statistiques, informatique, physique ou domaines connexes. Votre parcours de recherche est cohérent et montre un parcours, ou un potentiel clair, pour l'analyse, la modélisation, le contrôle et l'optimisation des systèmes de transport. Vous êtes très motivé et autodidacte, avec une vision de recherche claire, l'ambition académique, et d'excellentes compétences de communication et d'écriture (l'anglais parlé et écrit est obligatoire). Zur Unterstützung von Forschung und Lehre sind die Informatikdienste der ETH Zürich als Dienstleistungsorganisation in einer grossen und komplexen IT-Umgebung tätig. In enger Abstimmung mit internen Stakeholdern und Schnittstellenpartnern übernehmen Sie das Eskalations- und Anforderungsmanagement, steuern externe Dienstleister und Sourcing-Partner und treiben die Modernisierung der Plattformen – auch im Kontext von Multi-Vendor-Service-Designs – konsequent voran. Zudem vertreten Sie Ihre Services in strategischen IT-Infrastrukturprojekten und gestalten Entscheidungen in entsprechenden Steering Committees mit.

In Ihrer Führungsrolle leiten Sie mehrere Teams – direkt über Teamleitungen und situativ auch Mitarbeitende – und schaffen eine leistungsorientierte, kollaborative Organisationskultur. Sie stellen eine strategische Ressourcen- und Kompetenzplanung sicher und fördern gezielt die Entwicklung Ihrer Mitarbeitenden im Sinne moderner Leadership-Prinzipien wie Vertrauen, Transparenz, Empowerment und Ergebnisorientierung.

Sie tragen die Gesamtverantwortung für die Finanz- und Beschaffungsprozesse Ihrer Gruppe. Dazu gehören die mittel- und langfristige Finanzplanung (inkl. Forecasting bis 10 Jahre), das laufende Budgettracking sowie die Gestaltung von Service-Tarifen. Sie planen Beschaffungen im Einklang mit technologischen Entwicklungen und Architekturvorgaben und führen die entsprechenden Prozesse in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Procurement.

Profil

Projektmanager (m/w/d) 80%-100%, Zurich, unlimited print Print To support research and teaching, ETH Zurich's computer science services act as a service organization in a large and complex IT environment. We offer high-quality, flexible and scalable computer science services to members of ETH Zurich and support them in competition with the best universities in the world. Do you want to actively shape the future of a powerful, secure and sustainable IT infrastructure? In this key role, you take over the cross-border responsibility for our compute and storage services, perform several teams and shape the strategic further development of our platforms. You combine entrepreneurial thinking, leadership and technological vision. We are looking for a group management Compute & Storage (m/w/d) immediately or by agreement. Description They run the Compute & Storage group independently and are responsible for the entire operation of the associated services. Ensure that our systems meet the highest requirements in terms of availability, stability, security and compliance and at the same time are responsible for the further development of standards and guidelines. In close coordination with internal stakeholders and interface partners, you take over the escalation and requirement management, control external service providers and sourcing partners and drive the modernisation of the platforms – also in the context of multi-vendor service designs – consistently ahead. In addition, you represent your services in strategic IT infrastructure projects and make decisions in corresponding Steering Committees. In your leadership role, you guide several teams – directly via team management and site-based employees – and create a performance-oriented, collaborative organizational culture. They ensure strategic resource and competence planning and promote the development of your employees in the sense of modern leadership principles such as trust, transparency, empowerment and earnings orientation. You have the overall responsibility for the financial and procurement processes of your group. These include medium and long-term financial planning (incl. forecasting up to 10 years), ongoing budget tracking and the design of service plans. They plan procurement in line with technological developments and architectural specifications and conduct the corresponding processes in close cooperation with Procurement. They support section management and IT infrastructure architecture in the strategic orientation of the services. Develop roadmaps for standardization, automation and platform modernization, evaluate new technologies and operating models and manage lifecycle management as well as investment planning. Through regular reporting, you create transparency for the management level and make a central contribution to the sustainable development of the IT infrastructure. Profile
• Multiannual leadership experience in complex organizations, ideally across several teams
• Detectional ability to strategically align and develop organisations
• Strong, modern leadership confession
• Experience in the development and implementation of service and platform strategies
• Ability to translate technological trends into sustainable strategies
• Sovereign stakeholder management at all levels
• Very good understanding of financial management, investment planning and forecasting
• Experience with complex procurement processes and knowledge in the public

The deMello Group in the Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences at ETH Zürich, a world-leading group for the development of novel microfluidic technologies, is looking for a motivated PhD student in cutting-edge research in microfluidics and synthetic biology.

Project background

Living systems rely on continuous energy conversion to maintain vital functions, transforming external energy sources into biochemical units like ATP and NAD(P)H to power metabolic processes. One approach to understanding this complexity is to reconstruct a cell from scratch using a minimal set of components, i.e., to build a synthetic cell. In synthetic biology, micrometer-sized lipid vesicles can serve as artificial cells, providing a platform to reconstruct and manipulate essential biological functions. However, current methods to generate giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs) face challenges such as size heterogeneity, inefficient membrane protein reconstitution, and limited compartmentalization. Overcoming these limitations is essential for engineering self-sustaining synthetic cells that can autonomously regulate energy metabolism and biochemical processes.

Our approach integrates microfluidic precision with synthetic biology to engineer synthetic cells that autonomously regulate energy metabolism and biochemical processes. This interdisciplinary research is conducted in collaboration between ETH Zürich (Dr. Stavrakis) and the University of Bern (Prof. von Ballmoos). The outcomes will pave the way for innovative applications in biotechnology, biosensing, and synthetic bioengineering, contributing fundamentally to the design and fabrication of programmable living systems.

Job description

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to develop microfluidic platforms for reconstituting functional membrane proteins into lipid vesicles. The project combines microfluidics, super-resolution fluorescence imaging, and membrane protein biophysics to engineer synthetic cells that will autonomously regulate energy metabolism, biochemical synthesis, and nutrient transport, mimicking natural cellular homeostasis.

Key Responsibilities

• Establish microfluidic platforms for controlled fabrication of monodisperse synthetic vesicles with tunable membrane properties

• Develop microfluidic strategies for membrane protein reconstitution into synthetic vesicle membranes

• Work closely with both the Zurich and Bern groups, including microfluidics setup and preparation of fluorescently labelled membrane proteins

• Perform super-resolution microscopy of membrane proteins in the synthetic vesicles

The project is highly interdisciplinary, fostering close collaboration with biochemists and biophysicists, to accelerate the design and fabrication of programmable living systems.

Profile

• The successful candidate should hold an MSc degree in chemistry, biophysics, chemical or bio-engineering with first class grades

• Basic experience in microfabrication and microfluidics, biophysics, cell biology will be beneficial

• Fluent communication skills (written and presentation) in English are essential

• The PhD candidate will join an excellent and highly ambitious teams at the forefront of research in the areas of microfluidics and synthetic biology

Workplace

Un approccio alla comprensione di questa complessità è quello di ricostruire una cella da zero utilizzando un set minimo di componenti, cioè, per costruire una cella sintetica. PhD-Position in der Mikrofluidik für die Montage von synthetischen Zellen für die Energieerzeugung, Nährstoffmetabolismus und molekularen Transport 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Die deMello-Gruppe im Fachbereich Chemie und Angewandte Biowissenschaften der ETH Zürich, eine weltweit führende Gruppe für die Entwicklung neuartiger mikrofluidischer Technologien, sucht einen motivierten Doktoranden in der Spitzenforschung in der Mikrofluidik und der synthetischen Biologie. Projekt Hintergrund Living-Systeme setzen auf kontinuierliche Energieumwandlung, um lebenswichtige Funktionen aufrechtzuerhalten und externe Energiequellen in biochemische Einheiten wie ATP und NAD(P)H zu leistungsstoffwechselhaften Prozessen zu transformieren. Ein Ansatz, diese Komplexität zu verstehen, ist, eine Zelle von Kratzern mit einem minimalen Satz von Komponenten rekonstruieren, d.h. eine synthetische Zelle aufzubauen. In der synthetischen Biologie können Mikrometer-Größe Lipidvesikeln als künstliche Zellen dienen, die eine Plattform zur Rekonstruktion und Manipulation wesentlicher biologischer Funktionen bieten. Die aktuellen Methoden zur Generierung von riesigen unilamellaren Vesikeln (GUVs) stellen jedoch Herausforderungen wie Größe Heterogenität, ineffiziente Membranproteinrekonstitution und eingeschränkte Kompartimentalisierung. Die Überwindung dieser Einschränkungen ist für die Konstruktion selbsterhaltender synthetischer Zellen unerlässlich, die den Energiestoffwechsel und biochemische Prozesse autonom regulieren können. Unser Ansatz integriert mikrofluidische Präzision mit synthetischer Biologie, um synthetische Zellen zu entwickeln, die den Energiestoffwechsel und biochemische Prozesse autonom regulieren. Diese interdisziplinäre Forschung wird in Zusammenarbeit zwischen der ETH Zürich (Dr. Stavrakis) und der Universität Bern (Prof. von Ballmoos) durchgeführt. Die Ergebnisse werden den Weg für innovative Anwendungen in der Biotechnologie, Biosensing und synthetischen Bio-Engineering ebnen, was wesentlich zur Gestaltung und Fertigung von programmierbaren Lebenssystemen beiträgt. Jobbeschreibung Wir suchen einen hochmotivierten PhD-Kandidat, um mikrofluidische Plattformen für die Rekonstituierung von funktionellen Membranproteinen in Lipid-Vesicles zu entwickeln. Das Projekt kombiniert Mikrofluidik, superauflösende Fluoreszenz-Bildgebung und Membranprotein-Biophysik, um synthetische Zellen zu entwickeln, die den Energiestoffwechsel, die biochemische Synthese und den Nährstofftransport autonom regulieren und natürliche zelluläre Homöostase nachahmen. Hauptverantwortlichkeiten
• Aufbau mikrofluidischer Plattformen zur kontrollierten Herstellung von monodispersen synthetischen Vesikeln mit abstimmbaren Membraneigenschaften
• Entwicklung mikrofluidischer Strategien zur Membranproteinrekonstitution in synthetische Vesikelmembranen
• Arbeiten Sie eng mit den Gruppen Zürich und Bern zusammen, darunter Mikrofluidik-Setup und Herstellung von fluoreszierenden Membranproteinen
• Super-Resolution Mikroskopie von Membranproteinen in den synthetischen Vesikeln durchführen Das Projekt ist hochinterdisziplinäre und fördert die enge Zusammenarbeit mit Biochemisten und Biophysikern, um die Gestaltung und Fertigung von programmierbaren Lebenssystemen zu beschleunigen. Profil
• Der erfolgreiche Kandidat sollte einen MSc-Abschluss in Chemie, Biophysik, Chemie oder Bio-Engineering mit erstklassigen Noten halten

Doctorat en microfluidique pour l'assemblage de cellules synthétiques pour la production d'énergie, le métabolisme des nutriments et le transport moléculaire 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le groupe deMello du Département de chimie et de biosciences appliquées de l'ETH Zürich, un groupe mondial de pointe pour le développement de nouvelles technologies microfluidiques, recherche un doctorant motivé en recherche de pointe en microfluidique et en biologie synthétique. Contexte du projet Les systèmes vivants comptent sur la conversion continue d'énergie pour maintenir des fonctions vitales, transformant les sources d'énergie externes en unités biochimiques comme l'ATP et le NAD(P)H pour alimenter les processus métaboliques. Une approche pour comprendre cette complexité consiste à reconstruire une cellule à partir de zéro en utilisant un ensemble minimal de composants, c.-à-d., pour construire une cellule synthétique. En biologie synthétique, les vésicules lipidiques de taille micrométrique peuvent servir de cellules artificielles, fournissant une plate-forme pour reconstruire et manipuler les fonctions biologiques essentielles. Cependant, les méthodes actuelles pour générer des vésicules monolamellaires géantes (VGU) sont confrontées à des défis tels que l'hétérogénéité de la taille, la reconstitution inefficace des protéines membranaires et la compartimentation limitée. Surmonter ces limites est essentiel pour l'ingénierie des cellules synthétiques autosuffisantes qui peuvent réguler de façon autonome le métabolisme énergétique et les processus biochimiques. Notre approche intègre la précision microfluidique à la biologie synthétique pour concevoir des cellules synthétiques qui régulent de façon autonome le métabolisme énergétique et les processus biochimiques. Cette recherche interdisciplinaire est menée en collaboration entre ETH Zürich (Dr Stavrakis) et l'Université de Berne (Prof. von Ballmoos). Les résultats ouvriront la voie à des applications novatrices en biotechnologie, en biosension et en bioingénierie synthétique, contribuant fondamentalement à la conception et à la fabrication de systèmes vivants programmables. Description du poste Nous recherchons un doctorant très motivé pour développer des plates-formes microfluidiques pour reconstituer des protéines membranaires fonctionnelles en vésicules lipidiques. Le projet combine la microfluidique, l'imagerie par fluorescence à super-résolution et la biophysique des protéines membranaires pour concevoir des cellules synthétiques qui réguleront de façon autonome le métabolisme de l'énergie, la synthèse biochimique et le transport des éléments nutritifs, en imitant l'homéostasie cellulaire naturelle. Principales responsabilités
• Mettre en place des plates-formes microfluidiques pour la fabrication contrôlée de vésicules synthétiques monodispersées ayant des propriétés membranaires thoneuses
• Développer des stratégies microfluidiques de reconstitution des protéines membranaires en membranes vésiculeuses synthétiques
• Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les groupes Zurich et Berne, y compris la mise en place de microfluidiques et la préparation de protéines membranaires marquées fluorescentement
• Effectuer la microscopie super-résolution des protéines membranaires dans les vésicules synthétiques Le projet est hautement interdisciplinaire, favorisant une collaboration étroite avec les biochimistes et les biophysiciens, pour accélérer la conception et la fabrication de systèmes de vie programmables. Profil
• Le candidat retenu devrait être titulaire d'un diplôme de maîtrise en chimie, biophysique, chimique ou bioingénierie avec des grades de première classe
• Une expérience de base en microfabrication et en microfluidique, biophysique, biologie cellulaire sera bénéfique
• Les compétences de communication (écrites et présentées) en anglais sont essentielles
• Le doctorant se joindra à une excellente et très ambitieuse équipe à la pointe de la recherche dans les domaines de la microfluidique et de la biologie synthétique Lieu de travail Nous offrons
• Votre travail avec impact: Devenez membre de l'ETH Zurich, qui non seulement soutient votre développement professionnel, mais contribue également activement au changement positif dans la société

Postdoctoral Position in Stakeholder Engagement

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

We invite applications for a postdoctoral position at the Transdisciplinarity-Lab (TdLab) of the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zürich. You will be responsible for designing and implementing the stakeholder engagement of the NCCR CLIM+.

Project background

The postdoctoral position will be an integral part of the newly established National Competence Centre in Research NCCR CLIM+ . NCCR CLIM+ supports Switzerland’s transformation towards a climate-resilient society and trains a new generation of experts with strong disciplinary and transdisciplinary expertise. This project offers the opportunity to collaborate with leading experts in atmospheric and climate science within the NCCR CLIM+ as well as ETH Zurich.

Job description

In the NCCR CLIM+ storylines are key to achieve actionable knowledge and cross-disciplinary communication. Storylines are scientifically based stories that represent plausible futures and extreme climate outcomes in their physical and social dimensions. You will be responsible to embed the storylines in their societal environment. For each storyline you will

• Identify the most important stakeholders and establish a network that connects them with the storyline’s researchers.

• Develop, implement and evaluate a Theory of Change with the network.

• Design, implement and evaluate the transdisciplinary process of engagement and co-production of knowledge and practices.

You are welcome to further develop transdisciplinary methods and theories and to make your achievements known via talks and publications.

The position is for three years initially and can be extended. The starting date is as soon as possible.

In general, doctoral / postdoctoral researchers at ETH Zurich have a full-time employment. A part-time employment may only be considered in exceptional cases (e.g. child- or familycare, other projects or employment).

Profile

We are looking for a person who

• Has a doctorate in environmental or sustainability sciences.

• Is experienced in designing, implementing and evaluating transdisciplinary research processes.

• Has excellent interpersonal skills for both, collaborating with researchers of different disciplines as well as with stakeholders of different sectors of society.

• Can handle situations of conflicting communication, power and interests, looking for a pragmatic way forward.

• Is interested in critically questioning transdisciplinary theories and methods to develop them further.

• Is fluent in English and German.

Workplace

We offer

TdLab’s expertise lies in theories and practices of transdisciplinary research and teaching. We offer a work environment that invites you to take ownership of your project, while getting skilled support as needed. We are looking for collaborators who want to further develop transdisciplinary research and teaching with a mindset of failing forward. Your future colleagues have diverse disciplinary backgrounds. They work with theories and practices of transdisciplinary research and teaching as a means to promote sustainable development.

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

• Peut gérer des situations de communication, de pouvoir et d'intérêts contradictoires, à la recherche d'une voie pragmatique.
• S'intéresse à la remise en question critique des théories et méthodes transdisciplinaires pour les développer davantage.

jobs.description:
Leitung Brand- und Explosionsschutz (m/w/d)

100%, Zürich, unbefristet

print
Drucken

Die Abteilung Sicherheit, Gesundheit und Umwelt (SGU) berät, unterstützt und schult sämtliche Organisationseinheiten und Angehörigen der ETH Zürich bei Fragen zu Sicherheit und Gesundheit am Arbeitsplatz. Sie ist Anlaufstelle für alle zentral zu organisierenden Massnahmen im Umgang mit Gefährdungen und Risiken zum Schutz von Mensch, Tier, Sachwerten, Infrastruktur und Umwelt sowie bei Fragen bezüglich der Erfüllung der entsprechenden gesetzlichen Anforderungen. Für den Ereignisfall unterhält sie eine angemessene Notfallorganisation. Sowohl im Alltag als auch im Ereignisfall arbeitet sie eng mit den Behörden und externen Einsatzkräften zusammen.

Im Bereich Brand- und Explosionsschutz (BEx) verantworten wir die ETH-weite Organisation und Koordination von baulichen, technischen und organisatorischen Massnahmen: dazu gehören beispielsweise die Erarbeitung und Aktualisierung von internen Konzepten, von baulich-technischen Vorgaben und Merkblättern, Federführung oder Mitwirkung bei integralen Sicherheitskonzepten sowie Kontrolle von deren Umsetzung. Zudem sorgen wir für Information und Schulung der ETH-Angehörigen und bringen unsere Fachexpertise bei Bauprojekten ein. Auch die digitale Dokumentation der durchgeführten Qualitätssicherungen gehört zu unseren Aufgaben.

Um diese Aufgaben professionell und effektiv erfüllen zu können, suchen wir ab 1. Juli 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung eine engagierte, fachkundige und loyale Persönlichkeit als Leitung Brand- und Explosionsschutz (m/w/d) .

Projekthintergrund

Bist Du bereit, mit Deinem motivierten Team Verantwortung für Brand- und Explosionsschutz im Hochschulalltag zu übernehmen? Behältst Du auch im Ereignisfall die Übersicht? Dann bist Du bei uns genau richtig:

Als Leitung BEx setzt Du Dich massgeblich für die Sicherheit an einer weltweit führenden technischen Hochschule ein. Du kombinierst strategische Führung mit Expertenwissen und bringst Deine Erfahrung bei der Weiterentwicklung von Brand- und Explosionsschutz in Forschung, Lehre und Verwaltung sowie in Bauprojekten oder dem Risiko- und Ereignismanagement ein.

Bei grösseren Ereignissen bist Du Teil der Notfallorganisation der ETH Zürich: Du stehst mit Deinem Fachwissen und Deiner Erfahrung beratend zur Seite oder bietest Führungsunterstützung an.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Du trägst die personelle, organisatorische und inhaltlich-fachliche Verantwortung in Deinem Zuständigkeitsbereich und stellst die Umsetzung der Kernaufgaben sicher.

• Als Sicherheitsbeauftragter Brandschutz gemäss Weisung GVZ koordinierst Du die Belange des Brand- und Explosionsschutzes über das gesamte ETH-Portfolio hinweg wie z. B. Planung und Druchführung von internen Audits, Freihaltung Fluchtwege, Explosionsschutz, Veranstaltungsbeurteilungen, Betreuung und Ausbildung interner Erstintervention «Brand/Evakuation».

• Du verantwortest die Erstellung und Aktualisierung der Evakuationskonzepte für alle ETH Liegenschaften und definierst die zu gehörigen Alarmierungsprozesse.

• Dein Fachwissen bringst Du aktiv bei der Gestaltung integraler Sicherheitskonzepte ein und unterstützt das Risikomanagement z. B. für Veranstaltungen.

• Du nimmst Einsitz in Bauprojektteams der ETH und sorgst mit Deiner Fachexpertise für professionelle Beratung der Projektleitung (z. B. Brandmeldeanlagen, Sicherheitsausrüstungen).

• Du beteiligst Dich an der Organisation und Koordination des Ereignismanagements der ETH Zürich und übernimmst im Ereignisfall eine aktive Rolle.

• Netzwerkpflege im ETH-Bereich und darüber hinaus sind Dir zwecks Benchmarking, Know-How-Transfer und Erfahurungsaustausch wichtig, auf die fachliche Weiterbildung Deiner Mitar

descriptionByLocale.it: ## Posizione disponibile ### **Leitung Brand- und Explosionsschutz (m/w/d) Tipo di contratto**: 100%, Zürich, **unbefristet Modalità di selezione print** (Drucken) --- ## Descrizione dell'incarico La **Abteilung Sicherheit, Gesundheit und Umwelt (SGU)** consiglia, supporta e forma tutte le unità organizzative e i membri dell’ETH Zürich in materia di sicurezza e salute sul lavoro. È il punto di riferimento per tutte le misure centralizzate relative alla gestione delle **Gefährdungen e dei rischi** al fine di proteggere persone, animali, beni materiali, infrastrutture e ambiente, nonché per il rispetto delle **corrispondenti normative**. Nel settore **Brand- und Explosionsschutz (BEx)**, si assume la responsabilità dell’**organizzazione e coordinamento** delle misure architettoniche, tecniche e organizzative, tra cui: - la **redazione e aggiornamento** di concetti interni, prescrizioni tecnico-architettoniche e linee guida; - la **dirigenza o partecipazione** a concetti di sicurezza integrali; - la **controllo dell’applicazione** di tali misure; - la **informazione e formazione** degli appartenenti all’ETH; - l’apporto di **espertise tecnica** in ambito progettuale. La **documentazione digitale** delle attività di qualità assicurata svolte rientra tra le responsabilità. --- ## Progetto di riferimento Sei pronto a **prendere responsabilità** con un team motivato per la sicurezza **Brand- und Explosionsschutz** nell’ambito universitario? Mantieni anche in caso di evento la **visibilità strategica**? Allora sei nel posto giusto: Come **Leitung BEx**, ti impegnerai a garantire la sicurezza in una **istituzione tecnica leader a livello mondiale**. Combinerai **leadership strategica** con **esperienza tecnica**, portando la tua competenza nello sviluppo di **Brand- und Explosionsschutz** in ricerca, didattica, amministrazione e nei progetti di costruzione, nonché nel **gestione dei rischi e degli eventi**. In caso di **eventi significativi**, farai parte della **Notfallorganisation dell’ETH Zürich**: fornirai consulenza e supporto di leadership con le tue competenze e esperienza. --- ## Compiti principali - **Assumi la responsabilità** personale, organizzativa e **in termini di contenuti e competenze** nel tuo ambito di competenza e assicurati il **corretto svolgimento delle attività core**. - Come **Sicherheitsbeauftragter Brandschutz** secondo la **Weisung GVZ**, coordini **i temi di Brand- und Explosionsschutz** su tutto il **portfolio ETH**, tra cui: - pianificazione e **esecuzione di audit interni**, liberazione dei percorsi di evacuazione, **Explosionsschutz**, valutazione di eventi; - **gestione e formazione** di interventi interni di primo soccorso «Brand/Evacuazione». - **Responsabilizzarti della creazione e aggiornamento** dei **concept di evacuazione** per tutte le **immobili ETH** e definire i **processi di allarme** correlati. - **Contribuisci attivamente alla progettazione** di **concept di sicurezza integrali** e supporta il **risiko management**, ad esempio per eventi. - **Partecipare a team di progetto** dell’ETH e **fornire consulenza professionale** alla direzione di progetto (es. **Brandmeldeanlagen equipaggiamenti di sicurezza**). - **Collaborare nell’organizzazione e coordinamento** del **gestione degli eventi** dell’ETH Zürich e **assumere un ruolo attivo** in caso di evento. - **Mantenere il network** all’interno e al di fuori dell’ETH per **benchmarking, trasferimento di know-how e scambio di esperienze**, nonché per la **formazione continua dei tuoi collaboratori**.

It is the point of reference for all centralized measures relating to the management of Gefährdungen and the risks in order to protect people, animals, material goods, infrastructure and environment, as well as for compliance with the relevant regulations. In the Brand- und Explosionssschutz (BEx) sector, we assume responsibility for the organization and coordination of architectural, technical and organizational measures, including: - the drafting and updating of internal concepts, technical-architectural requirements and guidelines; - management or participation in integral safety concepts; - control of the application of such measures; - information and training of members of the ETH; - the contribution of technical experts in the design field. The digital documentation of the quality activities carried out is one of the responsibilities. -- Reference project Are you ready to take responsibility with a motivated team for safety Brand- und Explosionsschutz in the university? Do you also maintain strategic visibility in the event? Then you're in the right place. Like Leitung BEx, you will strive to ensure security in a leading technical institution worldwide. En cas d'événements importants, vous ferez partie de l'organisation de Notfall : vous fournirez des conseils et un soutien de leadership avec vos compétences et votre expérience. --- Principales tâches - Prendre des responsabilités personnelles, organisationnelles et en termes de contenu et d'expertise dans votre domaine de compétence et assurer la bonne exécution des activités de base. - Comme Sicherheitsbeauftragter Brandschutz selon le Weisung GVZ, coordonne les thèmes de Brand- und Explosionsschutz sur l'ensemble du portefeuille ETH, y compris: - la planification et l'exécution des audits internes, la libération des voies d'évacuation, Explosionsschutz, l'évaluation des événements; - la gestion et la formation des interventions internes de premiers secours «Brand/Evacuation». - La responsabilité de créer et de mettre à jour des concepts d'évacuation pour toutes les propriétés de l'ETH et de définir les processus d'alarme connexes. - Oui. jobs.description:
PhD in land use modeling

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair for Planning of Landscape and Urban Systems (PLUS) at the Institute for Spatial and Landscape Planning, ETH Zurich, is a young, dynamic and interdisciplinary research team addressing problems of sustainable spatial and landscape development. Starting in September 2026 or by mutual agreement, we are looking for a PhD in land use modeling.

Project background

The 4-year PhD position is funded by the NCCR CLIM+ program ( NCCR CLIM+ — Climate Extremes and Society ), financed by the Swiss National Science Foundation. NCCR CLIM+ supports Switzerland in the transformation towards a climate-resilient society. Together with stakeholders, the interdisciplinary NCCR CLIM+ research community tackles unexplored solution spaces to the climate crisis and develops a blueprint for actionable climate research worldwide. The project will be carried out in a collaborative environment between WSL, Agroscope, and ETH Zürich, providing extensive technical know-how and interdisciplinary expertise in hydrology, forestry and agriculture.

Job description

• The PhD student will further develop and apply a land use model, evoland-plus (pattern-based land use change model coupled with WASIM and FORCLIM), to forecast future changes in biodiversity and ecosystem services under various socio-economic and climate scenarios

• The candidate will use both statistical and process-based approaches to better represent hydrology, forest dynamics and agricultural production and their effects on land use and ecosystem services. In particular, the candidate should be interested in applying the model to contribute to robust storylines of self-consistent plausible futures encompassing the physical and social dimensions of extreme climate outcomes

The results will be transformed into policy guidance reports and other documentation.

Profile

• We are seeking a highly motivated candidate with a MSc degree in Land System Science, Environmental Sciences, Geography, Agricultural Science or related discipline, who has a deep understanding of social-ecological systems, experience in programming and has very good GIS skills

• Ideal candidates have experience with ecosystem services modeling, forest dynamic modeling, hydrological modeling or species distribution modeling, and interest in working on the interfaces between these topics

• Furthermore, the applicant should have a good command of English (both written and spoken) and should be willing to communicate with and work in a large interdisciplinary project. German or French is an advantage as a second language

The full-time position is funded for four years. Salary and social benefits are provided according to ETH Zurich rules.

Workplace

We offer

• A stimulating, interdisciplinary research environment in a dynamic and international team, see ALEA Award 2018 – Finalist Adrienne Grêt-Regame

• Close collaboration with leading experts in social-ecological systems, computational text analysis, and well-being research

• Excellent working conditions at ETH Zurich, one of the world’s leading universities

• Opportunities for academic development, publication, and international networking

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

• Curriculum vitae

• A comp

jobs.description:
Financial and administrative officer

60%-80%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The NCCR CLIM+ is a new National Center of Competence in Research that is establishing the first fully interdisciplinary, Switzerland-wide climate research community that tackles pressing issues related to climate extremes such as heatwaves, floods, heavy rainfalls, droughts, wildfires, and further compound events. It will thereby interact with stakeholders ranging from public health to finance, agriculture, and water management. tp produce actionable climate solution pathways related to adaptation and mitigation, forming a new transdisciplinary nexus between science, society, practice, and politics.

Project background

NCCR CLIM+ is led by ETH Zurich and the University of Bern, and includes 20 partner institutions across Switzerland. At ETH Zurich, NCCR CLIM+ is led by Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne and Prof. David N. Bresch, with a total involvement of 17 professors and research groups from 8 departments. The other leading house is the University of Bern (co-director: Prof. Karin Ingold; deputy co-director: Prof. Olivia Romppainen-Martius). In total, the NCCR CLIM+ has 57 project partners from a range of institutions from Switzerland. The first phase of NCCR CLIM+ is planned until April 30, 2030, with a possible extension for an additional 4–8 years (up to 12 years in total). NCCR CLIM+ will also lead the development of a newly founded long-term Center for Climate Extremes and Resilience in Swiss Society (CERESS).

Further information about NCCR CLIM+ can be found on our website .

Job description

The Financial and administrative officer position is part of the NCCR CLIM+ Management Center, which is headed by an Executive manager. The Management Center also includes a Communications Officer, as well as Technical and Scientific officers from the NCCR CLIM+. The main responsibilities of the NCCR CLIM+ Financial and administrative officer will be as follows:

• Establishment of the NCCR CLIM+ Management Center at ETH Zurich in collaboration with the Executive Manager, as well as Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne and Prof. David N. Bresch

• Budget management and accounting of NCCR CLIM+, including distribution and financial controlling of SNSF funds allocated to the principal investigators of NCCR CLIM+

• Budget management and accounting of ETH Zurich funding within NCCR CLIM+, including financial controlling

• Financial reports for SNSF and ETH Zurich

• Financial, human resources, and general administration of the Management Center

• Timely execution of all activities and services in accordance with the SNSF' and ETH Zurich’s guidelines and process requirements

• Correspondence and communication with the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF), ETH Zurich Administration, and NCCR CLIM+ PIs on financial and administrative matters

• Co-organization of site visits, conferences, workshops, reports, and proposals in collaboration with NCCR CLIM+ Executive Manager, as well as Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne and Prof. David N. Bresch

Profile

• Demonstrated expertise and experience in finance management and budget controlling

• High degree of autonomy

• Excellent command of English (written and spoken)

• Excellent command of German (written and spoken)

• Expertise and experience in administrative management (particularly finance and human resources)

• Expertise and experience in event management and reporting

• Solid computer skills (office, internet, budget accounting); ability to use programs and applications to solve complex problems and tasks quickly and independently

• Efficient and precise work style

• Sense of responsibility, quick learner, ability to take initiative, and organizational skills

• Interpersonal skills, flexibility, and ability to work under pressure

• Experience with university administrative processes is a plus

• Experience in the administration of interdisciplinary research projects is a plus

• Teamplayer

Workp

jobs.description:
Proteomics Laboratory Assistant

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Functional Genomics Center Zurich (FGCZ) is a joint state-of-the-art research and training facility of the ETH Zurich and the University of Zurich. With the latest technologies and key expertise for omics research, the FGCZ provides research services and project support to the Zurich life science research community.

Project background

The FGCZ Proteomics Unit supports internal and external research groups by offering services, training, and instrument access. The analytical portfolio includes identifying, characterizing and quantifying proteins in body fluids, tissues and cells. Together with the Bioinformatics team, the Proteomics Unit covers all steps from initial consultation, experimental design, sample preparation, liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) data acquisition, data processing and data analysis. The group is supported by IT and bioinformatics experts and by the Metabolomics and Genomics Units of the FGCZ to support multi-omics approaches.

Job description

• You will be part of an international team of specialists working in the FGCZ proteomics core facility

• You will be primarily supporting the team during the sample preparation and the data acquisition for a variety of mass spectrometry-based proteomics workflows aimed at the identification, characterization and quantification of peptides and proteins using LC-MS from various biological sources

• Examples of responsibilities are routine sample preparation methods such as in-gel, on-beads and in-solution digestion, peptide desalting, evaluating and interpreting quality control features during and after data acquisition and basic data analysis workflows

• Furthermore, you will be responsible for the maintenance of different LC-MS instrument platforms, and support practical organizational aspects of the proteomics laboratories. This position is initially foreseen as a two-year contract

Profile

• Completed professional training as a chemistry or biology laboratory technician or, alternatively, bachelor in analytical chemistry, biology, or in a closely related field

• Wet lab experience in biochemistry and/or analytical chemistry

• Hands-on experience with LC-MS and/or other protein analysis techniques is an asset

• Organizational skills, with the flexibility to adapt to a wide range of analytical protocols in a highly dynamic environment. Attention to detail and adherence to SOPs

• Problem-solving skills

• Effective and good written and oral communication skills in English are a must, knowledge of German is helpful

• Team player, ambitious, and motivated to learn and make a difference through proteomics and protein analysis

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We are looking forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

• Motivation letter

• CV

• Apprenticeship and/or degree certificates

• Reference letters/work certificates

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted

## Job Title Proteomics Laboratory Assistant ## Position Type & Location 100%, Zurich, fixed-term --- ## Descrizione del lavoro The Functional Genomics Center Zurich (FGCZ) è un centro di ricerca e formazione all'avanguardia, congiunto tra l'ETH Zurich e l'Università di Zurigo. Grazie alle ultime tecnologie e all'esperienza chiave nel campo della ricerca degli omici, il FGCZ offre servizi di ricerca e supporto ai progetti alla comunità scientifica delle scienze della vita di Zurigo. --- ## Background del progetto Il **Proteomics Unit** del FGCZ supporta gruppi di ricerca interni ed esterni offrendo servizi, formazione e accesso agli strumenti. Il portafoglio analitico include l'identificazione, la caratterizzazione e la quantificazione di proteine nei fluidi biologici, nei tessuti e nelle cellule. Insieme alla squadra di Bioinformatica, il Proteomics Unit copre tutte le fasi, dall'iniziale consulenza alla progettazione sperimentale, dalla preparazione dei campioni alla acquisizione dei dati tramite liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS), fino al trattamento e all'analisi dei dati. La squadra è supportata da esperti IT e bioinformatici, nonché dalle unità Metabolomics e Genomics del FGCZ per supportare approcci multi-omics. --- ## Mansioni - Sostenerà la squadra durante la preparazione dei campioni e l'acquisizione dei dati per una varietà di workflow basati su mass spectrometry proteomics, mirati all'identificazione, caratterizzazione e quantificazione di peptidi e proteine tramite LC-MS da fonti biologiche diverse - Esempi di responsabilità includono metodi di preparazione dei campioni di routine come digestione in-gel, su-beads e in-solution, desalazione dei peptidi, valutazione ed interpretazione dei controlli di qualità durante e dopo l'acquisizione dei dati e workflow di analisi dati di base - Responsabilità della manutenzione di diverse piattaforme di strumentazione LC-MS e supporto agli aspetti organizzativi pratici dei laboratori di proteomica - La posizione è inizialmente prevista per un contratto biennale --- ##
• Requisiti - Diploma professionale di tecnico chimico o biologico di laboratorio o, alternativamente, laurea in chimica analitica, biologia o in un campo strettamente correlato - Esperienza di laboratorio in biochimica e/o chimica analitica - Esperienza pratica con LC-MS e/o altre tecniche di analisi delle proteine è un asset - Competenze organizzative, con la flessibilità di adattarsi a una vasta gamma di protocolli analitici in un ambiente altamente dinamico - Attitudine al dettaglio e rispetto delle procedure standard operative (SOPs) - Capacità di risolvere problemi - Buone competenze comunicative scritte e orali in inglese (conoscenza del tedesco è un vantaggio) - Personalità di squadra, ambiziosa e motivata a imparare e fare la differenza attraverso la proteomica e l'analisi delle proteine --- ##
• Cosa offriamo - Il tuo lavoro con impatto: Diventa parte dell'ETH Zurich, che non solo sostiene il tuo sviluppo professionale, ma contribuisce attivamente a cambiamenti positivi nella società - Numerosi benefici, tra cui: - Biglietti per i mezzi pubblici stagionali e condivisione auto - Una vasta gamma di sport offerti dall'ASVZ - Assistenza per la cura dei bambini e vantaggi pensionistici attraenti - Lavoro, insegnamento e ricerca all'ETH Zurich - Valutiamo la diversità e la sostenibilità - In linea con i nostri valori, l'ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza di opportunità, valorizziamo la diversità e coltiviamo un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui i diritti e la dignità di tutti i nostri dipendenti e studenti siano rispettati. Visita il nostro sito sulle pari opportunità e sulla diversità per scoprire come garantiamo un ambiente aperto e giusto che permetta a tutti di crescere e prosperare. - La sostenibilità è un valore fondamentale per noi: lavoriamo costantemente verso un futuro climatico neutro. --- ## Contatto Curioso? Lo siamo anche noi. Invia la tua candidatura online con i seguenti documenti: - Lettera motivazionale - CV - Certificati di apprendistato e/o laurea - Lettere di riferimento o certificati professionali **Nota:** Le candidature vengono accettate esclusivamente tramite il portale online.

jobs.description:
Communication Specialist

50%-60%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

We are seeking a creative Communication Specialist starting from September/October 2026 to help us intensify our communication, outreach and online presence. In this role, you will be responsible for managing and further developing the communication channels of NADEL and ETH4D, ensuring clear and engaging messaging.

About NADEL and ETH4D

NADEL offers various educational programs and events for ETH students, professionals, and the Swiss public on global cooperation and sustainable development. NADEL works closely with various Swiss organisations within the field of global sustainable development.

ETH4D is an ETH-wide initiative of over 60 research groups from engineering, natural sciences to social sciences, which develop innovations that address global challenges and foster teaching collaborations in engineering and natural sciences with universities on the African continent.

This position is a great opportunity for communications professionals who are interested in global development issues and communication of scientific research and teaching to a wider audience.

Job description

You will be responsible for the overall planning, organization, and strengthening of the communication and outreach activities. Key responsibilities include:

• Coordination, layout design, and copy-editing of media information, research briefs, reports and further communications material

• Communicating teaching programs and engaging with donors

• Implementing and further developing the digital strategy of existing websites, newsletters, and social media, including producing text and visual content

• Support with NADEL's podcast, video series, and annual panel

• Planning, organizing and managing events

• Helping to grow our network

The position is limited to a duration of 2 years.

Profile

• Degree in communication, journalism, media studies, public relations or a related field

• At least 2 years of work experience in communications or public relations

• Proven experience in content creation, digital communication and social media (LinkedIn, Instagram)

• Strong writing and editing skills in English (German and French is a plus)

• Proven ability to handle a number of different tasks with tight deadlines

• Proactive, organized, and able to work independently

• Skills in graphic design, video/visual content creation is a plus

• Familiarity with the international cooperation sector is a plus

• Work experience in academic environment is a plus

Workplace

We offer

• A dynamic, international and interdisciplinary working environment

• The opportunity to contribute to impactful work at the interphase of research, education and global development

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents in one PDF file by 20th of June 2026:

• CV (max. 2-3 pages)

• A short video (max. 3 minutes) of yourself telling us: (1) what motivates you to apply, and (2) why you think you're a great fit for this role. We do not expect a professionally produced video. A recording with your smartphone is perfectly sufficient. Please upload the video to a platform of your choice (Dropbox, YouTube, Vimeo, Google Drive, etc.) and include the corresponding URL link in your CV.

• 1-2 work samples

• Degree certificates

• Letters of recomme

jobs.description:
Doctoral position in plant metabolism and stable isotope biology (H-Shifts)

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The position is part of the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) project H-Shifts : "The ²H fingerprint of plant metabolites to trace carbon metabolic shifts”. The project combines isotope biogeochemistry, plant physiology, and crop science to develop a novel tool for tracking metabolic fluxes in plants.

You will join a dynamic and interdisciplinary research team working at the interface of plant metabolism, stable isotope analysis, and crop improvement. The position sits within the Grassland Science group in the Institute of Agricultural Sciences at the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zurich, in close collaboration with the Physiological Plant Ecology group at the University of Basel where much of the work will be conducted.

Project background

Understanding how plant metabolism drives growth and yield remains a major challenge. While current approaches capture metabolite concentrations, they do not resolve metabolic fluxes – the dynamic processes underlying plant performance.

This project develops a novel approach based on natural-abundance hydrogen stable isotopes in plant carbohydrates (²H). These isotopic “fingerprints” encode information about key metabolic processes such as photosynthesis, carbon partitioning, and energy metabolism.

The doctoral project will contribute to three main objectives:

• Develop methods to separate metabolic isotope signals from environmental (hydrological) variation

• Quantify and attribute isotope signals to specific metabolic processes

• Apply the approach to investigate metabolic shifts associated with soybean domestication and crop breeding

Job description

The doctoral project will involve both controlled-environment experiments and field studies.

• Design and conduct plant growth experiments under controlled isotopic conditions

• Sampling and preparation of plant tissues (sugars, starch, cellulose)

• Stable isotope measurements (e.g., IRMS and NMR-based methods)

• Data analysis and modelling of isotope signals to infer metabolic processes

• Contribution to field experiments on soybean diversity and crop traits

• Statistical analysis (e.g., in R or Python) and interpretation of complex datasets

• Presentation of results at international conferences and publication in peer-reviewed journals

Profile

• A Master’s degree in plant biology, biochemistry, environmental sciences, biogeochemistry, agronomy, ecology or a related field.

• Experience or awareness of isotope applications

• Experience with laboratory protocols

• Interest in plant metabolism and physiology

• Quantitative and statistical skills (e.g., R, Python)

• Motivation to work in an interdisciplinary team

• Good written and spoken English

• Experience and skills working with analytical chemistry are an advantage but not required

Workplace

We offer

• An interesting interdisciplinary and cross-institutional position with collaborative partners from Switzerland and France

• A fully funded four-year doctoral position with competitive salary (ETH Zurich standards)

• Training in cutting-edge isotope techniques and plant physiology

• Access to state-of-the-art laboratory and growth facilities

• Opportunities for scientific training, networking, and career development

• We value diversity and promote an inclusive and respectful working environment.
