Posizione dottorale nel metabolismo delle piante e biologia isotopo stabile (H-Shifts) 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La posizione fa parte del progetto H-Shifts della Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF): "L'impronta ² H dei metaboliti vegetali per tracciare i cambiamenti metabolici del carbonio". Il progetto combina biogeochimica isotopo, fisiologia vegetale e scienza delle colture per sviluppare un nuovo strumento per tracciare flussi metabolici nelle piante. Si unirà a un team di ricerca dinamico e interdisciplinare che lavora all'interfaccia del metabolismo delle piante, analisi isotopo stabile e miglioramento delle colture. La posizione si trova all'interno del gruppo Grassland Science dell'Istituto di Scienze Agrarie presso il Dipartimento di Scienze Ambientali dell'ETH di Zurigo, in stretta collaborazione con il gruppo di Ecologia delle Piante Fisiologiche presso l'Università di Basilea dove si svolge gran parte del lavoro. Sfondo del progetto Capire come il metabolismo delle piante spinge la crescita e la resa rimane una grande sfida. Mentre gli approcci attuali catturano le concentrazioni di metaboliti, non risolvono i flussi metabolici – i processi dinamici sottostanti prestazioni della pianta. Questo progetto sviluppa un approccio innovativo basato su isotopi stabili dell'idrogeno ad assorbimento naturale nei carboidrati vegetali (² H). Queste “impronta digitale” isotopiche codificano le informazioni sui processi metabolici chiave come la fotosintesi, il partizionamento del carbonio e il metabolismo energetico. Il progetto di dottorato contribuirà a tre obiettivi principali:
• Sviluppare metodi per separare i segnali isotopi metabolici dalla variazione ambientale (idrologica)
• Segnali isotopi quantificabili e attributo a specifici processi metabolici
• Applicare l'approccio per indagare i cambiamenti metabolici associati all'addomesticamento di soia e l'allevamento di colture Descrizione del lavoro Il progetto di dottorato coinvolgerà sia gli esperimenti ambientali controllati che gli studi sul campo.
• Progettare e condurre esperimenti di crescita delle piante in condizioni isotopiche controllate
• Sampling e preparazione dei tessuti vegetali (sugars, amido, cellulosa)
• Misure isotopi stabili (ad esempio, metodi basati su IRMS e NMR)
• Analisi dei dati e modellazione dei segnali isotopi per indurre i processi metabolici
• Contributo agli esperimenti sul campo sulla diversità di soia e sulle caratteristiche delle colture
• Analisi statistica (ad esempio, in R o Python) e interpretazione di set di dati complessi
• Presentazione dei risultati a conferenze internazionali e pubblicazione in riviste peer-reviewed Profilo
• Laurea magistrale in biologia vegetale, biochimica, scienze ambientali, biogeochemistria, agronomia, ecologia o campo correlato.
• Esperienza o consapevolezza delle applicazioni isotopi
• Esperienza con protocolli di laboratorio
• Interessi del metabolismo delle piante e della fisiologia
• Abilità quantitative e statistiche (ad esempio, R, Python)
• Motivazione per lavorare in un team interdisciplinare
• Buono scritto e parlato inglese
• Esperienze e competenze che lavorano con la chimica analitica sono un vantaggio ma non richiesto Luogo di lavoro Offriamo
• Una interessante posizione interdisciplinare e inter-istituzionalista con partner collaborativi della Svizzera e della Francia
• Una posizione di dottorato a quattro anni completamente finanziata con uno stipendio competitivo (standard EH Zurich)
• Formazione in tecniche isotopi all'avanguardia e fisiologia vegetale
• Accesso alle strutture di laboratorio e di crescita all'avanguardia
• Opportunità di formazione scientifica, networking e sviluppo della carriera

Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza di opportunità, la diversità di valore e nutrire un ambiente di lavoro e di apprendimento in cui i diritti e la dignità di tutto il nostro staff e gli studenti sono rispettati. descriptionByLocale.de:
Doctoral Position im Pflanzenstoffwechsel und stabile Isotopenbiologie (H-Shifts) 100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Die Position ist Teil des Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) Projekts H-Shifts: "The ²H Fingerabdruck von pflanzlichen Metaboliten zu Spuren von Kohlenstoff-Stoffwechseln". Das Projekt kombiniert Isotopenbiogeochemie, Pflanzenphysiologie und Kulturwissenschaft, um ein neues Werkzeug für die Verfolgung von Stoffwechselflüssen in Pflanzen zu entwickeln. Sie begleiten ein dynamisches und interdisziplinäres Forschungsteam, das an der Schnittstelle des Pflanzenstoffwechsels, der stabilen Isotopenanalyse und der Ernteverbesserung arbeitet. In enger Zusammenarbeit mit der Gruppe Physiologischer Pflanzenökologie an der Universität Basel, wo ein Großteil der Arbeit durchgeführt wird, befindet sich die Position innerhalb der Grassland Science Gruppe am Institut für Agrarwissenschaften am Department of Environmental Systems Science der ETH Zürich. Projekt Hintergrund Wie Pflanzenstoffwechsel Wachstum und Ertrag treibt, bleibt eine große Herausforderung. Während aktuelle Ansätze Metabolitkonzentrationen erfassen, lösen sie keine Stoffwechselflüsse – die dynamischen Prozesse, die der Pflanzenleistung zugrunde liegen. Dieses Projekt entwickelt einen neuartigen Ansatz auf Basis von naturabgebenden, wasserstoffstabilen Isotopen in Pflanzenkohlenhydraten (²H). Diese isotopischen "Fingerabdrücke" kodieren Informationen über wichtige Stoffwechselprozesse wie Photosynthese, Kohlenstofftrennung und Energiestoffwechsel. Das Promotionsprojekt wird zu drei Hauptzielen beitragen:

Position au doctorat dans le métabolisme des plantes et la biologie isotopique stable (H-Shifts) 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Cette position fait partie du projet H-Shifts de la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences (SNSF) : « The ²H dactylographic of plant metabolites to trace carbon métabolique shifts ». Le projet combine la biogéochimie des isotopes, la physiologie des plantes et la science des cultures pour élaborer un nouvel outil de suivi des flux métaboliques dans les plantes. Vous rejoindrez une équipe de recherche dynamique et interdisciplinaire travaillant à l'interface du métabolisme des plantes, de l'analyse isotopique stable et de l'amélioration des cultures. Ce poste fait partie du groupe des sciences des prairies de l'Institut des sciences agricoles du Département des sciences des systèmes environnementaux de l'ETH de Zurich, en étroite collaboration avec le groupe de l'écologie physiologique des plantes de l'Université de Bâle, où une grande partie des travaux seront menés. Contexte du projet Comprendre comment le métabolisme des plantes stimule la croissance et le rendement demeure un défi majeur. Bien que les approches actuelles saisissent les concentrations de métabolites, elles ne résolvent pas les flux métaboliques – les processus dynamiques sous-jacents à la performance végétale. Ce projet développe une nouvelle approche fondée sur l'abondance naturelle des isotopes stables de l'hydrogène dans les glucides végétaux (²H). Ces empreintes digitales isotopiques encodent les informations sur les processus métaboliques clés tels que la photosynthèse, la partition du carbone et le métabolisme énergétique. Le projet de doctorat contribuera à trois objectifs principaux:
• Élaborer des méthodes pour séparer les signaux isotopes métaboliques des variations environnementales (hydrologiques)
• Quantifier et attribuer des signaux isotopiques à des processus métaboliques spécifiques
• Appliquer l'approche pour étudier les changements métaboliques associés à la domestication du soja et à la reproduction des cultures Description du poste Le projet de doctorat comprendra à la fois des expériences sur l'environnement contrôlé et des études de terrain.
• Concevoir et réaliser des expériences de croissance végétale dans des conditions isotopiques contrôlées
• Échantillonnage et préparation des tissus végétaux (sucres, amidon, cellulose)
• Mesures stables des isotopes (par exemple, méthodes IRMS et RMN)
• Analyse des données et modélisation des signaux isotopiques pour inférer les processus métaboliques
• Contribution aux expériences de terrain sur la diversité du soja et les caractéristiques des cultures
• Analyse statistique (par exemple en R ou en Python) et interprétation de ensembles de données complexes
• Présentation des résultats lors de conférences internationales et publication dans des revues évaluées par les pairs Profil
• Maîtrise en biologie végétale, biochimie, sciences de l'environnement, biogéochimie, agronomie, écologie ou domaine connexe.
• Expérience ou connaissance des applications des isotopes
• Expérience des protocoles de laboratoire
• Intérêt pour le métabolisme et la physiologie des plantes
• Compétences quantitatives et statistiques (par exemple R, Python)
• Motivation de travailler dans une équipe interdisciplinaire
• Bon anglais écrit et parlé
• Expérience et compétences dans le domaine de la chimie analytique sont un avantage mais non requis Lieu de travail Nous offrons

jobs.description:
Research Engineer

100%, Singapore, fixed-term

Drucken

The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions.

Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) .

The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems.

Project background

The healthcare systems of the future must harness data effectively to support clinicians, allowing them to focus on patient care while leveraging AIto detect patterns beyond human perception, enhance diagnostic accuracy, optimise workflows, improve risk assessment and communication. Developing AI models that address these needs is particularly urgent in ageing societies, where rising patient numbers coincide with increasing workforce constraints.

To do so, we are developing the AI for Science Instrumentation Gym, which is designed to bridge this gap by placing data-driven hypothesis generation at the center of its mission. It introduces a critical intermediate step: the tokenization and cartography of scientific data. Through tokenization, complex data is transformed into coarse-grained, interpretable units. Through cartography, these units are organized into latent spaces that can be explored as structured landscapes. In this way, machine learning becomes a tool for mapping high-dimensional data into forms that scientists can navigate, interpret, and use to generate new hypotheses.

To build the AIS Instrumentation Gym, we are opening a set of Instrumentation Gym Lead positions. IGLs are data scientists and systems builders who design, implement, and scale the AIS Instrumentation Gym across its different levels (S/M/L). They form the infrastructure backbone of the ecosystem, enabling domain scientists and machine learning researchers to work with complex scientific data in a structured, scalable, and interpretable way.

Job description

As a Research Engineer, you will be one of the Gym Leads for the ML platform for the Scientific Instrumentation, and you will be working on:

• Data pipelines — ingestion, metadata schemas, and provenance tracking for electron microscopy, X-ray, and light microscopy datasets

• Model interfaces — modular Python APIs that let representation models, tokenizers, and downstream models be swapped and composed

• Baseline tokenization and cartography pipelines, built collaboratively with ML researchers and domain scientists

• LLM- and RAG-assisted interfaces for dataset navigation, workflow discovery, and user interaction

• Forward-compatibility to HPC — ensuring S-Gym and M-Gym components can be lifted into the L-Gym tier without fundamental redesign

Profile

• Master’s degree on a relevant subject (e.g. Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, etc.)

• Strong Python and a modern ML framework (PyTorch preferred)

• Experience building data pipelines and reproducible ML workflows

• Comfort with GPU-based compute and basic scientific data formats

• Track record of building modular, maintainable software

• Interest in working at the intersection of science, ML, and systems enginee

jobs.description:
Doctoral position in social indicator development with text-based and spatial data

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Planning of Landscape and Urban Systems (PLUS) at the Institute for Spatial and Landscape Development , ETH Zurich, is seeking a highly motivated doctoral researcher (100%) to join the project “DEPOPLAND: Drivers and trajectories of social-ecological change in depopulating rural landscapes”, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation.here

Project background

Rural depopulation is emerging as one of the defining global transformations of the 21st century, with profound consequences for both ecosystems and human well-being. The DEPOPLAND project aims to provide the first systematic, global-scale analysis of ecological and social dynamics in depopulating rural landscapes, identifying trajectories of change and their underlying drivers. To do so, the project pioneers an integrated and data-driven approach to analysing social-ecological systems, combining diverse data sources and advanced computational methods to uncover long-term dynamics of ecosystems and human well-being.

DEPOPLAND is highly interdisciplinary, bringing together expertise from landscape ecology, physical and human geography, land system science, and computational linguistics. The project is carried out in collaboration with partners at ETH Zurich, the University of Zurich, and the Universities of Kassel and Göttingen.

Job description

The doctoral researcher will primarily work on Work Packages 1 and 3, focusing on modelling and analysing trajectories of objective and subjective well-being using spatial and computational text analyses.

• Identifying shrinking and growing rural landscapes globally using large-scale population datasets and spatial analysis

• Compiling, harmonising, and analysing region-specific time-series of objective and subjective well-being indicators

• Developing and applying computational text analysis workflows to derive spatially and temporally explicit indicators of subjective well-being from large text-based datasets (e.g. global news databases such as GDELT or other news archives)

• Designing and implementing machine learning models for analysing and predicting well-being indicators

• Collaborating closely with other project members (including a second doctoral student working on ecological trajectories)

• Presenting results at conferences and publishing in peer-reviewed journals

Profile

Required qualifications:

• A Master’s degree in geography, social sciences, landscape planning, economics, data science, or a related field

• Strong interest in well-being research, social indicators, or human–environment interactions

• Experience with computational analysis of text data (e.g. natural language processing, text mining, or computational social science)

• Experience with spatial data analysis and programming (e.g. Python or R)

• Excellent command of English (written and spoken) and strong teamwork skills

Additional assets:

• Experience working with large-scale datasets (e.g. text corpora, event databases, or geospatial data)

• Experience working with survey data or social indicator datasets

• Familiarity with statistical or machine learning methods

• Knowledge of reproducible research practices and version control

Workplace

We offer

• A stimulating, interdisciplinary research environment in a dynamic and international team

• Close collaboration with leading experts in social-ecological systems, computational text analysis, and well-being research

• Excellent working conditions at ETH Zurich, one of the world’s leading universities

• Opportunities for academic development, publication, and international networking

Posizione dottorale nello sviluppo degli indicatori sociali con dati basati sul testo e spaziali 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo La Cattedra di Pianificazione del Paesaggio e dei Sistemi Urbani (PLUS) presso l’Istituto per lo Sviluppo Spaziale e Paesaggio, ETH Zurich, sta cercando un ricercatore di dottorato altamente motivato (100%) per aderire al progetto “DEPOPLAND: Drivers and trajectories of social-ecological change in depopulating paesaggi rurali”, finanziato dalla Fondazione svizzera per la scienza nazionale. Qui Sfondo del progetto Lo spopolamento rurale sta emergendo come una delle trasformazioni globali del XXI secolo, con profonde conseguenze sia per gli ecosistemi che per il benessere umano. Il progetto DEPOPLAND mira a fornire la prima analisi sistematica su scala globale delle dinamiche ecologiche e sociali nel depopolare i paesaggi rurali, identificare le traiettorie del cambiamento e i loro driver sottostanti. A tal fine, il progetto promuove un approccio integrato e basato sui dati per analizzare i sistemi social-ecologici, combinando diverse fonti di dati e metodi computazionali avanzati per scoprire dinamiche a lungo termine degli ecosistemi e del benessere umano. DEPOPLAND è altamente interdisciplinare, che riunisce competenze dall'ecologia del paesaggio, geografia fisica e umana, scienza del sistema terrestre e linguistica computazionale. Il progetto è realizzato in collaborazione con i partner dell'ETH di Zurigo, dell'Università di Zurigo e delle Università di Kassel e Göttingen. Descrizione del lavoro Il ricercatore di dottorato lavorerà principalmente sui Pacchetti di lavoro 1 e 3, concentrandosi sulla modellazione e l'analisi delle traiettorie di benessere oggettivo e soggettivo utilizzando analisi di testo spaziali e computazionali.
• Identificare il restringimento e la crescita dei paesaggi rurali a livello globale utilizzando set di dati su larga scala e analisi spaziale
• Compilare, armonizzare e analizzare le serie temporali specifiche delle regioni di indicatori oggettivi e soggettivi di benessere
• Sviluppare e applicare flussi di lavoro di analisi del testo computazionale per ricavare indicatori spaziali e temporalmente espliciti del benessere soggettivo da grandi dataset basati sul testo (ad esempio database di notizie globali come GDELT o altri archivi di notizie)
• Progettare e implementare modelli di machine learning per analizzare e prevedere indicatori di benessere

Hier. Projekt Hintergrund Ländliche Entvölkerung ist eine der definierenden globalen Transformationen des 21. Jahrhunderts, mit tiefen Konsequenzen für Ökosysteme und menschliches Wohlbefinden. Ici. Contexte du projet Le dépeuplement rural apparaît comme l'une des transformations mondiales déterminantes du XXIe siècle, avec des conséquences profondes tant pour les écosystèmes que pour le bien-être humain. DEPOPLAND est hautement interdisciplinaire, réunissant des compétences en écologie du paysage, en géographie physique et humaine, en science du système terrestre et en linguistique computationnelle. Le projet est réalisé en collaboration avec des partenaires de l'ETH Zurich, de l'Université de Zurich et des Universités de Kassel et de Göttingen. Description du poste Le doctorant travaillera principalement sur les Work Packages 1 et 3, en mettant l'accent sur la modélisation et l'analyse de trajectoires de bien-être objectif et subjectif à l'aide d'analyses de texte spatiale et computationnelle.

• Collaborer étroitement avec d'autres membres du projet (y compris un deuxième doctorant travaillant sur les trajectoires écologiques)

Doctoral position in landscape ecology and geospatial analysis

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Planning of Landscape and Urban Systems (PLUS) at the Institute for Spatial and Landscape Development , ETH Zurich, is seeking a highly motivated doctoral researcher (100%) to join the project “DEPOPLAND: Drivers and trajectories of social-ecological change in depopulating rural landscapes”, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation.

Project background

Rural depopulation is emerging as one of the defining global transformations of the 21st century, with profound consequences for both ecosystems and human well-being. The DEPOPLAND project aims to provide the first systematic, global-scale analysis of ecological and social dynamics in depopulating rural landscapes, identifying trajectories of change and their underlying drivers. To do so, the project pioneers an integrated and data-driven approach to analysing social-ecological systems, combining diverse data sources and advanced computational methods to uncover long-term dynamics of ecosystems and human well-being.

DEPOPLAND is highly interdisciplinary, bringing together expertise from landscape ecology, physical and human geography, land system science, and computational linguistics. The project is carried out in collaboration with partners at ETH Zurich, the University of Zurich, and the Universities of Kassel and Göttingen.

Job description

The doctoral researcher will primarily work on Work Packages 1 and 2, focusing on assessing ecological change in depopulating rural landscapes.

• Identifying shrinking and growing rural landscapes globally using large-scale population datasets and spatial analysis

• Developing and applying spatial-temporal indicators of landscape heterogeneity and ecological processes

• Analysing long-term landscape transformations (composition and configuration) using multi-source geospatial datasets (including satellite remote sensing data)

• Working with large geospatial datasets and implementing scalable workflows

• Collaborating closely with other project members (including a second doctoral student working on well-being trajectories)

• Presenting results at conferences and publishing in peer-reviewed journals

Profile

Required qualifications:

• A Master’s degree in ecology, geography, environmental sciences, landscape planning, geomatics, or a related field

• Excellent understanding of landscape ecology concepts and metrics

• Strong background in spatial analysis and remote sensing

• Proven programming skills (e.g. Python or R)

• Experience working with large geospatial datasets

• Very good command of English (written and spoken) and strong teamwork skills

Additional assets:

• Experience with Google Earth Engine or cloud-based geospatial platforms

• Familiarity with spatial time-series analysis

• Experience with landscape metrics or ecological modelling

• Knowledge of reproducible workflows and version control

Workplace

• A stimulating, interdisciplinary research environment in a dynamic and international team

• Close collaboration with leading experts in landscape ecology, remote sensing, and social-ecological systems

• Ottima comprensione dei concetti di ecologia del paesaggio e metriche
• Forte sfondo nell'analisi spaziale e nel telerilevamento

Position au doctorat en écologie du paysage et analyse géospatiale 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken La Chaire de Planification du Paysage et des Systèmes Urbains (PLUS) de l'Institut de Développement Spatial et du Paysage, ETH Zurich, est à la recherche d'un doctorant hautement motivé (100%) pour rejoindre le projet «DEPOPLAND: Drivers and trajectories of social-écological change in dépepulling ruralscapes» financé par la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences. Contexte du projet Le dépeuplement rural apparaît comme l'une des transformations mondiales déterminantes du XXIe siècle, avec des conséquences profondes tant pour les écosystèmes que pour le bien-être humain. Le projet DEPOPLAND vise à fournir la première analyse systématique à l'échelle mondiale de la dynamique écologique et sociale dans les paysages ruraux dépeuplants, en identifiant les trajectoires du changement et leurs moteurs sous-jacents. Pour ce faire, le projet lance une approche intégrée et axée sur les données pour analyser les systèmes socio-écologiques, combinant diverses sources de données et des méthodes informatiques avancées pour découvrir la dynamique à long terme des écosystèmes et le bien-être humain. DEPOPLAND est hautement interdisciplinaire, réunissant des compétences en écologie du paysage, en géographie physique et humaine, en science du système terrestre et en linguistique computationnelle. Le projet est réalisé en collaboration avec des partenaires de l'ETH Zurich, de l'Université de Zurich et des Universités de Kassel et de Göttingen. jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in AI-Assisted Bridge Assessment for Special Road Transports

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

This project combines classical structural analysis with modern data-based and computational methods (AI & FEM) to advance the structural assessment of bridges under special road transports.

• A fully funded doctoral position at the Chair of Structural Engineering - Concrete Structures and Bridge Design (Prof. Walter Kaufmann), ETH Zurich

• In collaboration with the Computational Design Lab (Prof. B. Bickel), the ETH AI Center and Design++

• With direct practical relevance for Swiss infrastructure and the Swiss Federal Roads Office (ASTRA) as industry partner

Project background

The Swiss Federal Roads Office (ASTRA) processes more than 20,000 applications for special road transports every year — vehicles or vehicle combinations that exceed the legal limits. Roughly half of these applications require a structural assessment of the bridges along the route. Given the high number of applications and the diversity of transport configurations and bridge inventories that need to be considered, this manual assessment is correspondingly time-intensive. This research project explores how methods from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation can complement and further develop the structural assessment of existing bridges under heavy transportation loads. Starting from established engineering practice, we investigate:

• Which parametric models and which representations of the most common bridge types allow us to assess structural safety and serviceability efficiently for special road transports?

• How can simulation data and bridge inventory data be combined so that data-driven models remain mechanically consistent, reliable, and interpretable?

• How can the influence of recurring heavy transports on structural damage and therefore on the durability of the structure be meaningfully captured in such models?

Job description

• Independent research exploring how methods from AI and automation can complement and further develop the structural assessment of existing bridges under heavy transportation loads

• Regular exchange with the industry partner ASTRA (Swiss Federal Roads Office) to ensure practical relevance

• Scientific writing of a doctoral thesis as well as peer-reviewed journal and conference publications, with the opportunity to attend leading international conferences in the field

• Support of teaching activities at the Chair & co-supervision of Bachelor's and Master's theses within the thematic scope of the position

• Completion of 12 course credits in the research field as part of the doctoral programme

Profile

• You enjoy working at the intersection of classical structural engineering and modern data- and computer-aided methods

• You hold a Master's degree in Civil Engineering, preferably with a specialisation in Structural Engineering

• Ideally you also have experience in scripting (Python) and AI/ Machine Learning / Data Science

• You work independently and with high initiative

• You communicate your work clearly in English, both in writing and in exchange with academic and industry partners (German is a plus)

Workplace

We offer

• Supervision by Prof. Walter Kaufmann and Dr. Sophia Kuhn (Postdoc, computational design lab ).

• As part of a chair associated with the ETH AI Center , the opportunity to become an associated researcher and join its community

• Additionally, access to the community of the Center for Augmented Computational Design in Architecture, Engineering and Construction (Design++)

• A range of career development programmes, with mentors from both industry and academia

• A great working environment and a supportive group, according to former doctoral students

Posizione di dottorato in AI-Assisted Bridge Assessment for Special Road Transports 100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato stampa Druppo Questo progetto combina l'analisi strutturale classica con i moderni metodi basati sui dati e computazionali (AI & FEM) per far progredire la valutazione strutturale dei ponti sotto i trasporti stradali speciali.
• Una posizione di dottorato completamente finanziata presso la Cattedra di Ingegneria Strutturale - Strutture Concrete e Bridge Design (Prof. Walter Kaufmann), ETH Zurich
• In collaborazione con Computational Design Lab (Prof. B. Bickel), ETH AI Center e Design++
• Con un'importanza pratica diretta per le infrastrutture svizzere e l'Ufficio federale delle strade (ASTRA) come partner industriale Sfondo del progetto L'Ufficio federale delle strade (ASTRA) elabora più di 20.000 domande per i trasporti stradali speciali ogni anno — veicoli o combinazioni di veicoli che superano i limiti legali. Circa la metà di queste applicazioni richiedono una valutazione strutturale dei ponti lungo il percorso. Data l'elevato numero di applicazioni e la diversità delle configurazioni di trasporto e degli inventari di ponti che devono essere considerati, questa valutazione manuale è corrispondentemente tempo-intensivo. Questo progetto di ricerca esplora come i metodi dell'intelligenza artificiale (AI) e l'automazione possono integrare e sviluppare ulteriormente la valutazione strutturale dei ponti esistenti sotto carichi di trasporto pesanti. Partendo dalla pratica ingegneristica consolidata, studiamo:
• Quali modelli parametrici e quali rappresentazioni dei tipi di ponti più comuni ci permettono di valutare in modo efficiente la sicurezza strutturale e la facilità di servizio per i trasporti stradali speciali?
• Come si possono combinare dati di simulazione e dati di inventario del ponte in modo che i modelli data-driven rimangano meccanicamente coerenti, affidabili e interpretabili?
• Come può l'influenza dei trasporti pesanti ricorrenti sui danni strutturali e quindi sulla durata della struttura essere catturata significativamente in tali modelli? Descrizione del lavoro
• Ricerca indipendente che esplora come i metodi di AI e di automazione possono integrare e sviluppare ulteriormente la valutazione strutturale dei ponti esistenti sotto carichi di trasporto pesanti
• Scambio regolare con il partner del settore ASTRA (Ufficio federale delle strade) per garantire rilevanza pratica
• Scrittura scientifica di una tesi di dottorato e pubblicazioni di riviste e conferenze peer-reviewed, con l'opportunità di partecipare a importanti conferenze internazionali nel settore
• Sostegno alle attività didattiche presso la Cattedra & co-supervisione delle tesi di laurea e Master nell'ambito tematico della posizione
• Completamento di 12 crediti di corso nel campo della ricerca nell'ambito del programma di dottorato Profilo
• Ti piace lavorare all'intersezione dell'ingegneria strutturale classica e dei moderni metodi dati e computer-aided
• Hai una laurea magistrale in Ingegneria Civile, preferibilmente con una specializzazione in Ingegneria Strutturale
• Idealmente hai anche esperienza nello scripting (Python) e AI/ Machine Learning / Data Science
• Lavorate in modo indipendente e con alta iniziativa
• Comunica chiaramente il tuo lavoro in inglese, sia per iscritto che in cambio di partner accademici e industriali (il tedesco è un plus) Luogo di lavoro Offriamo
• Supervisione del Prof. Walter Kaufmann e della Dott.ssa Sophia Kuhn (Postdoc, laboratorio di progettazione computazionale).
• Nell'ambito di una sedia associata all'ETA AI Center , l'opportunità di diventare un ricercatore associato e unirsi alla sua comunità
• Inoltre, l'accesso alla comunità del Center for Augmented Computational Design in Architettura, Ingegneria e Costruzione (Design++)
• Una serie di programmi di sviluppo della carriera, con mentori sia dell'industria che dell'accademia
• Un grande ambiente di lavoro e un gruppo di sostegno, secondo gli ex dottorandi chevron right Lavoro, insegnamento e ricerca presso l'ETH di Zurigo Apprezziamo la diversità e la sostenibilità In linea con i nostri valori, ETH Zurich incoraggia una cultura inclusiva. Promuoviamo l'uguaglianza

Environ la moitié de ces applications nécessitent une évaluation structurelle des ponts le long de la route. jobs.description:
PhD Position on Sleep, Stress and Arousal in Humans

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

A World-Class Research Environment at the Intersection of Sleep, Physiology and Health Technology

The Neural Control of Movement Lab at ETH Zurich, Department of Health Sciences and Technology, invites exceptional candidates to apply for a PhD position focused on the physiological links between sleep, stress, arousal and health in humans. The project combines mechanistic laboratory experiments with real-world, home-based and decentralized phenotyping, using multimodal physiological recordings, mobile health technologies and computational analysis pipelines.

The Neural Control of Movement Lab focuses on understanding how the brain controls behavior and on developing non-invasive interfaces to measure and modulate brain function during wake and sleep. Within this environment, the PhD student will contribute to a translational research program that aims to understand how daily stress and arousal states shape sleep physiology, recovery and health-relevant outcomes in real life.

The Department of Health Sciences and Technology at ETH Zurich unites researchers across neuroscience, biomedical engineering, movement science, nutrition, physiology and medicine. It offers an interdisciplinary environment for research at the interface of human biology, technology and clinical translation.

Project background

Sleep, stress and arousal are deeply interconnected physiological processes. Persistent stress and heightened arousal can alter the transition into sleep, change nocturnal brain and autonomic activity, and influence recovery, resilience and longer-term health. Yet many key mechanisms are still studied either in tightly controlled laboratory settings or through simplified real-world measures that do not capture the richness of human physiology.

This project addresses that gap by combining mechanistic in-lab studies with real-world phenotyping of sleep, stress and arousal in daily life. The goal is to develop rigorous, scalable research workflows that can measure how stress and arousal unfold across the day, how they affect sleep and overnight recovery, and which physiological signatures are most informative for health-relevant phenotypes.

The project will use multimodal biosignal acquisition, such as pupillometry, sleep EEG, ECG, respiration, wearable and actigraphy data, smartphone-supported assessments and validated questionnaires, together with advanced signal processing, statistical modelling and machine learning. The PhD student will help implement, coordinate and analyze studies that bridge controlled physiology and ecological, home-based assessment.

Job description

The successful candidate will design, conduct and analyze human studies linking sleep, stress, arousal and autonomic physiology in both laboratory and real-world settings. A central part of the position will be the implementation of robust research pipelines for mobile and decentralized phenotyping, including data collection workflows, biosignal processing, quality control, synchronization, feature extraction and computational analysis.

The position is ideal for a candidate who wants to combine hands-on human physiology, sleep research, mobile health methods and strong computational data analysis. Professional software engineers may support parts of the technical backbone, but the PhD student should be able to implement and understand the data flow, work with technical collaborators, implement research-facing pipelines and take scientific ownership of the physiological data and its interpretation.

Your work will include:

• Design and conduct mechanistic laboratory studies and real-world sleep, stress and arousal studies in human participants

• Acquire and manage multimodal physiological data during wake and sleep such as pupillometry, EEG, ECG, respiration, photoplethysmography, actigraphy, wearable sensor data, smartphone-based assessments and questionnaires

• C

All'interno di questo ambiente, lo studente di dottorato contribuirà a un programma di ricerca traduttiva che mira a capire come lo stress quotidiano e gli stati eccitanti modellano la fisiologia del sonno, il recupero e risultati rilevanti per la salute nella vita reale. La posizione è ideale per un candidato che vuole combinare la fisiologia umana, la ricerca sul sonno, i metodi di salute mobile e una forte analisi dei dati computazionali. descriptionByLocale.fr: Descrizione Position du doctorat sur le sommeil, le stress et l'excitation chez les humains 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Un environnement de recherche de calibre mondial à l'intersection des technologies du sommeil, de la physiologie et de la santé Le Neural Control of Movement Lab de l'ETH Zurich, Département des sciences et technologies de la santé, invite des candidats exceptionnels à postuler à un poste de doctorat axé sur les liens physiologiques entre le sommeil, le stress, l'excitation et la santé chez l'homme. Le projet combine des expériences de laboratoire mécanistes avec le phénotypage réel, à domicile et décentralisé, en utilisant des enregistrements physiologiques multimodaux, des technologies de santé mobiles et des pipelines d'analyse computationnelle. Le Neural Control of Movement Lab se concentre sur la compréhension de la façon dont le cerveau contrôle le comportement et sur le développement d'interfaces non invasives pour mesurer et moduler la fonction cérébrale pendant le réveil et le sommeil. Dans ce contexte, le doctorant contribuera à un programme de recherche translationnelle qui vise à comprendre comment le stress quotidien et les états d'excitation façonnent la physiologie du sommeil, le rétablissement et les résultats pertinents pour la santé dans la vie réelle. Le Département des sciences de la santé et de la technologie de l'ETH Zurich réunit des chercheurs dans les domaines des neurosciences, de l'ingénierie biomédicale, des sciences du mouvement, de la nutrition, de la physiologie et de la médecine. Il offre un environnement interdisciplinaire pour la recherche à l'interface de la biologie humaine, de la technologie et de la traduction clinique. Contexte du projet Le sommeil, le stress et l'excitation sont des processus physiologiques profondément interconnectés. Le stress persistant et l'excitation accrue peuvent modifier la transition vers le sommeil, changer le cerveau nocturne et l'activité autonome, et influencer la récupération, la résilience et la santé à long terme. Pourtant, de nombreux mécanismes clés sont encore étudiés soit dans des laboratoires étroitement contrôlés, soit par des mesures simplifiées du monde réel qui ne saisissent pas la richesse de la physiologie humaine. Ce projet vise à combler cette lacune en combinant des études mécanistes en laboratoire avec le phénotypage réel du sommeil, du stress et de l'excitation dans la vie quotidienne. L'objectif est d'élaborer des flux de travail de recherche rigoureux et évolutifs qui permettent de mesurer comment le stress et l'excitation se déroulent au cours de la journée, comment ils affectent le sommeil et la récupération du jour au lendemain, et quelles signatures physiologiques sont les plus informatives pour les phénotypes pertinents pour la santé. Le projet utilisera l'acquisition de biosignaux multimodaux, tels que la pupillométrie, l'EEG du sommeil, l'ECG, la respiration, les données portables et actigraphiques, les évaluations soutenues par smartphone et les questionnaires validés, ainsi que le traitement avancé des signaux, la modélisation statistique et l'apprentissage automatique. Le doctorant aidera à mettre en oeuvre, coordonner et analyser les études qui relient la physiologie contrôlée et l'évaluation écologique à domicile. Description du poste Le candidat retenu concevra, mènera et analysera des études humaines sur le sommeil, le stress, l'excitation et la physiologie autonome en laboratoire et dans le monde réel. Un élément central de la position sera la mise en place de pipelines de recherche robustes pour le phénotypage mobile et décentralisé, y compris les flux de travail de collecte de données, le traitement des biosignales, le contrôle de la qualité, la synchronisation, l'extraction de fonctionnalités et l'analyse computationnelle. Le poste est idéal pour un candidat qui veut combiner la physiologie humaine pratique, la recherche sur le sommeil, les méthodes de santé mobiles et une analyse de données computationnelles solide. Les ingénieurs en logiciels professionnels peuvent soutenir des parties de l'épine dorsale technique, mais le doctorant devrait être en mesure de mettre en œuvre et de comprendre le flux de données, de travailler avec des collaborateurs techniques, de mettre en place des pipelines faisant face à la recherche et de s'approprier scientifiquement les données physiologiques et leur interprétation. Mansioni - Concevoir et mener des études de laboratoire mécanistes et des études sur le sommeil, le stress et l'excitation dans le monde réel chez les participants humains - Acquérir et gérer des données physiologiques multimodales pendant le sillage et le sommeil telles que pupillométrie, EEG, ECG, respiration, photopléthysmographie, actigraphie, données de capteur portable, évaluations basées sur smartphone et questionnaires - C

jobs.description:
DevOps Engineer

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the preferred work location is Lugano, but it could also be Zürich.

Project background

We are seeking a versatile and driven DevOps Engineer to help design, build, and operate the software-defined infrastructure and services powering advanced scientific computing and AI/ML workloads at scale.

You will work at the intersection of systems engineering, software engineering, cloud-native infrastructure, and high-performance computing (HPC), contributing to platforms and services used by researchers and engineers tackling complex scientific and AI challenges.

We value strong engineering fundamentals, curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to learn more than a perfect initial match of technical requirements. We welcome engineers from diverse backgrounds who are eager to contribute and grow. If you are motivated by challenging technical environments and enjoy understanding systems deeply, we strongly encourage you to apply even if your experience does not cover every area listed below.

We are offering a contract initially limited to two years , which will provide the opportunity to contribute to a fast-evolving AI landscape in which CSCS plays a key role and to support high-impact initiatives both nationally and internationally. This includes contributions to the Swiss AI Initiative and similar programs, such as lending support for the development and release of the Apertus models.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Job description

• Design, deploy, automate, and operate scalable infrastructure and cloud-native platform services

• Contribute to Kubernetes-based AI/ML and HPC platforms, including CI/CD, GitOps, observability, security, and operational tooling

• Collaborate with researchers and engineers to support complex workflows, troubleshoot production environments, and improve reliability and performance

• Contribute to platform engineering, automation, and developer productivity initiatives across evolving systems and services

• The technologies and areas below illustrate the breadth of our environment and interests. They are not a checklist of requirements, and experience in only some of these areas is expected

Profile

Technical environment and areas of interest:

• Linux systems engineering, and software development (e.g., Python, Bash)

• Containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitOps, and Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, Helm, Ansible, ArgoCD)

• Distributed systems concepts, APIs, scalability, observability, identity and access management, and security

• AI/ML platforms and supporting infrastructure services

• HPC systems, GPU clusters, and large-scale infrastructure environments

• Platform engineering and developer productivity tooling

• Secure or confidentiality-sensitive operational environments

Personal qualities:

• Curious, hands-on, and eager to understand systems inside-out

• Strong engineering mindset and problem-solving attitude

• Comfortable learning new technologies and working across disciplines

• Effective communicator and collaborative team player

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• Experience supporting research or scientific computing environments

• Familiarity with HPC systems and services

• Exposure to GPU clusters and accelerated computing

• Experience with SRE p

descriptionByLocale.de:
DevOps Ingenieur 80%-100%, Zürich, befristet Drucken Drucken Das Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) entwickelt und betreibt eine leistungsfähige Rechen- und Datenforschungsinfrastruktur, die Weltklasse-Wissenschaft in der Schweiz unterstützt. Das Anwenderlabor ist für inländische und internationale Forscher in Wissenschaft, Industrie und Wirtschaft verfügbar. Das Zentrum wird von der ETH Zürich betrieben und verfügt über Büros im Rechenzentrum in Lugano und in Zürich. Für diese Position ist der bevorzugte Arbeitsort Lugano, aber es könnte auch Zürich sein. Projekt Hintergrund Wir suchen einen vielseitigen und angetriebenen DevOps Engineer, um die softwaredefinierte Infrastruktur und Dienstleistungen zu entwerfen, zu bauen und zu betreiben, die fortschrittliche wissenschaftliche Computing- und AI/ML-Workloads im Maßstab vorantreiben. Sie arbeiten an der Schnittstelle von Systemtechnik, Software-Engineering, Cloud-native Infrastruktur und High-Performance Computing (HPC) und tragen zu Plattformen und Dienstleistungen, die von Forschern und Ingenieuren verwendet werden, die komplexe wissenschaftliche und AI-Herausforderungen bewältigen. Wir schätzen starke Engineering-Grundsätze, Neugier, Anpassungsfähigkeit und Bereitschaft, mehr als eine perfekte Erstanpassung an technische Anforderungen zu lernen. Wir begrüßen Ingenieure aus unterschiedlichen Hintergründen, die gerne dazu beitragen und wachsen. Wenn Sie von anspruchsvollen technischen Umgebungen motiviert sind und Verständnissysteme zutiefst genießen, empfehlen wir Ihnen, sich zu bewerben, auch wenn Ihre Erfahrung nicht alle unten aufgeführten Bereiche abdeckt. Wir bieten einen zunächst auf zwei Jahre begrenzten Vertrag an, der die Möglichkeit bietet, zu einer sich schnell entwickelnden KI-Landschaft beizutragen, in der CSCS eine Schlüsselrolle spielt und hocheffiziente Initiativen sowohl national als auch international unterstützt. Dazu gehören Beiträge zur Schweizerischen KI-Initiative und ähnliche Programme wie die Förderung der Entwicklung und Freigabe der Apertus-Modelle. Der erste Zweijahresvertrag könnte möglicherweise verlängert oder sogar dauerhaft werden. Jobbeschreibung
• Entwicklung, Bereitstellung, Automatisierung und Betrieb von skalierbaren Infrastruktur- und Cloud-Native-Plattformen
• Beitrag zu Kubernetes-basierten KI/ML- und HPC-Plattformen, einschließlich CI/CD, GitOps, Beobachtungs-, Sicherheits- und Betriebswerkzeugen
• Mit Forschern und Ingenieuren zusammenarbeiten, um komplexe Workflows zu unterstützen, Produktionsumgebungen zu beheben und Zuverlässigkeit und Leistung zu verbessern
• Mithilfe von Plattform-Engineering-, Automatisierungs- und Entwicklungsproduktivitätsinitiativen in den sich entwickelnden Systemen und Dienstleistungen
• Die folgenden Technologien und Bereiche illustrieren die Breite unserer Umwelt und Interessen. Sie sind keine Checkliste der Anforderungen, und Erfahrung in nur einigen dieser Bereiche wird erwartet Profil Technische Umgebung und Interessengebiete:
• Linux-Systeme Engineering, Skripting, Fehlersuche und Softwareentwicklung (z.B. Python, Bash)
• Container, Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitOps und Infrastruktur als Code (z.B. Terraform, Helm, Ansible, ArgoCD)
• Verteilte Systemkonzepte, APIs, Skalierbarkeit, Beobachtbarkeit, Identität und Zugriffsmanagement und Sicherheit
• KI/ML-Plattformen und Unterstützung von Infrastrukturdienstleistungen
• HPC-Systeme, GPU-Cluster und groß angelegte Infrastrukturumgebungen
• Plattformtechnik und Entwicklerproduktivitätstool
• Sichere oder vertrauliche betriebliche Umgebungen Persönliche Qualitäten:
• Curious, Hand-on und eifrig, Systeme im Innen-Out zu verstehen
• Starke technische Einstellung und Problemlösung
• Komfortables Lernen neuer Technologien und Arbeiten über Disziplinen
• Effektiver Kommunikator und Mitarbeiter Wege, um sich von der Menge abzuheben:
• Erfahrungen zur Unterstützung von Forschungs- oder wissenschaftlichen Rechenumgebungen

Ingénieur DevOps 80%-100%, Zurich, durée déterminée imprimer Drucken Le Centre National de SuperComputation Suisse (CSCS) développe et exploite une infrastructure informatique et de recherche de données de haute performance qui soutient les sciences de classe mondiale en Suisse. Son laboratoire d'utilisateurs est à la disposition des chercheurs canadiens et internationaux du milieu universitaire, de l'industrie et des entreprises. Le centre est exploité par ETH Zurich et dispose de bureaux dans son centre de données à Lugano et à Zurich. Pour cette position, le lieu de travail préféré est Lugano, mais il pourrait également être Zürich. Contexte du projet Nous recherchons un ingénieur DevOps polyvalent et motivé pour aider à concevoir, construire et exploiter l'infrastructure et les services définis par logiciel qui alimentent à l'échelle les charges de travail avancées en informatique scientifique et en AI/ML. Vous travaillerez à l'intersection de l'ingénierie des systèmes, de l'ingénierie des logiciels, de l'infrastructure cloud-native et de l'informatique haute performance (HPC), contribuant aux plateformes et services utilisés par les chercheurs et les ingénieurs pour relever des défis scientifiques et d'IA complexes. Nous accordons beaucoup d'importance aux principes fondamentaux de l'ingénierie, à la curiosité, à l'adaptabilité et à la volonté d'apprendre plus qu'à une correspondance initiale parfaite des exigences techniques. Nous accueillons des ingénieurs de divers horizons qui sont désireux de contribuer et de grandir. Si vous êtes motivé par des environnements techniques stimulants et que vous appréciez profondément les systèmes de compréhension, nous vous encourageons fortement à appliquer même si votre expérience ne couvre pas tous les domaines énumérés ci-dessous. Nous offrons un contrat initialement limité à deux ans, ce qui permettra de contribuer à un paysage d'IA en évolution rapide dans lequel le SCCS joue un rôle clé et d'appuyer des initiatives à impact élevé à l'échelle nationale et internationale. Cela comprend des contributions à l'Initiative suisse d'IA et à des programmes similaires, tels que le soutien au développement et à la diffusion des modèles Apertus. Le contrat initial de deux ans pourrait être prolongé ou même devenir permanent. Description du poste
• Conception, déploiement, automatisation et exploitation d'infrastructures évolutives et de services de plate-forme cloud-native

• Collaborer avec les chercheurs et les ingénieurs pour soutenir les flux de travail complexes, résoudre les problèmes des environnements de production et améliorer la fiabilité et les performances
• Contribuer aux initiatives d'ingénierie des plates-formes, d'automatisation et de productivité des développeurs dans les systèmes et services en évolution

• Ingénierie des systèmes Linux, script, dépannage et développement de logiciels (p. ex. Python, Bash)

• Systèmes HPC, grappes GPU et environnements d'infrastructure à grande échelle
• ingénierie de plate-forme et outillage de productivité du développeur
• Environnements opérationnels sûrs ou sensibles à la confidentialité Qualités personnelles:
• Curieux, pratique et désireux de comprendre les systèmes internes
• Une forte attitude d'ingénierie et de résolution de problèmes
• Apprentissage confortable des nouvelles technologies et travail à travers les disciplines
• Communicateur efficace et joueur d'équipe collaborative Des façons de se démarquer de la foule :
• Expérience de soutien aux environnements de recherche ou d'informatique scientifique
• Connaissance des systèmes et services HPC
• Exposition aux grappes GPU et calcul accéléré

Lehrentwickler:in Biowissenschaften (m/w/d)

70%-80%, Zürich, unbefristet

print
Drucken

Das Center for Active Learning (CAL) des Departements Biologie der ETH Zürich fördert innovative Lehr- und Lernformate und unterstützt Dozierende bei der Gestaltung aktivierender Lehrveranstaltungen in biowissenschaftlichen Curricula. Im Fokus stehen die didaktisch fundierte Weiterentwicklung von Lehrinhalten sowie der gezielte Einsatz digitaler Technologien zur Förderung nachhaltiger Lernerfolge. Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir eine engagierte Persönlichkeit als Lehrentwickler:in (70-80%). Die Position kann per 1. August 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung angetreten werden.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Konzeption von Lehrmaterialien in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Dozierenden

• Beratung von Dozierenden bei Aufbau, Einsatz und Weiterentwicklung von Lernmaterialien und Lehr-/Lerntechnologien

• Evaluation und Implementierung neuer Technologien und Lehrstrategien im Bereich des aktiven Lernens

• Erstellung, digitale Umsetzung und Optimierung von Lehrmaterialien sowie Prüfungen auf Moodle

• Technischer Support bei der Durchführung von digitalen Prüfungen

• Gestaltung und Betreuung von Moodle-Kursen für Lehrveranstaltungen der Biologie

Profil

• Masterabschluss im Bereich Biologie, Biochemie oder anderen Life Sciences; Doktorat bzw. mehrjährige Forschungserfahrung von Vorteil

• Erfahrung in der Hochschullehre, in der Didaktik im MINT-Bereich und/oder der Lehrmittelentwicklung

• Strukturierte, selbstständige und zielorientierte Arbeitsweise

• Kommunikations- und Teamfähigkeit im Austausch mit Dozierenden und Studierenden

• Hohes Mass an Flexibilität, Belastbarkeit und Organisationsfähigkeit sowie Freude an einem dynamischen Hochschulumfeld

• Interesse an digitalen Lehr- und Prüfungsformaten

• Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sowie gute Englischkenntnisse

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

• Eine vielseitige Tätigkeit im Bereich Lehre am Departement Biologie mit Einblick in innovative Lehr- und Prüfungsformate

• Möglichkeiten zur aktiven Mitgestaltung und Weiterentwicklung von Kursen und Prüfungen im Curriculum der Biologie und angrenzender Life Sciences

• Flexible Arbeitszeiten und vielfältige Zusatzleistungen wie z.B. ÖV-Abonnemente und Car Sharing, ein breites Sportangebot des ASVZ, Kinderbetreuung sowie attraktive Vorsorgeleistungen

• Zusammenarbeit in einem engagierten, interdisziplinären Team an der Schnittstelle von Didaktik, Lehrtechnologie und Fachwissenschaft

• Möglichkeiten zur Weiterentwicklung im Bereich digitale Lehre

chevron_right
Arbeiten, Lehren und Forschen an der ETH Zürich

Diversität und Nachhaltigkeit sind uns wichtig

Im Einklang mit unseren Werten unterstützt die ETH Zürich eine inklusive Kultur. Wir fördern Chancengleichheit, schätzen Vielfalt und pflegen ein Arbeits- und Lernumfeld, in dem die Rechte und die Würde aller Mitarbeitenden und Studierenden respektiert werden. Auf unserer Webseite zur Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt erfahren Sie, wie wir ein faires und offenes Umfeld sicherstellen, in dem sich alle entwickeln und entfalten können. Nachhaltigkeit ist für uns ein zentraler Wert – wir arbeiten konsequent an einer klimaneutralen Zukunft.

Neugierig? Sind wir auch.

Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Online-Bewerbung mit den folgenden Unterlagen:

• Motivationsschreiben

• Lebenslauf

• Diplome und Arbeitszeugnisse

Weitere Informationen über das Center for Active Learning finden Sie auf unserer Website . Für Auskünfte steht Ihnen Dr. Katja Köhler, koehlerk@ethz.ch (keine Bewerbungsunterlagen), gerne zur Verfügung.

Bitte bewerben Sie sich bis 26. Juni 2026 ausschliesslich über das Online-Bewerbungsportal. Bewerbungen per E-Mail sowie auf dem Postweg werden nicht berücksichtigt.

jobs.description:
Werkstattverantwortliche:r Raplab (m/w/d)

60%, Zürich, unbefristet

print
Drucken

Das Rapid Architectural Prototyping Laboratory des Departement Architektur versteht sich als Kompetenzzentrum für Modell- und Prototypenbau mit einem klaren Fokus auf Architekturmodellbau. Für unsere rund 2000 Studierenden stellen wir eine breite Werkstattinfrastruktur, von traditionellen Techniken bis zum 3d-Druck, mit entsprechender Beratung und Projektbegleitung zur Verfügung. Die Stelle ist per 01.08.2026 oder nach Vereinbarung zu besetzen.

Projekthintergrund

Die Umsetzung von Ideen zum Objekt ist unser zentrales Anliegen. Wir versuchen diesen Prozess möglichst direkt, einfach und elegant zu gestalten. Dabei befähigen wir unsere Studierenden und Forschenden durch diverse Lehrangebote, selbständig in den Werkstätten des Raplabs zu arbeiten. Wir verknüpfen Konzept, Methodik und Gestaltung über die Praxis des Herstellens. Dreh- und Angelpunkt ist im Raplab die handwerkliche und gestalterische Auseinandersetzung, durch welche wir gezielt einen Dialog mit unserer Umwelt herstellen - über die konkrete handwerkliche Arbeit an sich, erschliessen wir systematisch theoretische und technische Zusammenhänge, die immer eine Anbindung an ein Modell haben. Handwerk wird dabei als breit gefasster Begriff verstanden; beinhaltet technische Anliegen, Konstruktion, Material, Haptik, Wahrnehmung, Ausdruck und Gestalt. Bei der Vermittlung von Fertigkeiten achten wir besonders darauf, dass die hergestellten Modelle eine Ausgewogenheit im Bezug auf alle Aspekte des Prozesses haben und somit die gestalterische Idee konsequent zeigen. Durch die aus der Lehre am Departement entstehende Dynamik ist das Raplab ein Arbeitsumfeld, welches sich ständig in Weiterentwicklung befindet und sich der Unterstützung der Lehre und Ausbildung im Architekturstudium widmet. Dabei reichen unsere Aufgaben von Projektberatung, Ausstellungsgestaltung, Entwicklung von Lernkonzepten, Modellbau, technischer Planung und Projektarbeit, bis hin zu komplexen Kontrollsystemen, um unser Werkstattumfeld so effizient wie möglich zu gestalten.

Stellenbeschreibung

• Sie sind die zentrale Ansprechsperson für Studierende und Professuren für die Werkstätten und zuständig für Sicherheit, Unterhalt und Betrieb

• Sie pflegen den direkten persönlichen Kontakt zu den Werkstattnutzern und beraten und unterstützen diese bei der Umsetzung ihrer Arbeiten

• Als werkstattverantwortliche Person entwickeln Sie zusammen mit Ihren Kolleginnen und Kollegen das Werkstattumfeld des Raplabs weiter

• Sie bringen sich aktiv ins Planungsgeschehen ein und sind darauf bedacht, dass die angebotenen Prozesse den Bedürfnissen unserer Nutzer entsprechen

• Dabei wägen Sie je nach Projekt selbständig ab, welcher Grad der Unterstützung angemessen ist

• Im Weiteren beteiligen Sie sich auf inhaltlicher und handwerklicher Ebene an strategischen Projekten und Lehrveranstaltungen des Raplabs

Profil

• Sie verfügen über ein abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich der Vermittlung von Gestaltung und Kunst oder Architektur (oder vergleichbar) mit einem Arbeitsschwerpunkt in den Bereichen Architekturmodellbau und Prototypenbau

• Idealerweise besitzen Sie in Ergänzung zu ihrem Studium ein Eidgenössisches Fähigkeitszeugnis (EFZ) in einem einschlägigen Beruf

• Sie besitzen ausgeprägte konzeptionelle und handwerkliche Fähigkeiten, eine Affinität für Technik, vertieftes Wissen über Materialien und Herstellungstechniken und haben einige Jahre im Bereich der Vermittlung gearbeitet – idealerweise an einer Hochschule oder im hochschulnahen Umfeld

• Sie sind gewohnt, selbständig Studierende zu beraten und in grösseren Gruppen Projekte umzusetzen bzw. zu leiten

• Deutsch und sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Sprache und Schrift, sind ein Muss; Interesse a

Descrizione Projektmanager (m/w/d) 60%, Zurigo, illimitato stampa Stampa Il Rapid Architectural Prototyping Laboratory del Dipartimento di Architettura è un centro di competenza per la costruzione di modelli e prototipi con un chiaro focus sulla costruzione di modelli architettonici. Per i nostri circa 2000 studenti forniamo un'ampia infrastruttura di officina, dalle tecniche tradizionali alla stampa 3d, con un'adeguata consulenza e supporto di progetto. Il luogo è occupato dal 01.08.2026 o d'accordo. Sfondo progettuale Sfondo del progetto L'attuazione delle idee sull'oggetto è la nostra preoccupazione centrale.
• Cerchiamo di rendere questo processo il più diretto, semplice ed elegante possibile. Permettiamo ai nostri studenti e ricercatori di lavorare in modo indipendente ai laboratori del Raplab attraverso vari corsi. Colleghiamo concetto, metodologia e design alla pratica della produzione. Al Raplab, il punto di rotazione e l'attenzione è sul dibattito artigianale e creativo, attraverso il quale stabiliamo un dialogo con il nostro ambiente in modo mirato - sul lavoro artigianale concreto stesso, sviluppiamo sistematicamente relazioni teoriche e tecniche che hanno sempre un legame con un modello. l'artigianato è inteso come un concetto ampio; comprende le preoccupazioni tecniche, costruzione, materiale, ottica, percezione, espressione e forma. Quando si comunicano competenze, si presta particolare attenzione al fatto che i modelli prodotti hanno un equilibrio in relazione a tutti gli aspetti del processo e quindi mostrare costantemente l'idea di design. A causa delle dinamiche derivanti dall'insegnamento presso il dipartimento, Raplab è un ambiente di lavoro costantemente in sviluppo ed è dedicato al supporto dell'insegnamento e della formazione negli studi architettonici. I nostri compiti spaziano dalla consulenza progettuale, dalla progettazione espositiva, dallo sviluppo di concetti di apprendimento, dalla costruzione di modelli, dalla pianificazione tecnica e dal lavoro di progetto, ai sistemi di controllo complessi per rendere il nostro ambiente di laboratorio il più efficiente possibile. Mansioni - Sono la persona di contatto centrale per studenti e professori per workshop e responsabili della sicurezza, manutenzione e funzionamento - Mantengono contatti personali diretti con gli utenti del workshop e li consigliano e li sostengono nell'attuazione del loro lavoro - Sviluppando come direttore di laboratorio Insieme ai vostri colleghi, continuerete l'ambiente di workshop del Raplab - Sono attivamente coinvolti nella pianificazione e sono progettati per soddisfare le esigenze dei nostri utenti. - A seconda del progetto, si considera indipendentemente il grado di supporto appropriato - Inoltre, parteciperai a progetti strategici e corsi del Raplab a livello di contenuti e fiere.
• Requisiti - Hanno completato i loro studi nel campo del design e dell'arte o dell'architettura (o simili) con un focus sulla costruzione di modelli di architettura e costruzione di prototipi - Idealmente, oltre ai loro studi, hai un certificato di invidia in una professione rilevante. - Possiedano competenze concettuali e artigianali distinte, affinità per la tecnologia, conoscenza approfondita dei materiali e delle tecniche di produzione, e hanno lavorato per alcuni anni nel campo della mediazione – idealmente in un'università o in un ambiente di scuola superiore - Sono utilizzati per consigliare in modo indipendente gli studenti e realizzare progetti in gruppi più grandi. di portare - Il tedesco e la buona conoscenza inglese in lingua e scrittura, sono un must

For our around 2000 students we provide a wide workshop infrastructure, from traditional techniques to 3d printing, with appropriate consulting and project support. The place shall be occupied by 01.08.2026 or by agreement. Progettual background Project background The implementation of ideas on the object is our central concern. Ihr Engagement schafft beste Voraussetzungen für Exzellenz in Lehre, Forschung, Wissenstransfer und Nachhaltigkeit der ETH Zürich.

In der Abteilung Facility Services der ETH Zürich schaffen wir die optimale Voraussetzung für Lehre, Forschung und Technologietransfer. Wir unterhalten die Gebäude und stellen die Energie- und Medienversorgung sowie das technische und infrastrukturelle Gebäudemanagement aller von der ETH Zürich genutzten Gebäude und Räume sicher.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir per 1. Mai 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung eine:n Mitarbeiter:in im Info + Service Center (80%). Die Arbeitstage sind Dienstag - Freitag.

• Bringen mehrjährige Erfahrung im Bereich Empfang / Schalterdienst mit.

• Sie fühlen sich im Frontoffice-Bereich wohl.

• Bringen eine schnelle Auffassungsgabe, technisches Verständnis sowie gute organisatorische Fähigkeiten mit.

• Schätzen die Vorzüge eines Gemeinschaftsbüros.

jobs.description:
Systems Engineer – Platform Automation

80%-100%, Lugano, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS) develops and operates a high-performance computing and data research infrastructure that supports world-class science in Switzerland. Its user laboratory is available to domestic and international researchers in academia, industry, and the business sector. The centre is operated by ETH Zurich and has offices at its data centre in Lugano and in Zurich.

For this position the work location is Lugano.

Project background

As high-performance computing, AI, and cloud technologies continue to converge; CSCS is redefining how advanced computational services are designed and delivered. Modern scientific and engineering workloads are no longer just large—they are complex, data-intensive, and highly diverse, pushing existing infrastructure to its limits.

We are offering a contract initially limited to two years , which will provide the opportunity to contribute to a fast-evolving AI landscape in which CSCS plays a key role and to support high-impact initiatives both nationally and internationally. This includes contributions to the Swiss AI Initiative and similar programs, such as lending support for the development and release of foundation models in the weather and climate domain.

The initial two-year contract could potentially be extended or even become permanent.

Job description

The main goal of this position is to develop and manage HPC/AI services on top of a multi-tenant infrastructure. As a Platform automation engineer, you will directly contribute to the design, implementation, maintenance, and documentation of platform services to support HPC and AI. Your work will directly enhance the overall system functionality and efficiency.

Main duties:

• Investigating, troubleshooting, and debugging platform services and infrastructure resources

• Developing, maintaining, and supporting tools and pipelines to support platforms on a geographically redundant infrastructure

• Developing automations to provision, test, deploy, and monitor resources to support the needs of HPC and AI platforms

• Supporting, documenting, and sharing knowledge of tools, and procedur

Profile

You should have a bachelor’s or higher degree in computer engineering, computer science, a relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

You should have a sound knowledge of:

• Experience in the deployment of HPC, AI, or Cloud infrastructures

• Management of HPC/AI services to maximize utilization of compute, storage and high speed network components

• Working knowledge of automation tools and frameworks, including CI/CD processes and ecosystem

• Linux administration skills

Experience with the following is preferred, though there will be ample opportunities to learn and gain more experience with all of these skills on the job:

• Versioning systems and CI/CD workflows such as ArgoCD

• Debugging of microservices running on Kubernetes

• Performance monitoring and diagnostic tools for HPC/AI hardware

• Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform and Ansible

Personal qualities:

• Self-motivated and proactive team player

• Strong communication skills or interest in developing them

• Strong problem-solving mindset with tolerance for uncertainty and change

• Understands user needs and works collaboratively to address them

• Adaptive and willing to learn new technologies with and from others

• Comfortable tackling complex or ambiguous problems

• Comfortable admitting when you don’t know, reaching out and leveraging the right expertise when needed

Project management and methodology:

• Experience with working in self-organized teams

• Familiarity with Agile methodology

• Experience with test-driven development is a plus

Workplace

We offer

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive engineering team and particularly encourage applications from groups underrepres

Il suo laboratorio di utenti è disponibile per i ricercatori nazionali e internazionali in accademia, industria e settore business. Il centro è gestito da ETH Zurich e ha sede presso il suo data center di Lugano e a Zurigo. Per questa posizione la posizione di lavoro è Lugano. Sfondo del progetto Poiché le tecnologie di calcolo ad alte prestazioni, AI e cloud continuano a convergere; CSCS sta ridefinindo come i servizi computazionali avanzati sono progettati e consegnati. I moderni carichi di lavoro scientifici e ingegneristici non sono più solo grandi—sono complessi, intensivi di dati e altamente diversificati, spingendo le infrastrutture esistenti ai suoi limiti. Stiamo offrendo un contratto inizialmente limitato a due anni , che fornirà l'opportunità di contribuire a un paesaggio AI in rapida evoluzione in cui CSCS svolge un ruolo chiave e di sostenere iniziative ad alto impatto sia a livello nazionale che internazionale. Questo include i contributi all'Iniziativa dell'AI svizzera e programmi simili, come il supporto di prestito per lo sviluppo e il rilascio dei modelli di fondazione nel dominio meteo e clima. Il contratto iniziale di due anni potrebbe potenzialmente essere esteso o addirittura diventare permanente. Descrizione del lavoro L'obiettivo principale di questa posizione è quello di sviluppare e gestire i servizi HPC/AI in cima a un'infrastruttura multi-tenant. Come ingegnere di automazione della piattaforma, contribuirai direttamente alla progettazione, implementazione, manutenzione e documentazione dei servizi della piattaforma per supportare HPC e AI. Il vostro lavoro migliorerà direttamente la funzionalità e l'efficienza del sistema generale. Principali doveri:
• Investigazione, risoluzione dei problemi e debug dei servizi della piattaforma e delle risorse infrastrutturali
• Sviluppare, mantenere e supportare strumenti e tubazioni per supportare piattaforme su un'infrastruttura geograficamente ridondante
• Sviluppare automazione per fornire, testare, distribuire e monitorare le risorse per supportare le esigenze delle piattaforme HPC e AI
• Sostenere, documentare e condividere la conoscenza degli strumenti, e procedur Profilo Si dovrebbe avere un diploma di laurea o superiore in ingegneria informatica, informatica, un campo tecnico rilevante, o esperienza pratica equivalente. Si dovrebbe avere una solida conoscenza di:
• Esperienza nella distribuzione delle infrastrutture HPC, AI o Cloud
• Gestione dei servizi HPC/AI per massimizzare l'utilizzo di componenti di calcolo, archiviazione e rete ad alta velocità
• Conoscenze di lavoro di strumenti e quadri di automazione, compresi i processi CI/CD e l'ecosistema
• competenze di amministrazione Linux L'esperienza con il seguente è preferita, anche se ci saranno ampie opportunità per imparare e acquisire più esperienza con tutte queste competenze sul lavoro:
• Sistemi di versione e flussi di lavoro CI/CD come ArgoCD
• Debug di microservizi in esecuzione su Kubernetes
• Monitoraggio delle prestazioni e strumenti diagnostici per l'hardware HPC/AI
• Infrastrutture come strumenti di codice come Terraform e Ansible Qualità personali:
• Giocatore di squadra automotivato e proattivo
• Forte capacità di comunicazione o interesse a svilupparle
• Forte mentalità problem solving con tolleranza per l'incertezza e il cambiamento
• Comprende le esigenze degli utenti e lavora in collaborazione per affrontarli
• Adattativo e disposto ad imparare nuove tecnologie con e da altri
• Confortevoli problemi complessi o ambigui
• Confortevole ammettere quando non si sa, raggiungere e sfruttare la giusta esperienza quando necessario Gestione e metodologia del progetto:
• Esperienza con il lavoro in team auto-organizzati
• Familiarità con la metodologia Agile
• L'esperienza con lo sviluppo guidato da test è un plus Luogo di lavoro Offriamo Ci impegniamo a costruire un team di ingegneria diversificato e inclusivo e in particolare a incoraggiare le applicazioni di gruppi underreprepres

Das Zentrum wird von der ETH Zürich betrieben und verfügt über Büros im Rechenzentrum in Lugano und in Zürich. Für diese Position ist der Arbeitsort Lugano. Dazu gehören Beiträge zur Schweizerischen KI-Initiative und ähnliche Programme wie die Förderung der Entwicklung und Freisetzung von Grundmodellen im Wetter- und Klimabereich. • Erfahrungen bei der Bereitstellung von HPC-, AI- oder Cloud-Infrastrukturen

Son laboratoire d'utilisateurs est à la disposition des chercheurs canadiens et internationaux du milieu universitaire, de l'industrie et des entreprises. Le centre est exploité par ETH Zurich et dispose de bureaux dans son centre de données à Lugano et à Zurich. Pour ce poste, le lieu de travail est Lugano. Contexte du projet À mesure que les technologies de l'informatique, de l'intelligence artificielle et du cloud continuent de converger, le SCCS redéfinit la façon dont les services informatiques avancés sont conçus et fournis. Les charges de travail scientifiques et d'ingénierie modernes ne sont plus seulement importantes : elles sont complexes, à forte intensité de données et très diverses, ce qui pousse l'infrastructure existante à ses limites. jobs.description:
PhD Position in Numerical Modelling of Debris Flows

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Chair of Engineering Geology (Prof. Dr. Jordan Aaron, Geological Institute) is looking for a creative and motivated PhD candidate with a strong interest in fluid mechanics and numerical modelling. The position is expected to start in September 2026 and is fully funded for 4 years.

Job description

• You will develop a new coupled solid/ fluid mechanics-based numerical model to simulate the motion of debris flows

• You will incorporate novel field data currently being collected at numerous locations around the world to validate the new numerical model

• You will combine the numerical model results with field data to further our understanding of the motion of debris flows

Profile

• MSc in Fluid Mechanics, Hydraulics, Engineering Geology, Geological Engineering, Geophysics or related fields

• Strong background in numerical modelling

• Interest in natural hazards

• Motivation, creativity, independence, and ability to work in a team

• Excellent English communication skills

Workplace

We offer

We are an enthusiastic and collaborative research group with many opportunities for multi-disciplinary cutting-edge research in engineering geology. There are significant opportunities to broaden your research interests and develop your academic career. We further offer training in teaching through teaching assistantships, as well as access to state-of-the-art computing infrastructure, laboratories, and research equipment.

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application until 1 July 2026 with the following documents:

• A brief cover letter summarizing your motivation to apply for the position.

• Your CV

• Transcripts

• The contact details of two references

Further information about the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences can be found on our website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Prof. Jordan Aaron, jordan.aaron@eaps.ethz.ch (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

About ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.
